# Monthly Ordinances for Nourishing Life
## Recorded in the Bibliography of the History of the Song Dynasty
## Yao Cheng of the Song Dynasty

In the general practice of **Nourishing Life** <term>She-sheng</term>, there are three distinct paths. The first involves breathing techniques, refining the internal organs, and cultivating the "embryonic fluid" to maintain one's youthful appearance. The second involves consuming medicinal herbs like Ganoderma or atractylodes and the alchemical "Flying and Hidden Cinnabar Flowers." The third—which remains unchanged through the ages—involves using the **Five Grains** <note>The traditional staples of the Chinese diet: rice, wheat, soy, and two types of millet.</note> and the various flavors of food. Our very existence and destiny are bound to this third path. While the study of breathwork and alchemical medicines are covered in separate volumes, this current collection focuses on using food to extend life and adjusting one's palate according to the seasons.

According to the treatise by **Bian Que** <note>A semi-mythical physician of the 5th century BCE, revered as the father of Chinese pulse diagnosis.</note>: Food has the power to expel evil influences and stabilize the internal organs. The spirit can refresh the will to support the **Blood and Vital Energy** <term>Xue-Qi</term>. For those practicing the nourishment of life, when the breath is correct, the flavors of food will be harmonious. When flavors are harmonious, the spiritual energy is clear. When spiritual energy is clear, one aligns with the **Spirit of Truth** <note>Original: "Zhen." In Taoism, this refers to the primordial, undistorted essence of a human being.</note>. When the spirit is whole, the "five evils" and the "hundred diseases" cannot interfere. Thus it is said: when the water dries up, the fish grow thin; when the energy is clouded, man falls ill. The spirit is the root of life, and this root is the truth of existence. Excessive use tires the spirit, and great exhaustion fatigues the physical form.

According to the Treatise on Nourishing Life by **Peng Zu** <note>The Chinese "Methuselah," a legendary figure said to have lived over 800 years through diet and exercise.</note>: The eyes should not look at improper colors, the ears should not listen to improper sounds, the mouth should not taste toxic or cloying flavors, and the heart should not harbor deceitful schemes. These several habits are what cause the soul to vanish and the essence to perish, cutting short one's **allotted lifespan** <term>Suanshou</term>.

According to the **Record from Within the Pillow** <note>A title often used for esoteric manuals containing secret or "dreamt" wisdom.</note>: The **Five Flavors** <note>Sour, bitter, sweet, spicy, and salty.</note> are the physical manifestation of the energy of the **Five Elements** <note>Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, and Water.</note>. They are formed in response to the environment. Humanity is born because of the five flavors, yet is also consumed by them.

According to the **Inner Record of the Yellow Emperor**: Those who "eat" the wind become spiritual and extend their lives. Those who eat grains become wise but tire their spirits. Those who eat plants become foolish but possess great strength. Those who eat meat become coarse and brave but harbor much anger. Those who **consume Vital Energy** <term>Fu-qi</term> <note>Refers to the practice of "breath-eating" or absorbing cosmic energy directly rather than relying on solid food.</note> live forever and attain the Way.

The Record of **Master Sun** <note>Likely referring to Sun Simiao, the "King of Medicine" from the Tang Dynasty.</note> says: When the five flavors are in harmony, they generate life; when they conflict, they work against each other. When a person eats, they must be careful not to be resentful or angry. Do not speak of unlucky matters at the table. Do not swallow or belch in haste. One must regulate oneself into a state of peace and composure before eating.

<summary>This page introduces a Song Dynasty manual on "Nourishing Life" through diet, citing legendary authorities like Bian Que and the Yellow Emperor. It argues that while breathwork and alchemy are valid, the most fundamental path to longevity lies in the disciplined and seasonal consumption of food.</summary>

<keywords>Nourishing Life (She-sheng), Bian Que, Peng Zu, Five Flavors, Five Elements, Vital Energy (Qi), Dietetics, Yellow Emperor, Sun Simiao</keywords>

<page-num>136</page-num>

**The Inner Tradition of the Yellow Emperor** says: In Spring, one should eat sweet flavors; sweetness travels to the flesh. However, eating too much sweet food causes phlegm to overflow and the skin to become rough like millet. In Summer, one should eat spicy flavors; spiciness travels to the **Vital Energy** <term>Qi</term>. However, eating too much spicy food makes the energy restless and leads to frequent thirst. In Autumn, one should eat sour flavors; sourness travels to the bones. However, eating too much sour food causes the tendons to contract and pain within the bones. In Winter, one should eat salty flavors; saltiness travels to the blood. However, eating too much salty food makes the blood sluggish and the mouth dry. Eating too much bitter food leads to vomiting, nausea, and loose teeth.

---

<margin>Commentary</margin>
The **Record of Nourishing Life** says: Although common people may regularly take medicinal supplements, if they do not know the **Way of Nourishing Life** <term>She-sheng</term>, they will certainly fail to preserve their **True Essence** <note>Original: "Zhen." The primordial vitality one is born with.</note> in its entirety.

The **Record of the Lesser Existence** says: To force one's thoughts upon that which the mind cannot master is a source of injury. To force one's strength upon a weight one cannot carry is a source of injury. Deep sorrow and excessive joy both cause injury.

**Master Baopu** <note>The pseudonym of Ge Hong (283–343 CE), a famous Taoist alchemist and philosopher.</note> says: The body of a single person is like the image of a kingdom. The positions of the chest and abdomen are like the palaces and chambers. The arrangement of the four limbs is like the outlying frontiers. The divisions of the bones and joints are like the hundred officials of the court. The spirit is like the monarch, and the blood is like the common people.

The **Record of Nourishing Life** says: The taboo for a single day is to not eat to fullness in the evening. The taboo for a single month is to not become heavily intoxicated at night. The taboo for a single year is to be cautious and not travel to distant lands. The lifelong taboo is to never face the Northwest when urinating or defecating, nor to expose one's nakedness to that direction.

### The First Month of Spring
### <note>Meng-chun: the beginning of the lunar year.</note>

The first month of spring <gloss>The Dipper points to the "Tiger" <note>Yin</note> position. The Sun is in the "House" constellation. The musical pitch corresponds to "The Great Cluster" <note>Taizu</note>. The Five Generals are in the East. The lunar essence is within. The month aligns with the eighth Heavenly Stem <note>Xin</note>. The life-force is in the "Rat" <note>Zi</note>. Heaven's benefit is in the "Rabbit" <note>Mao</note>. The "Five Riches" are in the "Pig" <note>Hai</note>. The "Monthly Killing Energy" is in the "Ox" <note>Chou</note>. The "Monthly Disturbance" is in the "Dog" <note>Xu</note>. The "Nine Emptinesses" are in the "Dragon" <note>Chen</note>. The "Deathly Energy" is in the "Horse" <note>Wu</note>. Forbidden days fall on the "Ox" <note>Chou</note>. Unlucky deaths occur on the "Tiger" <note>Yin</note>. Blood taboos fall on the "Ox" <note>Chou</note>.</gloss>

In this first month of spring, Heaven and Earth generate life together; this is called the "Issuing of the Yang." Heaven and Earth provide the beginning, and the ten thousand things are transformed into life. One should go to bed at night and rise early, moving with ease to relax the physical form. Allow the will to live and grow—do not kill; give and do not take away. A person of noble character should remain firm and disciplined, not allowing their **True Energy** <term>Zhen-Qi</term> to leak away.

The internal organ of this season is the **Liver** <note>Associated with the element of Wood</note>, its position is in the East. Its star is Jupiter. Its months are the first, second, and third. Its hexagram is **The Arousing Thunder** <note>Zhen</note>. Its region is Qingzhou. Its book is the *Classic of Poetry*. Its music is the *se* lute. Its presiding deity is Lingwei Yang. Its guardian spirits are the Green Sprout and the Azure Dragon, representing the Nine Heavens, while the White Tiger represents the Nine Earths. Its creatures are fish. Its livestock is the dog. Its grain is wheat. Its fruit is the plum. Its vegetable is the leek. Its flavor is sour. Its scent is rank. Its color is green-blue. Its sound is anger. Its fluid is tears. 

At the "Beginning of Spring," the Wood element is in a state of assistance. At the "Spring Equinox," Wood is King. At the "Beginning of Summer," Wood rests. At the "Summer Solstice," Wood is exhausted. At the "Beginning of Autumn," Wood is imprisoned. At the "Autumn Equinox," Wood dies. At the "Beginning of Winter," Wood is submerged. At the "Winter Solstice," Wood is in the womb <note>The cycle describes the metaphorical birth, peak, and death of elemental energy through the year.</note>.

### The Second Month of Spring: The Great Strength Hexagram <note>Original: "Da Zhuang." This hexagram represents the rising power of the Yang energy.</note>
<gloss>The Dipper points to the "Rabbit" <note>Mao</note> position. The Sun is in the "House" constellation. The musical pitch corresponds to "The Pressed Bell" <note>Jiazhong</note>. The Five Generals are in the North. The Monthly Virtue aligns with the first Heavenly Stem <note>Jia</note>. The Monthly Harmony aligns with the sixth Heavenly Stem <note>Ji</note>. The Vital Energy <term>Qi</term> is in the "Ox" <note>Chou</note> position. Heaven's Benefit is in the "Dragon" <note>Chen</note>. The "Five Riches" are in the "Tiger" <note>Yin</note>. The "Monthly Killing Energy" is in the "Dog" <note>Xu</note>. The "Monthly Disturbance" is in the "Rooster" <note>You</note>. The "Nine Emptinesses" are in the "Ox" <note>Chou</note>. The "Deathly Energy" is in the "Goat" <note>Wei</note>. Return Taboos <note>Days unlucky for returning home</note> fall on the "Tiger" <note>Yin</note>. Departure Taboos <note>Days unlucky for setting out</note> fall on the "Snake" <note>Si</note>. "Great Failure" falls on the "Horse" <note>Jiawu</note> day. Blood Taboos fall on the "Goat" <note>Wei</note>.</gloss>

The second month of spring is known as the "Satiation of the Sun." One should harmonize the will and calm the heart. Avoid extreme cold and extreme heat. Keep the spirit and energy quiet and still to follow the laws of growth and transformation. Do not eat daylilies or aged pickles; these will trigger the recurrence of old illnesses and stir up long-standing ailments. Do not eat garlic, as it causes the energy to become congested and creates blockages in the body. Do not eat smartweed or eggs, as they cause the person’s energy to stagnate. Do not eat small garlic, as it harms one's mental resolve. Do not eat rabbit meat, as it makes the soul and spirit restless. Do not eat the meat of foxes or raccoon dogs, as it harms the spirit. In this month, the energy of the **Kidney** is weak, while the energy of the **Liver** is at its peak. It is advisable to cleanse the diaphragm and remove phlegm. One should also encourage the skin to release a light sweat to disperse the lingering warmth trapped during the previous winter. On the 6th and 8th days of this month, it is auspicious to bathe and fast, as Heaven will grant its blessings. On the 14th day, avoid traveling far; one should not travel by water or land. On the 9th day, avoid eating any fish or turtles. On the 20th day, it is auspicious to practice the **Way of Cultivating Truth** <term>Xiu-zhen</term>.

### The Third Month of Spring: The Breakthrough Hexagram <note>Original: "Guai." This hexagram represents the final push of Yang energy to displace the last of the Yin.</note>
<gloss>The Dipper points to the "Dragon" <note>Chen</note> position. The Sun is in the "Stomach" constellation. The musical pitch corresponds to "The Cleansing Wash" <note>Guxi</note>. The Five Generals are in the West. The Monthly Virtue aligns with the ninth Heavenly Stem <note>Ren</note>. The Monthly Harmony aligns with the fourth Heavenly Stem <note>Ding</note>. The Vital Energy is in the "Tiger" <note>Yin</note>. Heaven's Benefit is in the "Snake" <note>Si</note>. The "Five Riches" are in the "Pig" <note>Hai</note>. Return Taboos fall on the "Rat" <note>Zi</note>. Departure Taboos fall on the "Monkey" <note>Shen</note>. "Great Failure" falls on the "Dog" <note>Jiaxu</note> day. The Dipper is in the Yang. Blood Taboos fall on the "Tiger" <note>Yin</note>.</gloss>

The third month of spring is when the ten thousand things bloom and display their beauty. Heaven and Earth generate life together; the Yang energy is blazing, and the Yin energy is hidden. Rise early and go to bed early. Do not allow yourself to sweat profusely, so as to nourish the stored energy of the organs. Do not eat leeks, as they trigger chronic diseases and damage the spirit and energy. Do not eat horse meat, as it makes the soul and spirit restless. Do not eat the meat of elk or deer, as it harms the energy and the will. In this month, the Liver energy begins to hide, and the **Heart** is about to become the ruling organ. It is advisable to support the Liver and supplement the Kidneys to stay in harmony with the season. On the 5th day of this month, avoid looking at anything involving raw blood; one should fast, sit in quiet contemplation of sacred texts, and avoid worldly affairs. On the 16th day, avoid traveling far by land or water. On the 27th day, it is auspicious to bathe. In this month, the Fire element is in a state of assistance, and the Water element is "Dead." Do not expose yourself to Northwest winds or stay long in damp places, as this will surely invite toxic influences. Do not face the wind when sweating heavily, and do not expose your naked body under the stars, lest you invite misfortune.

In this month, strictly avoid the unseasonable winds from the Northwest. This is "Evil Qi"; if it strikes you, it will cause the four limbs to be blocked and the hundred joints to lose their strength.

It is advisable to assist the Kidney energy to strengthen the sinews and bones. Be extremely cautious of "thieving evil winds." In the sixth month, one should bathe and fast, cutting off worldly entanglements. On the 24th day, avoid traveling far by land or water. In this month, it is not suitable to begin any earth-moving or construction projects, as authority will not be effectively exercised. Avoid "warm energy" <note>heat stroke or humid heat</note>. Do not face the wind immediately after bathing. Do not habitually soak the hands and feet in cold water. Be careful of the evil wind coming from the East; if it strikes, it causes the hands to become paralyzed and slow, the body to feel heavy, shortness of breath, and weakness in the limbs.

### The Second Month of Autumn: Mid-Autumn
<gloss>The Dipper points to the "Rooster" <note>You</note> position. The Sun is in the "Wings" <note>Yi</note> constellation. The musical pitch corresponds to "The Southern Pipe" <note>Nanlü</note>. One should assist the Liver energy to strengthen the tendons and nourish the **Spleen** and **Stomach**. On the 7th day of this month, it is best to shut out external worries, bathe, and fast; this is auspicious. On the 29th day, avoid traveling far; one should not travel by water or land. Keep your daily routine in accordance with the time. Do not expose yourself to "thieving evil winds." Do not increase your consumption of fatty or greasy foods, as they cause sudden illness. One must especially avoid the "true poisonous energy" of this season. This month is a time to offer thanks and seek blessings to remove past transgressions.

On the 18th day, avoid traveling far, as you will not reach your destination. On the 20th day, it is best to fast, bathe, and maintain pure thoughts; you will surely obtain auspiciousness, as Heaven protects and blesses such a person.

# Discourse on the Message of Preserving Life

### Written by Qiu Chuji of Dongmu during the Yuan Dynasty
<note>Qiu Chuji (1148–1227) was a renowned Daoist master and leader of the Dragon Gate sect. This text focuses on "Yang Sheng" or life-nourishing practices aligned with the seasons.</note>

## Message on Preserving Life in the Spring Season

The three months of Spring are what is called "dispersing the old." Heaven and Earth both give birth to life, and the ten thousand things flourish. One should go to sleep at night and rise early, walk with broad strides in the courtyard, and loosen the hair and walk slowly to allow the mind’s resolve to come alive. Give life and do not kill; give to others and do not take away; reward and do not punish. This is the response to the nourishment of <term>Qi</term> <note>vital energy</note> and the Way of preserving life. To go against this will injure the **Liver**. The Liver corresponds to **Wood** and its flavor is **Sour**. Wood has the power to overcome **Earth**. Earth corresponds to the **Spleen**, which is dominated by the **Sweet** flavor. During the time of Spring, one’s diet should decrease sour flavors and increase sweet flavors to nourish the **Spleen Qi**.

As the Spring **Yang** energy first begins to rise, the ten thousand things start to sprout. Between the 1st and 2nd months, the weather is suddenly cold and suddenly hot. Elderly people often have lingering chronic illnesses; when the Spring energy attacks them, their spirits become dim and weary, and their old ailments flare up. Furthermore, since the past winter, they have huddled by stoves, scented their clothes with smoke, and eaten roasted and fried foods. This accumulation of heat reaches its peak in Spring and then vents outward, leading to body heat, dizziness, obstructions in the diaphragm, coughing with phlegm, weariness in the four limbs, and weakness in the waist and legs. These are all illnesses stored up during the winter.

One should constantly monitor their physical condition. If you feel a slight flare-up of an old ailment, you must not immediately take harsh purgative medicines, for fear of damaging the internal organs and causing other complications. Only use remedies that "dispel wind and harmonize energy" or "cool the diaphragm and transform phlegm." Alternatively, select a recipe from a dietary therapy guide that is slightly cooling in nature, beneficial for eating and drinking, and use it to regulate and balance the body; naturally, things will flow smoothly. If there are no symptoms of illness, one must not take medicine.

On Spring days when the air is mild and harmonious, one should gaze out from gardens, groves, pavilions, and open spaces to release stagnant thoughts and allow the "birthing energy" to flow freely. One must not sit in a daze, as this creates other forms of stagnation. One must not drink too much wine. At this time, households make their own rice and flour cakes, which often damage the Spleen and Stomach and are the most difficult to digest. Elderly people must never eat too much on an empty stomach just to satisfy a momentary craving, as this leads to unexpected complications. Because the weather fluctuates between cold and warm, one must not suddenly discard their quilted cotton clothing. The <term>Qi</term> of the elderly is weak, their bones are sparse, and their bodies are frail; they are easily injured by wind and cold. One should always have lined garments ready at the skin's pores <note>referring to the "interstices" or "Li" where the body meets the environment</note>; when it is warm, remove one layer, and gradually reduce layers one by one. Do not remove them all at once.

The Recluse Liu says: "Illnesses that come in Spring mostly stem from after the Winter Solstice. At midnight, the 'One Yang' is born. If the Yang has no outlet for venting and the Yin has no capacity for receiving, then the residual heat in the heart and diaphragm will clash with the rising Yang energy. It is like two tigers meeting in a narrow..."

...path will be obstructed. When reaching the transition between Spring and Summer, this deficiency allows "Cold Damage" and "Vacuity Heat" to take hold. The troubles of seasonal epidemics arise because, during the winter months, people huddled by fires and ate roasted foods; the phlegm that lodged in the heart and diaphragm then flows into the four limbs. One should take phlegm-dispelling medicines to guide this out, so that it does not become a full-blown disease. One must not allow the back to grow cold; if the back is cold, it immediately injures the **Lungs**, causing nasal congestion and coughing. If the body feels excessively hot, remove a small amount of upper clothing, but if it feels slightly cold, do not force yourself to endure it—immediately add more layers. As the proverbs say: "Avoid the wind as you would avoid an arrow; avoid lust as you would avoid a riot," and "Adjust your clothing according to the hour; eat less after the <term>Shen</term> hour <note>3:00 PM to 5:00 PM</note>."

# The Liver Flourishing in Spring

The **Liver** belongs to **Wood**. It is governed by the **Green Emperor**. In the <term>Bagua</term> <note>the eight Daoist trigrams</note>, it corresponds to **Zhen** <note>The Arousing/Thunder</note>. Its spiritual form is the **Azure Dragon**, and its shape is like a hanging gourd. The word for Liver (*Gan*) means "trunk" (*Gan*); its shape is like the branches and trunk of a tree. it is located in the lower torso, slightly near the **Heart**, with three lobes on the left and four lobes on the right. Its color is like white silk reflecting a deep navy blue. The **Liver** is the mother of the **Heart** and the child of the **Kidneys**. Within the **Liver**, there are three spirits named *Shuangling* (Refreshing Spirit), *Taiguang* (Embryonic Light), and *Youjing* (Ethereal Essence). When lying down at night and at dawn, one should click the teeth thirty-six times and call out the names of these Liver spirits to make the spirit clear and the <term>Qi</term> refreshing.

The **Eyes** are the official portal of the Liver. The left eye corresponds to the <term>Jia</term> stem and the right eye to the <term>Yi</term> stem <note>Jia and Yi are the two "Heavenly Stems" associated with the Wood element</note>. When a man reaches sixty, his **Liver Qi** declines, the lobes of the liver become thin, the bile gradually diminishes, and the eyes become dim and cloudy. In physical form, it manifests in the **Sinews** (tendons). The pulse of the **Liver** harmonizes with **Wood**. It is the storehouse of the <term>Hun</term> <note>the "Ethereal Soul" associated with mental activity and dreaming</note>. Among bodily fluids, it is expressed as **Tears**. When the "evils" of the **Kidney** enter the **Liver**, it results in excessive tearing. Among the six hollow organs, the **Gallbladder** is the palace of the **Liver**, as the Gallbladder and Liver are paired. Therefore, when the **Liver Qi** flows through, it distinguishes the five colors. If the **Liver** is "excessive," the eyes will turn yellow.

The **Heart** harmonizes with the pulse, but its glory is found in the nails; this is where the **Liver** connects. If the sinews are limp and weak and the pulse cannot sustain itself, the **Liver** is the first to die. The eyes correspond to *Jia* and *Yi*. The hours correspond to *Yin* and *Mao* <note>3:00 AM to 7:00 AM</note>. In music, its sound belongs to *Jue* (the "horn" note). Its flavor is **Sour**. Its smell is **Rancid**. If the "evils" of the **Heart** enter the **Liver**, one will develop a loathing for rancid smells. Externally, the **Liver** responds to the **Eastern Peak** <note>Mount Tai</note>, and above it connects to the essence of the **Year Star** <note>the planet Jupiter</note>.

During the three months of Spring, one should constantly visualize the green energy of the **Year Star** entering the **Liver**. Thus, those with **Liver** deficiency will have cramped sinews. Those with withered skin have **Liver** heat. Those with spots on the muscles and flesh have "**Liver Wind**." When a person's complexion is green, the **Liver** is overabundant. When a person craves sour flavors, the **Liver** is insufficient. When a person's hair is withered, the **Liver** is injured. Only when a person's hands and feet perspire freely is the **Liver** truly without disease. If the "evils" of the **Lung** enter the **Liver**, the person will weep frequently. To treat **Liver** disease, one should use the *Xu* <note>a "hissing" sound</note> breath. The *Xu* breath is for purging (sedating), while inhalation is for supplementing (tonifying).

Its character is **Benevolence**. It loves to perform acts of kindness and mercy, and it is a source of compassion. This is why one sheds tears upon hearing something sad. During the three months of Spring, when the water is flourishing <note>likely referring to the generative "mother" of Wood</note> and the energy of Heaven and Earth is being born, those who wish to pacify their spirits should extend their kindness to all living things and let their grace soak into all creatures. Do not exhaust the rivers and marshes. Do not drain the ponds and embankments. Do not harm the new sprouts. Love life and do not kill, so as to harmonize with the Great Purity and the life-giving nature of Heaven and Earth.

...of the energy. One should lie down at night and rise early to harmonize with the "balanced path." If one goes against this, the hair and bones will not flourish, **Metal** and **Wood** will clash <note>In the Five Elements, Metal (Lungs) overcomes Wood (Liver); disharmony here causes systemic illness</note>, and various diseases will arise.

## Method for Observing Liver Diseases

When the **Liver** is hot, the left cheek will be red. When the **Liver** is diseased, the vision is lost and there is pain beneath the ribs that pulls toward the lower abdomen, making a person prone to bouts of anger. If the **Liver** is "deficient," the person feels fear, as if someone is about to capture them. If it is "excessive," the person is prone to anger. If the **Liver** is deficient, there is cold; when there is cold, the <term>Yin Qi</term> becomes too strong, causing one to dream of wandering through mountain forests. 

If the **Liver Qi** flows backward (rebelliously), it causes headaches, deafness, and swollen cheeks. The **Liver** naturally desires to "disperse" (spread energy); one should quickly eat **Pungent** flavors to assist this dispersal, and use **Sour** flavors to supplement it. One must avoid the wind, as the **Liver** has an aversion to wind. 

If the **Liver** is diseased, there will be a "moving energy" <note>a pulsing sensation</note> to the left of the navel; if pressed, it feels hard or painful. This may be accompanied by a feeling of fullness in the limbs, urinary difficulty, or trouble with bowel movements, and a tendency toward muscle cramps. When the **Liver** is ill, the person is often dazed and prone to excessive sleep. A "membrane" may grow over the eyes, vision becomes blurred as if "flying flies" are dancing up and down, or growths may appear on the eyeballs. Other symptoms include "halos" in the vision, cold tears, and redness or itching in the corners of the eyes. In such cases, one should take medicinal formulas containing <term>Shengma</term> <note>Cimicifuga or Black Cohosh, used to clear heat and lift sunken energy</note> to disperse the "evils."

## Advice for Maintaining Health in the Summer

The three months of **Summer** belong to **Fire**. This season is primarily responsible for "growth and nourishment." The **Heart Qi** and **Fire** are flourishing. The corresponding flavor is **Bitter**. Since **Fire** can overcome **Metal**, and **Metal** corresponds to the **Lungs** (which are associated with the **Pungent** flavor), one must adjust their diet during the summer. It is appropriate to **decrease bitter flavors and increase pungent flavors** to nourish the **Lungs**.

When the **Heart Qi** needs regulation, one should use the *He* <note>a "haaa" sound</note> breath to disperse it and the *Xu* <note>a "hissing" sound</note> breath to smooth it. 

During the "Three Dog Days" <note>the hottest period of summer</note>, the inside of the abdomen is actually often cold. During this time, one should avoid diarrhea, as there is a fear of leaking out the <term>Yin Qi</term>. For this reason, acupuncture and moxibustion are not recommended; only inducing perspiration is appropriate. After the **Summer Solstice**, the first "unit" of **Yin** energy is born at midnight. One should consume warm foods and take tonifying soups for the **Kidneys**. 

During the summer, the **Heart** is flourishing but the **Kidneys** are weak. Even in great heat, one must not eat cold noodles, ice, snow, honey-ice, cold jellies, or cold porridge. Filling the belly with such items and allowing the body to catch a cold will inevitably lead to <term>Huoluan</term> <note>a traditional term for acute vomiting and diarrhea</note>. Do not eat melons, eggplant, or raw vegetables. Because the abdomen is just beginning to receive the "cool" **Yin** energy, eating these stagnant, cold things will often cause "accumulations and masses" (lumps or tumors) to form. People suffering from "cold phlegm" or "fire" must strictly avoid these. 

The elderly should be especially careful. In daily life, one must not seek coolness under the eaves of houses, in corridors, in drafty streets, or by broken windows. Although these places feel cool, the "Thief Wind" <note>harmful, unexpected drafts</note> found there strikes a person most violently. Instead, one should stay in airy halls, clean rooms, waterside pavilions, under the shade of trees, or in clean, empty spaces; these are naturally cool. 

Furthermore, one should regulate the breath. If the heart is kept as still and pure as ice and snow, the feeling of scorching heat will naturally diminish. One must not "use heat to fight heat" <note>by getting agitated</note>, as this only creates more internal heat. Daily, one should take mild, warming, and tonifying pills or powders. Food and drink should be warm, and one should never eat to the point of being overly full. It is beneficial to regularly consume cinnamon soup or cardamom-steeped water. One must abstain from greasy and fatty foods. Do not lie exposed under the stars or the moon, and do not fall asleep while someone is fanning you to provide a breeze. Although it feels pleasant for a moment, the wind enters the "texture of the skin" <note>the pores and interstitial spaces</note>, and the resulting illness will be severe.

One must most deeply avoid craving coolness. Furthermore, if one lies down to sleep while sweaty and exposed to the wind, it often leads to <term>Fengbi</term> <note>original: "風痺", literally "Wind Numbness" or "Wind Blockage," a condition involving joint pain, numbness, or loss of mobility</note>. This causes numbness in the hands and feet, hesitant or slurred speech, and paralysis of the four limbs. Although this does not happen to everyone, some are struck instantly, while others are not. However, the illness will eventually flare up later. If their strength is waning with age, they encounter a "hollow" moon <note>a waning or new moon when energy is low</note>, and the season is discordant, they will inevitably be struck.

The head is the meeting point of all **Yang** <note>active, warm, and external</note> energies; it especially must not be exposed to wind. In sleeping quarters, one should carefully guard against small gaps or tiny holes <note>drafts</note> so as not to injure the <term>Naohu</term> <note>original: "腦戶", literally "Brain Door," an acupuncture point at the base of the skull</note>. During the three months of **Summer**, one should comb their hair one or two hundred times daily, though one must not scrape the scalp too hard. Always comb in a place free from wind. This naturally dispels internal "wind" and brightens the eyes.

The *Treatise on Nourishing Life* says: "Summer is called the season of 'Abundant Flourishing' <note>original: "蕃秀", referring to the peak of growth</note>. The energies of Heaven and Earth intersect, and all things flower and bear fruit. One should lie down at night and rise early, and not grow weary of the long days. Keep the mind free from anger. By the **Winter Solstice**, the illness will become severe. It is also said: "Summer energy is hot; it is appropriate to eat beans to provide a cooling effect, but one should not rely solely on heat." Avoid scalding hot drinks, avoid eating to excess, avoid sleeping on damp ground, and do not wear wet clothes.

It weighs twelve *liang* <note>approximately 1 pound</note>. People of middle wisdom have five apertures, where the heart-holes allow energy to pass. The **Heart** is the "child" of the **Liver** and the "mother" of the **Spleen** <note>Following the Five Elements "Generating Cycle": Wood/Liver feeds Fire/Heart, which creates Earth/Spleen</note>. The **Heart pulse** emerges from the <term>Zhongchong</term> <note>an acupuncture point at the tip of the middle finger</note>. It is the root of life and the dwelling place of the Spirit (*Shen*). It governs clarity and functional movement. The **Heart** is joined with the vessels; its healthy color is radiant. ## Methods for Observing Heart Disease

When there is excess heat in the **Heart**, the face becomes deep red and the pulse feels "overflowing" (large and surging). Sores will form in the mouth, becoming rotten and foul-smelling. There will be pain in the chest, diaphragm, shoulders, back, and both ribs and arms. If the **Heart** is deficient, the heart and the abdomen will pull at each other in pain. The **Heart**'s disease desires "moistening." One should quickly eat salty flavors to moisten it, use bitter flavors to supplement it, and sweet flavors to drain the excess. One must forbid sexual indulgence, "hot" (stimulating) clothing, and hot food. The **Heart** "loathes" heat and water <note>excessive cold/dampness</note>. When the **Heart** is diseased, there is a throbbing pulse above the navel; if pressed, it feels hard. If there is pain, the person will feel even more distressed and anxious. The palms and soles of the feet will feel hot, the mouth will be dry, the tongue stiff, the throat sore, and the breath will be shallow. The person will forget what happened before and lose track of what comes after.

## Information on Maintaining Health in Autumn

The three months of **Autumn** are governed by the energy of "Solemn Killing" <note>original: "肅殺", referring to the cooling energy that withers vegetation and prepares nature for dormancy</note>. After the **Start of Autumn** <note>Liqiu, one of the 24 solar terms</note>, things should gradually become peaceful and balanced. One must be mindful of their health, for the transition between Spring and Autumn is a time when old illnesses often flare up. One must focus on resting and nourishing oneself according to one's own constitution. During the Autumn, it is not advisable to induce vomiting or sweating, as this causes a person to "wither and melt away," leading to instability in the internal organs. It is only appropriate to use acupuncture, moxibustion, or gentle purgatives, and to take medicinal soups or powders to assist the **Yang Qi**. 

Furthermore, if one suffers from chronic exhaustion, the "Five Hemorrhoids," or <term>Xiaoke</term> <note>original: "消渴", "wasting and thirsting" disorder, similar to diabetes</note>, they should avoid eating dry rice, fried or toasted foods, the meat of cattle that died naturally, raw fish slices, chicken, pork, murky wine, stale or foul-smelling things, salty vinegar, or sticky, slippery foods that are difficult to digest, as well as raw vegetables...

## Methods for Observing Lung Disease

* **Lung Vacuity:** Shortness of breath and inability to regulate the breathing.
* **Lung Dryness:** The throat feels dry.
* **Lung Wind:** Excessive sweating, fear of wind, and a cough that sounds like wheezing—better in the morning but worse in the evening.

When the Qi of a disease moves upward in reverse, eat **Bitter** foods immediately to drain it. It is also said: use **Sour** tastes to collect the energy, **Pungent** tastes to supplement it, and **Bitter** tastes to purge it. Forbid the eating of cold items, for the Lungs loathe the cold. If the Lungs are diseased, one cannot smell fragrances or stenches, and the nose may develop **polyps** <note>original: "瘜肉", small growths</note> or sores. The skin will be dry and itchy. If the Qi is too exuberant, there will be coughing with the spitting of pus and blood. In such cases, one should take **Pai Feng San** <note>Wind-Expelling Powder</note>.

# News on Health Preservation for the Winter Season

During the three months of **Winter**, Heaven and Earth are "closed and stored." The water freezes, the earth cracks, and one must not disturb the **Yang energy** <note>the active, warm, life-sustaining force</note>. One should go to bed early and rise late, waiting for the sunlight to appear before getting up. Seek warmth and avoid the cold; do not allow the skin to sweat <note>opening the pores in winter was thought to leak vital heat</note>, for to go against this will harm the **Kidneys**. This results in "atrophy and reversal" <note>weakness or paralysis of the limbs</note> in the Spring, as there is little energy left to support the "birthing" of that season.

At this time, "Hidden Yang" resides within the body. If one falls ill, it is appropriate to induce vomiting. There is often much heat in the heart and diaphragm, but one must avoid inducing sweat, for fear of leaking the Yang energy. It is advisable to take medicinal tonics soaked in wine, or one or two cups of **Wild Yam Wine**, to welcome the Yang energy. 

When sleeping, it is better to have a slightly cool, empty space rather than being stifled. Only when the cold is extreme should one add cotton-padded clothing; add layers gradually and do not put on too much at once. It is enough to simply not feel cold. One must not frequently use large fires for roasting or drying themselves, as this is extremely damaging to a person. The hands and feet correspond to the **Heart**; one should not roast the hands over a fire, as this "leads fire into the Heart," causing a person to become irritable and restless. Do not use fire to roast or cook food directly. Cold medicines will not cure illnesses now, and if the heat is extreme, over-cooked medicines will also fail to cure. Cold tends toward dampness, and fire tends toward dryness. 

Regarding the flavors of food and drink: one should **reduce Sour** and **increase Bitter** to nourish the **Heart Qi**. In the Winter months, the **Kidney Water** possesses a salty taste; there is a fear that "Water will conquer Fire," causing the Heart to suffer disease. Therefore, one must nourish the Heart. One should live in a tightly sealed room, with warm clothing and bedding, and regulate diet to suit the cold or warmth of the environment. One must not expose themselves to the cold wind—this is especially true for the elderly. There is a fear that "Cold Evils" will cause the common cold, leading to coughing, numbness, dizziness, and other ailments. 

In the Winter months, Yang energy is internal and Yin energy is external. The elderly often suffer from "Heat above and Cold below." One should not bathe frequently. When the Yang energy is pent up inside, if it is suddenly forced by hot water, it will inevitably cause heavy sweating. In old age, the bones and flesh are thin and sparse, making one easily affected by external influences, which leads to many external diseases. One must not go out early and encounter the frost. Upon rising early, drink a cup of mellow wine to ward off the cold. In the evening, take medicines that "dissolve phlegm and cool the diaphragm" to balance the Heart Qi and prevent heat from surging upward. One should strictly avoid sexual activity and must not eat too much fried or roasted meat, noodles, dumplings, or similar heavy foods.

## The Kidney Organ Flourishes in Winter

The *Classic of Internal Landscapes* <note>original: "Neijing Jing," a text describing the spiritual and physical anatomy of the body</note> says: The **Kidneys** belong to the North and the element of **Water**. It is the "Palace of Living Qi" and the "Abode of Dying Qi." If you guard it, you survive; if you use it up, you are exhausted. The Kidneys are the "Mother" of the **Liver** <note>Water nourishes Wood</note> and the "Child" of the **Lungs** <note>Metal generates Water</note>.

The movement of Essence and Qi back and forth is called **Spirit** <note>original: "Shen"</note>. As for the Spirit, the Kidneys store its "Emotions" and "Wisdom." 

The left Kidney corresponds to the Heavenly Stem **Ren**, and the right corresponds to **Gui**. In the Earthly Branches, they correspond to **Zi** and **Hai**. In energy/sound, they correspond to **Chui** <note>original: "吹", pronounced 'chwee', one of the Six Healing Sounds</note>. In fluids, they correspond to **Spittle**. In form, they correspond to the **Bones**. Standing for a long time harms the bones, which damages the Kidneys. Their health is reflected in the **Teeth**; if the teeth ache, it is a sign of Kidney damage. Their pathways pass through the **Upper Burner**, flourish in the **Middle Burner**, and protect the **Lower Burner** <note>The "Three Burners" or Triple Heater are functional divisions of the body's torso</note>. The Kidneys...

If "evil influences" <note>external pathogens like cold or dampness</note> enter the body, it results in excessive spitting. The **Bladder** serves as the storehouse for all bodily fluids, and its health is reflected in the luster of the hair. 

The *Yellow Court Classic* <note>original: "Huangting Jing," a Daoist meditation text focused on internal deities</note> says: "The Palace of the Kidney region is a primordial, circular gate. Within it resides a divine youth named **Shangyuan** <note>the 'Superior Origin,' a spiritual representation of the Kidney's vital force</note>. He governs all the internal organs and is the source of the nine bodily fluids. Externally, this corresponds to the two ears and the moisture of all fluids." The sound associated with this organ is *Yu* <note>one of the five tones of ancient Chinese music</note>, its flavor is **Salty**, and its scent is **Rot**. If "Heart-evils" <note>unbalanced energy from the Heart</note> invade the Kidneys, the person will develop a loathing for the smell of rot.

Generally, for a man, at age sixty the **Kidney Qi** <note>vital energy</note> begins to decline; the hair changes color and the teeth become loose. At seventy, the physical body becomes weary and burdened. At ninety, the Kidney Qi is "scorched," the bones wither, and the person cannot rise from bed—this indicates the Kidneys have "died" before the rest of the body. 

When the Kidneys are diseased, it results in deafness and "bone atrophy" <note>weakness or loss of use of the limbs</note>. The Kidneys govern the bones, and their health is visible in the **beard**. Externally, the Kidneys correspond to the **Northern Peak** <note>Mt. Heng, associated with Water and Winter</note>, and they communicate above with the essence of the **Planet Mercury** <note>original: "Chenxing," the Water Star</note>. During the three months of Winter, one should visualize the "Black Qi" of Mercury entering and dwelling within the Kidneys. 

Diagnostic signs of the Kidneys include:
*   Pain in the bones indicates **Kidney Deficiency**.
*   Frequent tooth decay indicates **Kidney Decline**.
*   Loss of teeth indicates **Kidney Wind** <note>a specific type of pathogenic influence causing tremors or loss of stability</note>.
*   Pain in the ears indicates **Kidney Qi Congestion**.
*   Frequent yawning indicates **Kidney Evils**.
*   Inability to straighten the lower back indicates **Kidney Exhaustion**.
*   A black, darkened complexion indicates **Kidney Decline**.
*   A purple, lustrous complexion indicates **no disease** in the Kidneys.
*   Clicking or popping joints indicate **Kidney Weakness**.

If "Lung-evils" enter the Kidneys, the person will groan frequently. When the Kidneys are afflicted, one should use the **"Chui" sound** <note>a blowing sound, 'chwee'</note> to drain the excess energy, and use controlled inhalation to supplement it. This keeps the energy harmonious. If the Kidney Qi is heavy and stagnant, one should use a forceful "Chui" sound to gradually open the pathways. 

When the Kidneys are deficient, one may dream of entering dark places, or see women, monks, nuns, turtles, tortoises, camels, horses, banners, spears, or see oneself clad in armor. One may also dream of walking in the mountains or rowing a boat on a stream. Therefore, during the three months of Winter, when the energy of Heaven and Earth is closed, and the "Ten Thousand Things" are hidden away, the person of noble character <note>original: "Junzi"</note> should be cautious and restrained. One must moderate desires and regulate the senses while waiting for the **Ying and Yang** <note>the balance of dark/light and passive/active forces</note> to stabilize. Do not struggle against the cycle of Yin and Yang, so that you may preserve your life and remain in harmony with **Great Purity** <note>original: "Taiqing," a state of primordial celestial harmony</note>.

## Methods for Observing Kidney Disease

When there is **Heat** in the Kidneys, the chin becomes red. When there is **Disease**, the complexion is black, the teeth are dry, the abdomen is distended, the body feels heavy, and there is coughing, sweating, and an aversion to wind. 

**Kidney Deficiency** causes pain in the center of the lower back. The symptoms of **Kidney Wind** include excessive sweating from the neck, aversion to wind, and a desire to eat but an inability to swallow due to a blockage in the diaphragm; the abdomen feels full, and eating cold food leads to diarrhea. 

If the body is dark and thin, it indicates **Kidney Dryness**; one should quickly eat **Acrid** flavors to moisten it. If the Kidney disease is "Hard" <note>stubborn or excess</note>, one should quickly eat **Salty** flavors to supplement it and **Bitter** flavors to drain it. Do not consume overcooked food, and do not wear clothing that is too warm. 

If there is "Moving Qi" <note>a pulsing sensation</note> below the navel that feels firm or painful when pressed, or if food does not digest, the body feels heavy, the bones ache, the hips and bladder suffer from "cold pain," or the legs are painful or numb with urinary dribbling and the presence of <term>hernias or masses</term> <note>original: "Shan jia," abdominal masses or protrusions</note>, one should take the **Kidney Qi Pill**.

Lord **Xue Wenqing** <note>original: "Xue Wenqing gong," referring to Xue Xuan (1389–1464), a prominent Neo-Confucian philosopher of the Ming Dynasty</note> said: The most critical part of one’s **disciplined effort** <note>original: "Gongfu," here referring to the internal work of self-cultivation and character building</note> lies in the transition between dawn and dusk. # The Recorded Sayings of the Perfected One of Danyang
## Collected by Wang Yizhong, the Master of Hidden Spirit

In the third month of the **Guimao year of the Dading era** <note>1183 CE, during the Jin Dynasty</note>, I first paid my respects to the Master south of the hermitage of Fan Mingshu in Muping. The Master asked, "From where have you come?" I replied, "I have come from Dongwu. I look up to your virtue, Master—that you do not consider material wealth to be true riches, but remain tranquil and self-possessed as you advance in this **Way** <note>the Dao</note>. Having heard of your reputation, I was moved with joy and wished to serve you as a humble attendant and listen to your words."

The Master was pleased and said, "It is a rare thing for a youth to possess a heart that seeks the Way." After a long silence, he added: "When you are hungry, eat your fill; when you are finished eating, go and sleep."

One day, the Master saw me standing with my hands clasped respectfully. He scolded me, saying, "A seeker of the Way must be open and unconstrained. You must not maintain a stiff, formal appearance. A hermitage is not a **government office** <note>original: "xieyu," an official administrative building</note>, and you are not a high official. If you insist on these worldly etiquettes, you will miss the true point of our connection. The ancients said: 'Among companions of the three sacred mountains, human attachments are as thin as the sea; for those without a home, the path of righteousness is deep.' These words were not spoken in vain."

The Master often taught, saying, "Those who study the Way must rely on **self-awakening** <note>original: "ziwu"</note>. Those who do not awaken fail because they are clouded by ignorance. To dispel this ignorance, you must first wash your heart. It is simply a matter of making it peaceful and clear. When your effort is sufficient, the goal is achieved. You do not need to beg for answers from others. Whether your work is skillful or clumsy will become perfectly clear to you."

While the Master was traveling on the road in Eastern Mou, whenever he encountered monks or Daoists—whether he knew them or not—he would always be the first to bow. His followers were puzzled and asked, "We have no prior acquaintance with these people; why is it necessary to bow?" 

The Master replied, "The Way takes **softness, weakness, and humility** <note>core virtues in the Dao De Jing</note> as its foundation. Furthermore, the **three teachings** <note>Confucianism, Buddhism, and Daoism</note> come from the same gate; they are merely different doors to the same house. Confucius said that he would perform even the humble task of a carriage driver for a worthy person; I have never heard of a single bow being considered a mistake."

The Master said: "The **Ancestral Master** <note>original: "Zushi," referring to Wang Chongyang (1113–1170), the founder of Quanzhen Daoism</note> was naturally skilled in literature. After he realized the Way, he became even more quick-witted. Whether it was composing hidden acrostics, deconstructing characters, or creating riddles and 'linked pearls' of verse, he did so without the slightest effort. He often composed poems in response to others. Once, when everyone was using the word 'joint' as a rhyme, the Ancestral Master was the last to finish. He wrote: 'Three hundred and sixty golden joints.' Everyone was moved to deep admiration, considering it the language of an immortal. Who could succeed him today? Perhaps only the **Duke of Panxi** <note>original: "Panxi gong," referring to Qiu Chuji (1148–1227), another of the 'Seven Perfected Ones' and a successor to the lineage</note> comes close to following in those footsteps."

The Master also said: "When the Ancestral Master first arrived in Dengzhou, he wore a bamboo hat and tattered clothes like a **quail's feathers** <note>a metaphor for ragged, patched clothing</note>. He carried a bamboo staff and an iron gourd. His appearance was strange and ancient, and he begged for food in the marketplaces. The people of Dengzhou did not recognize him for who he was. At night, he would return to his lodgings to read books."

<summary>This page records the first meeting between the disciple Wang Yizhong and the Daoist Master Ma Danyang, emphasizing themes of humility, self-awakening, and the "ordinary" nature of the spiritual life. It also includes anecdotes about the legendary founder Wang Chongyang's eccentric behavior and literary brilliance.</summary>

A seven-character quatrain was written on the wall:

"A farewell to the Water-Bamboo Village of the Southern Mountains <note>The Zhongnan Mountains, a famous retreat for hermits and the site of Wang Chongyang's early cultivation</note>.
In my home, I have no sons, nor have I grandsons.
From thousands of miles away, I sought a true friend,
To lead them through the gate of long life and immortality."

The next day, he brushed off his clothes and journeyed toward the East.

A few days later, the regional governor, a man named Heshelie <note>A common Jurchen surname during the Jin Dynasty</note>, visited the hermitage. He saw the poem inscribed there and was filled with such deep admiration that he composed a poem using the same rhyme scheme:

"Looking back, it has been three years since I left my old village,
I have quite forgotten the courtyard bamboo and the growth of my children.
At another time, I shall brush off my sleeves and come seeking you,
Hoping for a peaceful moment to knock at your gate."

->The Master said: Subtle flavors are for nourishing your **vital energy** <term>Qi: the life force or breath that sustains the body</term>. Discarding anger is for nourishing your **inner nature** <note>original: "xing," one's original spiritual character</note>. Enduring insults and staying in a lowly position is for nourishing your **virtue**. Maintaining a state of clarity, stillness, and contentment is for nourishing the **Way**. When your name is no longer recorded on official registers and your heart is no longer tied to power or profit, you have shed the human husk and become a companion of Heaven.<-

->The Master said: Wine is a liquid that throws one's nature into chaos. Meat is a substance that cuts life short. It is best to abstain from them entirely. If you slip and consume wine or meat, it may yet be forgiven; but if you slip into **lustful desire** <note>original: "se," referring to sexual craving or physical attraction</note>, your crime is beyond pardon. Why is this? Lust is fiercer than a wild tiger. It ruins a person's noble conduct, destroys their good works, wastes their essence, and extinguishes their spirit, even leading to the death of the body. Therefore, it is the greatest obstacle for a person of the Way.<-

->The Master said: There is no greater joy in a time of peace than to be a leisurely person of the Way. If you grow weary of staying in a hermitage, find one or two companions. Carry your travel bags over your shoulders, take up a staff, and wander while singing. Seek out beautiful mountains and fine waters; linger under the moon. Do not be in a hurry to reach your destination.<-

The Master said to me: "A student of the Way must have a beginning and an end. You must not give up halfway and become a laughingstock to others. Furthermore, you are a 'child of books' <note>an educated youth</note>. Surely you know that for a person to establish themselves in the world, they must have a vocation. For us, the pursuit of the Way is the ultimate vocation for a true man."

The Master once wrote a couplet in large characters for his Daoist friends:

"Quickly pull down the Mountain of Self and Other;
Urgently break through the Dragon and Tiger Den."

I asked him: "I have come to understand the 'Mountain of Self and Other' <note>a metaphor for the ego and the dualistic thinking that separates people</note>. But may I ask about the 'Dragon and Tiger Den'?"

The Master laughed and said: "Heaven's secrets may not be handed over lightly. Look into it closely, worthy one, and see if you awaken or not." <note>The 'Dragon and Tiger' are common alchemical metaphors for the energies of the breath (wood/east) and the vital essence (metal/west) that must be harmonized within the body.</note>

One day, the Master called for me. It took me a long time to answer and go to him. He asked where I had been. I replied, "I had just had a full afternoon nap and felt my spirit was clear and calm. There was a copy of the **Zhuangzi** <note>The classic Daoist text by the philosopher Zhuang Zhou</note> at the head of my bed, so I picked it up to read. That is why I was not here."

The Master said: "The Way requires the heart to be in harmony with it. If you allow yourself to be bound by written words again, when will there ever be an end to it? As the saying goes: 'If you try to understand the **Classic of Southern Florescence** <note>original: "Nanhua," the honorary title for the Zhuangzi</note> through the intellect alone, the more you understand, the more lost you become.'"

While the Master was in Huating, he said: "What is this thing called the Way? **Ancestral Energy** <term>Zuqi: the primordial life force inherited at birth</term> is the very root and source. Do you not recognize it as that which exits and enters through the nose? Have you not heard what the immortal Guangchengzi <note>A legendary figure said to have taught the Yellow Emperor the secrets of longevity</note> said?"

->“Cease your frantic laboring with the alchemical furnace and the waterwheel; 
The crane’s embryo and the turtle’s breath are naturally continuous.”<-

The Master spoke to the assembly, saying: "If one is single-minded in studying the Way, then every person can become an immortal. It is not like the worldly pursuit of official rank, where some are promoted and others are rejected. The way of the scholar is broad but lacks the essentials; the Way is simple and easy to practice. Simply remaining in a state of **Clarity, Stillness, and Non-action** <term>Wuwei: effortless action in harmony with the Dao</term> is the most supreme method."

***

The Master lived within a small, enclosed cell. He had nothing there but a small desk, a couch, a brush, an inkstone, and a sheepskin; he was utterly unencumbered by possessions. In the morning, he ate a single bowl of porridge, and at noon, a bowl of noodles. Beyond this, no fruit or vegetables passed his lips. One day, he called me in and told me to sit. After a long silence, I asked, "Does my Master’s Way involve deliberate action?" 

The Master replied: "It does not. Although my songs and poems often mention the **Dragon and Tiger** or the **Infant and Maiden** <note>metaphors in internal alchemy for the balancing of Yin and Yang energies</note>, these are all merely figurative language. The essence of the essential Way is nothing more than **Nourishing Qi** <term>Yangqi: the practice of preserving and refining one's internal energy</term>. Most people drown themselves in profit and fame, constantly wasting and dissipating their energy. A student of the Way has no other task but to nourish this energy. When the 'liquid' of the heart descends and the 'energy' of the kidneys rises, they meet at the spleen. When the **Original Energy** <term>Yuanqi</term> is thick and swirling without being scattered, the 'Elixir' gathers. The liver and lungs serve as the pathways for this coming and going. If you practice stillness for a long time, you will naturally come to understand this yourself. If you do not nourish your energy, even if you could lift Mount Tai or leap over the North Sea, it would not be the Way." 

These words were spoken ten days before his passing. While I and two or three companions, including Zeng and Liu, were standing outside his cell, he suddenly came out and said: "The Way is simply: **Clarity, Stillness, Non-action, Carefree Ease, Self-Sufficiency, Untaintedness, and Non-attachment.** <note>original: "Qingjing wuwei, xiaoyao zizai, buran buzhu"</note> If you can truly 'chew through' and digest these twelve characters, you will be a Daoist to the very core. Just trust this old man’s words; if you practice them, you will certainly find benefit. I would never mislead you young men."

***

While at the hermitage of Ma Congren in the western suburbs of Huang County, the Master sang:

->"Even if you consume ten thousand ounces of gold a day, 
It is better to win simple clothes and plain food."<-

He mentioned that last year, while passing through the outer gate, he heard someone reciting these words. He liked the truth in them so much that he memorized them, though he did not know who wrote them. A man named Ma Yuanzhi said, "These words come from the *Huajiang Collection* by the Elder Shun." The Master remarked, "How extraordinary those words are!"

***

The Master said: "Who is the ancestor of our family tradition? It was passed down directly from Zhong and Lü <note>Zhongli Quan and Lü Dongbin, the legendary patriarchs of the Quanzhen lineage</note>." He offered a poem:

->"A single point of Numinous Light illuminates the Great Void; 
Even the most skilled painter could not capture its likeness. 
Do not idly compare it to the bright moon; 
The moon has phases of waning, so how could it be like me?"<-

These words showed a bit of his sharp, hidden power.

***

The Master said: "Energy is as difficult to govern as a galloping horse. Only those who are still find it easy. You must cast away external longings. Even when you see the chaotic splendor of the world before your eyes, you must feel as though you are in a deep mountain or a remote valley. Only then is it the Way."

Human intentions and character cannot be stolen. In the realm of **No-Mind** <term>Wuxin: a state of mind free from attachment, ego, and discriminatory thought</term>, nothing can be controlled or restricted. Therefore, those who know the Way value the state of No-Mind above all else.

***

## The Master also said:
The Master also said: "When the heart is stable, then worldly emotions are forgotten. When the body is empty, then **Qi** <term>internal energy or life force</term> circulates. When the [deluded] heart dies, the Spirit becomes alive. When **Yang** <term>the active, bright, masculine principle</term> flourishes, then **Yin** <term>the receptive, dark, feminine principle</term> is extinguished. This is the law of nature. 

Those who are ignorant do not understand this; they only focus on schemes for their children and grandchildren, and in turn, they view those who study the Way as useless. How could they fail to reflect so deeply?"

***

## The Master said:
The Master said: "I was over forty years old when I first met my teacher and entered the Way. That is why my hair is now white. Yet, within my belly, there is another 'one with indigo hair.' How was this achieved? It came simply from spending more than ten years in the Guanzhong region nourishing my Spirit and Energy. It is like an echo in an empty valley; when there is a call from within, there is a corresponding answer. How could it be some other object? It is simply because the center is 'flushed and empty' <term>Chongxu: a state of meditative void</term>. If you, my friends, do not believe me, then truly cultivate stillness and emptiness to nourish it, and you shall know it for yourselves."

***

## The Master spoke of Lord Haichan
The Master said: "Lord Haichan <note>Liu Haichan, a prominent Daoist immortal and a predecessor in the Quanzhen lineage</note> was originally a high Chancellor for the State of Yan. One day he awakened to the Way and immediately severed his family ties. His poetry contains lines such as: 

->'I have abandoned a household of three thousand souls; 
I have cast aside a family protected by a million soldiers.'<-

Afterward, he supported himself solely by begging for food, wandering through marketplaces and acting out plays. He even went so far as to carry wine and tuck combs into his hair for those in brothels, feeling no shame. Some of those who study the Way today say, 'I come from a wealthy and noble background,' but they cannot even begin to compare themselves to Lord Haichan." 

<note>The "household of three thousand" and "million soldiers" refers to leaving the "Burning House" <gloss>huozhai: a Buddhist metaphor for the world of suffering and desire</gloss></note>

***

## The Master spoke on the Way of Clarity and Stillness
The Master said: "If a person can discern the **Way of Clarity and Stillness** <term>Qingjing zhi dao</term>, then they have reached the height of goodness and beauty. Thus, the scripture says: 'If a person can remain constantly clear and still, Heaven and Earth will both return to them.' 

When the text speaks of 'Heaven and Earth,' it does not refer to the external sky and ground that cover and support us. Rather, it refers to the **Heaven and Earth within the body**. In a human, the area above the diaphragm is Heaven, and the area below the diaphragm is Earth. If the 'Heavenly Energy' descends and the 'Earthly Meridians' open, then the upper and lower will harmonize in a state of 'flushed peace,' and the **Essential Energy** <term>Jingqi</term> will naturally become solid. This is what the Little Immortal Ren taught."

***

## The Master spoke on Guarding Energy
The Master said: "The secret of **Guarding Energy** <term>Shouqi</term> lies entirely in preserving the **Essence** <term>Jing: the physical/vital foundation of life</term>. One must be especially defensive regarding sleep. When you are about to sleep, let right-mindfulness manifest before you, and let the ten thousand worries all vanish. Coil your body and lie on your side, with your nasal breathing being continuous and fine. Then the soul will not be agitated within, and the spirit will not wander outside. In this way, the Energy and Essence will naturally stabilize."

***

## The Master said of the Confucian School
The Master said: "The Confucian school says: 'Repay virtue with virtue, and repay resentment with justice.' In ancient times, the **Realized Man** <term>Zhenren: a perfected Daoist master</term> said: 'Use care to make friends, and use kindness to repay an enemy.' This can be called the ultimate expression of the Way."

When the Master was in Laizhou, a man named Jiang Xi brought a biography of Lord Lü <note>referring to the immortal Lü Dongbin, one of the Eight Immortals</note> to present to him. The Master read the passage: "Worldly people only strive for fame and profit; they do not know that the body possesses a Spirit. They chase after external things and never return, completely losing their **Heavenly Truth** <term>Tianzhen: one's original, uncorrupted nature</term>. Who is to blame for this?" 

The Master closed the book and said to Jiang Xi: "These words truly strike the heart of the matter. Yet, there are no awakened ones in this world—how difficult it is for the Way to be practiced!"

***

There was a man named Han Tao, styled Qingfu, who admired the character of Tao Yuanming <note>a famous hermit-poet of the 4th century</note> and Shao Yaofu <note>Shao Yong, a prominent philosopher and cosmologist of the Song Dynasty</note>. He went by the title "The Gentleman of the Garden of Peace and Joy." When the Master returned from the region west of the pass to Dongmu, his path took him through Jinan. Han Tao invited the Master into his garden and provided him with a simple meal of noodles. 

After finishing the meal, Han Tao bowed his head to the Master and said: "I have admired the Way since my youth, and now my hair is turning white. I am fortunate to meet you, my Master. I hope you will grant me a single word to illuminate my foolishness and ignorance."

The Master replied: "The Way takes **No-Mind** as its essence and the forgetting of words as its function. It takes softness and weakness as its root, and **Clarity and Stillness** <term>Qingjing</term> as its foundation. If you are to apply this to yourself, you must moderate your food and drink, sever your worries and thoughts, sit in stillness to regulate your breathing, and sleep peacefully to nourish your **Energy** <term>Qi</term>. 

When the heart does not race, the inner nature becomes stable. When the physical form is not overworked, the **Essence** <term>Jing</term> remains whole. When the Spirit is not disturbed, the **Elixir** <term>Dan: the concentrated internal result of alchemical practice</term> forms. Then, by dissolving emotions into the Void and steadying the Spirit in the Ultimate, one can obtain the Wondrous Way without even stepping out of the courtyard."

Han Tao thanked him, saying: "The Great Way is vast and misty; I had nowhere to begin my inquiries. Now, hearing this profound discourse, I have found the gate through which to enter."

***

The two gentlemen, Cao and Lai, were originally Confucian scholars. They had followed the Master to study the Way for many years, remaining his constant and loyal companions. Someone asked them: "When the Master was west of the pass, how did he manage his practice?"

Cao and Lai replied: "In both winter and summer, the Master wore only a single, simple cloth garment. He ate coarse food, taking only enough to be full. In the depths of winter, amidst the snow and cold, there was no fire in his hut. At times, he even used cold water. Yet his **Spirit and Energy** remained harmonious and flowing; he felt no sense of cold at all. Having lived like this for ten years, if he did not possess the **Energy of the Way** <term>Daoqi</term> within his belly, he could not have endured it."

***

## The Master said:
"In all things, if there is preparation, there will be no disaster. Therefore, those who practice the Way must guard against their passions and desires while they are young and strong. If you prepare early, then becoming a Divine Immortal can be hoped for. If you wait until your hair is thinning and your collar is drooping—when your will and energy are exhausted—before beginning to study the Way, it is like waiting for the Great Cold to arrive before searching for a fur coat. Is it not too late?"

***

## The Master said:
"The thirty-six methods of **Guiding Energy** <term>Daoyin: stretching and breathing exercises</term> and the twenty-four methods of the **Returned Elixir** are merely 'gradual gates' <note>preliminary or introductory stages</note> for entering the Way; they should not be mistaken for the Great Way itself. To exhaust oneself with external furnaces and cauldrons, or to use the imagery of the Tortoise and the Snake <note>symbolic animals in Daoist alchemy representing Water/North and Fire/South</note>, is simply to create trouble where there is none, adding artificiality to one's inner nature. These things mislead people greatly. 

The Daoist school has left behind thousands of scriptures on the Elixir and ten thousand discourses. These can all be summed up in one phrase: **Clarity and Stillness**."

***

## The Master said:
"Regarding **Clarity and Stillness**: 'Clarity' means to clear the source of the heart. 'Stillness' means to purify the sea of Energy. When the source of the heart is clear, external objects cannot disturb it; thus, the emotions are stabilized and the radiance of the Spirit is born. When the sea of Energy is purified, perverse desires cannot interfere; thus, the Essence is made whole and the belly becomes full. Therefore, clarifying the heart is like clarifying water, and nourishing the Energy is like nourishing a child. When the Energy is refined, the Spirit becomes divine; when the Spirit is divine, the Energy transforms. This is the result of Clarity and Stillness..."

<summary>Ma Danyang explains that internal alchemy is rooted in "Clarity and Stillness" rather than complex exercises, emphasizing early practice and the purification of the heart and Energy.</summary>
<keywords>Lü Dongbin, No-Mind (Wuxin), Clarity and Stillness (Qingjing), Qi (Energy), Dan (Elixir), Daoyin (Guiding Energy), Essence (Jing), Preparation</keywords>

# Sayings of the Daoist School

...reaching it. If your practice relies on a mind of intention and the work of "doing," then your techniques and methods will have an end. If you practice the principle of **No-mind** and **Non-action** <term>Wuwei: effortless action or "doing nothing" that is artificial</term>, then you reside in the limitless **Clear Void** <term>Qingxu: the state of primordial purity</term>.

***

**The Master said:**
"Non-action" means to be without obsessive thought or calculation. Even if you are caught between the accumulation of desires, anger, profit, and harm, you can be "acting" yet remain constantly in a state of "non-action." Although you are involved in worldly affairs, you can remain constantly free of affairs. How much more so if you can dedicate yourself to clarifying the heart and purifying the mind, nourishing the **Energy** <term>Qi</term> and making the Spirit whole, wandering in the land of "Carefree Ease" and entering the "Village of Nowhere" <note>references to the *Zhuangzi*, a foundational Daoist text</note>.

***

**The Master said:**
**Liu Gaoshang** <note>Liu the Noble, a hermit known for his extreme asceticism</note> lived in a tiny, walled enclosure for forty years with no other business. He simply emptied his heart and filled his belly. He discarded ostentation and forgot fame. He abandoned profit and purified his Spirit. Because he kept his Energy whole, the **Elixir** formed naturally and he became an immortal naturally. There is a verse of praise for him: "Block the openings, shut the doors." <note>A quote from the *Dao De Jing*, Chapter 52, referring to closing the senses to external distractions.</note> I used to recite these words in the past; today, I see them embodied in this man. His way can be called simple and appropriate.

***

**The Master said:**
"No-mind" does not mean being like a cat or a dog—dull and mindless. It means striving to keep the mind in the realm of Clarity and Stillness, free from deviant thoughts. The common person lacks a heart of Clarity and Stillness, while the person of the Way lacks a heart of "dust and grime" <note>metaphor for worldly attachments and delusions</note>. It is not as if both are "mindless" in the same way as stones, trees, cats, or dogs.

***

**The Master said:**
"When the view of birth and death no longer arises, one sees the **Tathagata** <note>original: 如來 (Rulai). A Buddhist term for the Buddha, used here by Daoists to mean one's true, unchanging nature</note>; when one is fully awakened, one avoids returning to the womb." 

**Qiu Changchun** <note>Qiu Chuji, the most famous disciple of Wang Chongyang and founder of the Dragon Gate branch</note> said: "This refers to the emergence of the **Yin Spirit** <term>Yinshen: a person's spirit that can leave the body but is still tied to the earthly realm</term>. If one reaches the Heavenly Court and suddenly sees 'double flowers' flying, only then does the **Yang Spirit** <term>Yangshen: the refined, 'immortal embryo' that can appear in the physical world</term> emerge. This is but the initial stage."

***

**The Master said:**
"The Great Way is far from human emotions,
Non-action is the wondrous root and foundation.
If the world contains nothing you love,
Afflictions will not follow you."

***

**The Master said:**
"If a practitioner's merit and deeds are not yet complete but their 'Great Limit' <note>a euphemism for death</note> arrives, the Sages and Worthies will not allow them to die. However, if one is not a practitioner of the Way, when the Great Limit arrives, there is no escaping it."

***

**The Master said:**
"If a single thought is not severed, a whole lifetime is wasted." 

**Qi Daosheng** asked: "What is it like when one is in a state of profound and constant silence?" 
The Master replied: "In the future, even that 'profound silence' will not be needed."

***

**Yu Qingfeng** asked: "I have practiced for many years, yet my **Dao-eye** <note>spiritual insight</note> is not bright and my heart-ground is not divinely inspired. Why is this?" 
The Master said: "There is no other reason; you are simply not refined in your practice of the Way."

***

**The Master said:**
"All men and women, from the beginningless past until now, have been unable to escape the world of **Samsara** <term>Lunhui: the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth</term> because of various kinds of affection, love, and greedy desires. Whether born from a womb, an egg, moisture, or by transformation <note>the four types of birth in ancient cosmology</note>, all types of natures and appearances are born because of love and desire. Nature and life are born from love; the physical body exists because of desire. Because of love and desire, people give rise to 'following' and 'resisting' <note>attraction and repulsion</note> and breed jealousy. From this, the cycle of reincarnation continues without end. The words of the Law say: 'Desire must be purified...'"

<summary>The Master defines Non-action and No-mind as active spiritual states rather than mere passivity, while discussing the advanced stages of spirit-cultivation with Qiu Chuji and warning that desire is the root of reincarnation.</summary>
