# Establishing Righteousness and Setting Punishments; Acting with Benevolence and Bestowing Virtue

The **Five Elements** circulate through the <term>Three Talents</term> <note>Heaven, Earth, and Humanity</note>. 
* In **Heaven**, they manifest as the Five Planets. 
* In **Earth**, they are distributed as the Five Directions. 
* In **Humanity**, they are endowed as the **Five Constants** <note>the core Confucian virtues</note>. 

Therefore, it is said that the spirit of **Wood** is Benevolence; **Metal** is Righteousness; **Fire** is Propriety; **Water** is Wisdom; and **Earth** is Trust. Consequently:
* **Spring** belongs to Wood and is Benevolence.
* **Autumn** belongs to Metal and is Righteousness.
* **Summer** belongs to Fire and is Propriety.
* **Winter** belongs to Water and is Wisdom.
* **Late Summer** <note>the transition period</note> belongs to Earth and is Trust.

This is how the Five Elements and Five Constants harmonize with the four seasons. 

Now, regarding **"establishing righteousness and setting punishments"**: "Establishing" means to build up. "Righteousness" means what is appropriate. This says that when one establishes righteousness, one must set punishments to distinguish what is appropriate, mirroring the strict, gathering energy of the **Autumn** season. 

Regarding **"acting with benevolence and bestowing virtue"**: "Acting" means to take responsibility for. "Benevolence" refers to the human quality of care. This says that when one takes up benevolence, one should bestow kindness and grace to nourish others, mirroring the life-giving energy of the **Spring** season. 

However, in this path of "Punishment and Virtue," if one follows the proper timing and measure, the four seasons will be in harmony and all affairs will be orderly. If one violates these regulations, the sequence of vital energy will become erratic and all matters will fail. Therefore, it is said: **"Those who oppose it meet with misfortune; those who follow it meet with good fortune."** 

As **Master Guan** <note>Guan Zhong, an ancient philosopher-statesman</note> said: "Punishment and Virtue are the union of the four seasons. When they harmonize with the time, blessings are born; when they depart from it, disasters arise." This is the meaning here. This section explains that the issuing of government and education must harmonize with the energetic sequence of the seasons.

# Even the Slightest Impropriety Leads to Failure; Regret and Humiliation Act as Thieves
<gloss>*Xian* <note>fiber</note> is pronounced *xian*. *Lin* <note>humiliation</note> is pronounced *lin*.</gloss> ◯ Note: **Following the laws of the calendar** and being **utterly sincere, concentrated, and secret** means that one must calculate and follow the measured degrees of the laws and the sequence of the government-like regulations. One must be extremely sincere without any falsehood, remaining focused, cautious, and discreet. 

Regarding **"carefully waiting for the day and hour; examining the waxing and waning"**: There are twelve <term>Earthly Branches</term> <note>the 12 two-hour periods</note> in a single day, and each branch contains eight <term>marks</term> <note>original: "ke," a unit of approximately 15 minutes on a water clock</note>. **"Waxing"** refers to the birth of Yang, occurring from the hour of the **Rat** <note>Zi, 11 PM – 1 AM</note> to the hour of the **Snake** <note>Si, 9 AM – 11 AM</note>. **"Waning"** refers to the birth of Yin, occurring from the hour of the **Horse** <note>Wu, 11 AM – 1 PM</note> to the hour of the **Pig** <note>Hai, 9 PM – 11 PM</note>. The numerical cycles of the years, seasons, and solar terms are governed by the days and hours, while the movement of the two breaths of Yin and Yang is driven by this "waxing and waning." Therefore, one must carefully wait for and examine them. 

Regarding **"even the slightest impropriety leads to failure; regret and humiliation act as thieves"**: "Slightest" refers to something as tiny as a fiber or a mustard seed. "Regret" means remorse; "humiliation" means shame; "thieves" means harm. This says that if there is even the smallest trace of not following the measured laws, or if one does not correct the timing of the days, then the "government regulations" of the work will produce regret and humiliation, and the sequence of the vital breath will suffer the disaster of harmful "thieves." This section follows the previous text to introduce the ideas that follow.

# The Two Solstices Change their Measure, Becoming Distorted and Crooked; Deep Winter Brings Great Heat, While Mid-Summer Brings Frost and Snow; The Two Equinoxes Cross Paths and Disregard the Water Clock; Wind and Rain Lose Their Rhythm; Flood and Drought Attack Each Other; Locusts Boil Up and Swarm; Various Wonders Appear Everywhere as Heaven Reveals Its Portents; Mountains Collapse and the Earth Splits
<gloss>*Xian* <note>appears</note> is pronounced *xian*.</gloss> ◯ The **Two Solstices** are the Winter and Summer solstices. This means that if the two solstices change or swap their roles in winter and summer, altering their constant measures, then the four seasons become distorted and the sequence of the vital breath becomes "crooked." Thus, it is said: "The two solstices change their measure, becoming distorted and crooked." 

When the two solstices are reversed and distorted, the freezing months of **Deep Winter** instead become periods of **Great Heat**, hot enough to melt metal and shrivel stone. The sweltering months of **Mid-Summer** conversely become periods of **Frost and Snow**, freezing and bitter. Thus, it is said: "Deep winter brings great heat, mid-summer brings frost and snow." 

The **Two Equinoxes** are the Spring and Autumn equinoxes. Regarding **"cross paths"**: North and South are called "vertical," while East and West are called "horizontal." The two solstices occur in the months of the Rat and Horse <note>the North-South axis</note>, which is the "vertical." The two equinoxes occur in the months of the Rabbit and Rooster <note>the East-West axis</note>, which is the "horizontal." This says that the equinoxes and solstices are turned upside down and swapped. Thus, it is said: "The two equinoxes cross paths." 

Regarding **"disregard the water clock"**: At the two equinoxes, the day and night marks on the <term>water clock</term> <note>clepsydra</note> should be equal, while at the two solstices, the day and night marks reach their maximum lengths and shortcuts. If the seasonal commands are now swapped and disordered, then the water clock timings for the equinoxes and solstices will no longer match their constant measures. 

Regarding **"wind and rain lose their rhythm; flood and drought attack each other"**: Because the equinoxes and solstices are swapped, Spring/Autumn and Winter/Summer are inverted, leading to a total disorder of the climate. Therefore, wind, rain, floods, and droughts do not follow their proper seasons, but instead overcome and "attack" one another, violating natural harmony. 

Regarding **"locusts boil up and swarm; various wonders appear everywhere"**: **Locusts** are insects that eat young sprouts. **Boil up** refers to water bubbling up from a spring. This means that when the solstices and equinoxes cross paths and change their measure, the locusts that harm crops will appear as thick as bubbling spring water, and the disasters of flood and drought will be seen everywhere. Thus, when the four "cardinal" points of the year are changed, summer becomes freezing and winter becomes scorching; wind and rain lose their rhythm, and droughts and floods follow one after another. Eventually, it reaches the point where mountain peaks collapse on their own and the earth splits without cause—the strange portents of Heaven and Earth appear in full. Thus, it is said: "Heaven reveals its portents..."

# Firmness and Softness are Determined; They Do Not Interfere with Each Other; The Five Elements Guard Their Boundaries; They Do Not Allow for Excess or Deficiency; The Changes Flow in a Cycle, Contracting and Expanding, Reversing and Returning

The word **"Determined"** <note>original: "duan," meaning decided or separated</note> is pronounced like *duan* in the departing tone. ◯ The *Book of Changes* <note>the *I Ching*</note> says: "Movement and stillness have constancy; **firmness and softness** are determined." Generally, Yang is movement and Yin is stillness; this is the constant law of Heaven and Earth. **Firmness** represents the Yang, and **softness** represents the Yin; these are the determinations of the hexagram lines. 

When it says "Firmness and softness are determined; they do not interfere with each other," it means that the spring and summer are Yang and firm—they should correspond to movement, growth, and expansion. The autumn and winter are Yin and soft—they should correspond to stillness and gathering-in. Just as cold, heat, warmth, and coolness each correspond to their specific season, the vital breaths of the four seasons' Yin and Yang are "determined" or distinguished. Thus, they do not interfere with one another in a chaotic or erroneous way. 

Regarding **"The Five Elements guard their boundaries,"** this means that spring belongs to Wood, summer to Fire, late summer to Earth, autumn to Metal, and winter to Water. These seasonal timings of the Five Elements' vital breath each keep to their own limits and do not trespass or encroach upon one another. 

**"They do not allow for excess or deficiency"** <note>original: "ying suo," literally filling and shrinking</note> means that the seasonal nodes and the vital breaths of the Five Elements must not be allowed to go too far or fail to reach their mark.

Naturally, no strange mutations or errors will occur. 

This section summarizes the preceding text regarding the "Superior Man’s" use of the heart/mind; his influence and effectiveness are such as this. <meta>Page 77 continues the astronomical observations of the moon's path, transitioning from the general alignment of the Sun and Moon to the specific positions where the lunar crescent first appears. It connects these observations to the hexagrams of the Book of Changes, specifically the Zhen trigram and the "Hidden Dragon" stage, to illustrate the very first stirring of internal Yang energy.</meta>

One must not abandon this search to look elsewhere. I have carefully observed the rising and setting positions of the moon, which differ slightly from those of the sun. Let us test this by speaking of the four "cardinal" months. 

In the **Zi month** <note>the month of the Winter Solstice</note>, the new moon of the 3rd or 4th day and the waning moon of the 27th or 28th day rise and set in the Southeast and Southwest. These positions gradually shift forward and backward. By the time of the **Full Moon** <note>original: "Wang"</note>, the moon rises and sets in the Northeast and Northwest; it is only then that the position of the "long-night moon" is finally fixed. 

In the **Wu month** <note>the month of the Summer Solstice</note>, the rising and setting of the new and waning moons occur in the Northeast and Northwest, also shifting gradually. By the time of the Full Moon, they rise and set in the Southeast and Southwest, and the position of the "short-night moon" is fixed. 

In the **Mao and You months** <note>the Spring and Autumn Equinoxes</note>, although the positions of the new, waning, and full moons still shift, they never truly leave the East and West. 

Generally, in the Zi month, the sun rises and sets in the Southeast and Southwest, while in the Wu month, it rises and sets in the Northeast and Northwest. Therefore, the **Lunar Body** <note>the moon</note> at its new and waning phases takes its starting point from the sun's position. If it were not so, then during the interval of the **Dark and New Moon**, the Sun and Moon could not "join their tallies" or "grasp the contract" <note>align perfectly</note>. Only in the Mao and You months do the Sun and Moon rise and set together in the East and West; thus, the moon’s shift is not very far. 

This movement of the moon differs from the movement of the sun, a fact that previous scholars have not yet discussed. Having now observed its rising and setting throughout the year, the image is exactly as described. 

Today, the phrase **"Starting in the Northeast"** refers to the "short-night moon" <note>the summer moon</note>. At the dawn of the New Moon, the moon follows the sun, traveling with it from the Northeast without any light of its own. As the heavens rotate to the left and the celestial bodies turn to the right, the moon gradually separates from the sun. By the evening of the 3rd day, it first "vomits" its light in the West. 

In the fourth chapter of the previous volume, the phrase **"Losing its brilliance in the Northeast"** refers to the evening of the transition to the Dark Moon, when the moon cannot be seen. By dawn, it is in the Northeast, and its light is seized by the sun, thus losing its brilliance entirely. Therefore, although both passages mention the Northeast and the short-night moon, the underlying principles are different and must be understood clearly.

This is the meaning. **"The divine tally wanes and breaks"** means that when a thing becomes too rigid or strong, it must break. Once the moon passes its fullness, it must wane. This is the sign <note>tally</note> that the spiritual light of Yang is beginning to retreat. **"Prosperity and decline gradually change"** means the moon has reached its peak and must now decline, gradually transforming its "Heavenly" body. **"Finally returning to the beginning"** says that once the moon's fullness is exhausted, its momentum inevitably leads to depletion, eventually returning to the darkness of the New Moon. This ebb and flow of Yin and Yang is the Natural Way <note>Tao</note>. Thus, Lord Wei <note>Wei Boyang, the author of the *Cantong qi*</note> deeply understood that fullness cannot be maintained forever.</gloss>

# The Xun Trigram Succeeds the Rule; Maintain Firmness and Control; At the Fourth Nine-Line, the Dragon Leaps; The Path of Advancing and Retreating is Precarious.

<gloss>**"The Xun trigram succeeds the rule"** refers to the sixteenth day of the month, when the moon's light first begins to wane. Its image is the **Xun trigram** <note>Wind / The Gentle</note>, which contains a single Yin line beneath two Yang lines; thus, Yin succeeds the lineage of Yang. **"Maintain firmness and control"** means that at this time, Yang is retreating and Yin is advancing—growth is turning into decay. One must firmly preserve the virtue of Yang while managing the rising Yin lineage. **"Nine in the Fourth Place: The dragon leaps"** refers to the fourth line of the Heaven Hexagram. 
> The Master said: "The dragon leaps in the abyss; advancing is without blame." 
> He also said: "Leaping in the abyss; the Way of Heaven is changing." 
**"The path of advancing and retreating is precarious"** because the number Nine represents Yang, but the fourth position is a Yin position. Thus, a Yang line resides in a Yin place. Because the choice to advance or retreat is not yet settled—characterized by "leaping" or hesitating—the path seems dangerous. If one can follow the timing of the heavens, there is no blame. This interprets the meaning of the fourth line text.</gloss>

# The Gen Trigram Governs Stopping and Advancing; One Must Not Exceed the Proper Time.

<gloss>On the twenty-third day, one holds the post <note>The moon reaches its Last Quarter</note>.</gloss>

<summary>This page maps the lunar cycle from the first quarter to the full moon and into the waning phase, correlating these stages with the specific line-readings of the Heaven Hexagram and the transition from the Qian (Heaven) to the Xun (Wind) trigrams.</summary>

## At the Stage of the Quarter Moon, Nine in the Fifth Place: The Flying Dragon is in the Heavenly Position, Adding Joy.

<gloss>The character for "exceed" <note>original: 逾, yu</note> is pronounced *yu*.</gloss> The **Gen trigram** <note>Mountain / Keeping Still</note> governs advancing and stopping. The phrase **"One must not exceed the proper time"** means that "advancing" is like walking or acting, while "exceeding" means going too far. When the moon reaches the twenty-third day, the **Last Quarter** <note>lower chord</note>, its light is half-depleted. Its image is the **Gen trigram**, which consists of two Yin lines below one Yang line. Since the essential meaning of Gen is "stopping," and since both acting and stopping have their proper moments, one must not miss the timing and violate the Natural Way <note>Tao</note>. The *Book of Changes* says: "Gen means stopping. When it is time to stop, then stop; when it is time to act, then act. When movement and rest do not miss their proper time, the Way is bright and shining." This is the meaning here. Regarding **"On the twenty-third day, one holds the post of the Quarter phase,"** the word "hold" <note>original: 典, dian</note> means to govern or preside over. It says that the twenty-third day governs the period of the waning half-moon. **"Nine in the Fifth Place: The flying dragon"** explains that within the **Qian Hexagram** <note>The Creative / Heaven</note>, this corresponds to the fifth line's text. 
> The Master <note>Confucius</note> said: "The dragon flies in the sky; it is advantageous to see the great man." 
> He also said: "The dragon flies in the sky; this is the position of Heavenly virtue." 
This is it. As for **"the Heavenly position adds joy,"** it means that when the Sage occupies the supreme "Heavenly" position of the fifth line, how could there not be added joy? This also interprets the meaning of that specific line.

## Six in the Fifth Place: The Kun Trigram Receives; Binding the End and the Beginning; Nurturing All Children, Serving Throughout the Ages as the Mother of All Species.

<gloss>The character for "nurturing" <note>original: 韞, yun</note> is pronounced *yun*.</gloss> **"Six in the Fifth Place: The Kun trigram receives"** refers to the thirtieth day of the month. When the moon reaches the thirtieth day, its light is entirely gone. Its image is the **Kun trigram** <note>The Receptive / Earth</note>, consisting of three Yin lines, which "receives" the cycle. **"Binding the end and the beginning"** means that the moon gradually produces light from the New Moon and gradually reaches darkness from the Full Moon. Furthermore, among the hexagrams of the six lunar phases, the cycle begins with **Xun** <note>Wind, on the 16th day</note> and ends with **Kun** <note>Earth, on the 30th day</note>. As the dark of the moon and the new moon meet, and Yin and Yang intersect, are they not "binding together" the end and the beginning? **"Nurturing all children, serving throughout the ages as the mother of all species"**: "Nurturing" means to contain or hide within. "All children" refers to the various hexagrams, and is also a metaphor for all created things. This says that the virtue of the Earth <note>Kun</note> is the ability to contain and nurture all things, acting as the mother to every species in the world. **"The top line: The dragon exceeds the limit"** <note>original: 亢龍, kang long</note> refers to the sixth line of the Heaven Hexagram. 
> The Master said: "The dragon exceeds the limit; there will be cause for regret. What is full cannot be maintained forever." 
> He also said: "The dragon exceeds the limit; it reaches the extreme along with the time." 
Regarding **"Virtue wars in the wilderness,"** when the moon reaches its darkest day, it is called "Pure Earth" <note>Kun</note>. In terms of the Heaven Hexagram, it is the top line. This is the moment where Yin and Yang both refuse to yield, and their momentum inevitably leads to conflict. Therefore, the text uses the meaning of the top line of the Earth Hexagram—"Dragons war in the wilderness"—to explain this transition.

## Using the Nine: Fluttering and Light, it Serves as the Way.

<gloss>The character "fluttering" <note>original: 翩, pian</note> is pronounced *pian*. "Completed" <note>original: 訖, qi</note> is pronounced *qi*. "Return" <note>original: 復, fu</note> is pronounced *fu*.</gloss> Generally, in the lines of a hexagram, **"Nine"** is used to represent the Yang (solid) lines, and **"Six"** is used to represent the Yin (broken) lines. Here, **"Using the Nine"** follows the discussion of the Heaven Hexagram. **"Fluttering and light"** describes a state of coming and going. It means that "Using the Nine" allows one to move back and forth through the six positions of the hexagram <note>the six voids</note>. It is firm yet capable of being yielding; this is the standard and the law of the Way of Change. Thus it is said: "Using the Nine, fluttering and light, serves as the standard for the Way."

## The Compass and Square: The Yang Numbers are Completed; Once Completed, They Rise Again, Pushing Emotion to Join with Nature, Turning and Connecting with One Another.

<summary>This page concludes the lunar-hexagram correlation, mapping the Last Quarter moon to the Gen (Mountain) trigram and the Dark Moon to the Kun (Earth) trigram. it explains the "war" between Yin and Yang at the cycle's end and the flexible nature of "Nine" (Yang) as the cycle prepares to restart.</summary>

<meta>Page 80 continues the exploration of the "Using the Nine" phase, transitioning from the mathematical completion of the Yang cycle (the number nine) to the philosophical and alchemical implications of the cycle's restart. It concludes Chapter 3 by linking cosmic rotation to the human internal state of nature and emotion.</meta>

This is it. The Master <note>Confucius</note> said: **"In Using the Nine, the virtue of Heaven cannot be the head."** He also said: **"The Primal Beginning of Heaven Uses the Nine; thus one sees the Laws of Heaven."** These quotes illustrate the point. **Yang numbers** consist of the sequence one, three, five, seven, and nine. As for **"being completed,"** the Yang numbers begin from one and reach their completion at nine. "Completed" <note>original: 訖, qi</note> means to reach the end or to be exhausted. However, because **Nine is "Old Yang"** <note>a state of energy so mature it must transform</note>, and since the rule is that "Old" lines change while "Young" lines remain stable, once the nine is exhausted, it returns to begin again at one. It is like a ring with no end. Therefore, it says: **"The Yang numbers are completed; once completed, they rise again."** 

Regarding **"Emotion and Nature"** <note>original: 情性, qing xing</note>: When the mind is utterly still and unmoved, in the state of "The Middle" before any feelings have arisen, that is called **Nature**. Thus, Nature is the stillness of Emotion. When the mind is affected by something and responds, in the state of "Harmony" after feelings have arisen, that is called **Emotion**. Thus, Emotion is the movement of Nature. Because Nature and Emotion serve as "Substance and Function" <note>the inner reality and its outward expression</note> for each other, the **Five Constants** <note>the virtues of benevolence, righteousness, ritual, wisdom, and trust</note> are born within the body, and "all things are complete within me." Because a human's Nature and Emotion can achieve their proper balance, we are distinguished from the "one-sidedness" of other animals and objects. Now, the pushing and joining of the firm and yielding lines in their positions, and the turning and interaction of Yin and Yang to form the images of the hexagrams, are exactly the same principle as the stillness and movement of human Nature and Emotion serving as the "Substance and Function" of the body and mind. Therefore it is said: **"Pushing emotion to join with nature, turning and connecting with one another."** 

Furthermore, the **Circulation of the Fire** <note>a technique for directing energy</note> in alchemical methods is exactly like this. When the Spirit governs the Breath, and Nature is joined with Emotion, the Spirit acts as the Nature and the Breath acts as the Emotion. Thus, all the metaphorical names found in alchemical scriptures can be understood through this same kind of comparison.

## The Circulating Armillary Sphere Rises and Falls, Moving Up and Down; It Flows Throughout the Six Lines and Is Difficult to Observe; Thus It Has No Constant Position, Serving as the Ancestral Source of Change.

<gloss>The characters for "Armillary Sphere" <note>original: 璿璣, xuanji</note> are pronounced *xuan-ji*. ○ "Circulating" <note>original: 循, xun</note>: The *Collected Commentaries on the Book of Documents* says: "A beautiful pearl is called *xuan*. A *ji* is a machine or mechanism." An instrument decorated with pearls to track the stars is an armillary sphere, used to represent the rotation of the heavenly bodies. Here, it refers to the transformations of "Using the Nine" in the Heaven Hexagram. Because these transformations follow the laws and measures of the Armillary Sphere, they rotate infinitely. Thus, as the lines "rise and fall" through the upper and lower trigrams of the hexagram, their changes never settle in one place. As they "flow throughout" the six empty positions of the lines, the firm and the yielding exchange places with one another. Consequently, it is difficult to perceive where they begin or end; they have no fixed, permanent position. This makes them the "Ancestral Source" of all the transformations in the imagery of the *Book of Changes*. The transformations of "Using the Six" <note>the Yin lines</note> in the Earth Hexagram follow this same Way.</gloss>

# At the dawn of the New Moon, the Return Hexagram appears. The Yang energy begins to penetrate. Its coming and going are without haste. Setting the gnomon, it is slightly firm. The Yellow Bell pipe is established in the month of the Rat. The light thus increases and manifests. Spreading...

<gloss>The character for **Return** <note>original: 復, Fu</note> is pronounced *fu*. The character for **Spreading** <note>original: 施, shi</note> is in the departing tone. ○ In one year, there are twelve months. The twelve hexagrams are distributed among them, starting from the **Return Hexagram** in the eleventh month and ending with the **Pure Yin Hexagram** <note>Kun</note> in the tenth month of the following year. This forms the creative process of the waning and waxing of Yin and Yang throughout a year. If one applies these twelve hexagrams to a single month, then one hexagram represents two and a half days. Starting from the first day of the month and ending on the last, the cycle of twelve hexagrams is completed. Therefore, the first day of the month is assigned to the Return Hexagram; this is when the first Yang line is born, and its energy begins to penetrate. The phrase **"coming and going without haste"** <note>original: 出入無疾, churu wu ji</note> is taken from the "Decision" <note>Tuanzhuan</note> of the Return Hexagram in the *I Ching*. Master Wei <note>Wei Boyang, the author of this text</note> cites it here to mean that at this time, the advancement and retreat of Yin and Yang are both subtle, and the movement of energy should naturally be steady and not hurried. The **gnomon** <note>original: 表, biao</note> is a tool used to measure shadows and determine the seasons. This means that when observing the season with the gnomon, the Yang energy is found to be "slightly firm" <note>just beginning to take strength</note>. The **Yellow Bell** <note>original: 黃鐘, Huangzhong</note> is the pitch-pipe for the eleventh month; it is the month of the **Rat** <note>Zi, the first of the twelve earthly branches</note>, used to observe the arrival of the energy. The phrase **"the light thus increases and manifests"** means that the first signs of Yang energy are beginning to grow and become visible.</gloss>

# ...Spreading soft warmth. The common people obtain their constancy.

<gloss>**Soft warmth** refers to the subtle, early Yang energy. The **common people** <note>original: 黎蒸, lizheng</note> refers to the masses. This means that as the subtle Yang energy is spread and distributed, the people will experience the regular, harmonious weather of the season.</gloss>

# Approaching the furnace and extending the branches; the path is opened for the correct light. The radiance gradually advances, and the daylight grows longer. In the month of the Ox, the Greater Lute pipe is played; the ending and beginning are balanced.

<gloss>**Approach** <note>original: 臨, Lin</note> is the hexagram for the twelfth month. The **furnace** <note>original: 爐, lu</note> symbolizes the Yang energy. **Extending** <note>original: 條, tiao</note> means to grow long. This means that moving from the Return Hexagram to the Approach Hexagram, the Yang energy spreads and grows. The "Way of Yang" is opening up, the radiance is advancing step-by-step, and the sun's shadow indicates the days are becoming longer. This month is the seasonal marker of the **Ox** <note>Chou</note>, and its corresponding musical pitch-pipe is the **Greater Lute** <note>original: 大呂, Dalu</note>. However, because the Ox month marks the end of the year, and an end must lead to a new beginning, the twelfth month sits exactly in the balance between the "falling" of the old and the "rising" of the new.</gloss>

# Rising up to form Peace. Firm and yielding are both prosperous. Yin and Yang intersect; the "small departs and the great arrives." Converging like spokes in the month of the Tiger, connecting to follow the season.

<gloss>○ **Rising up** <note>original: 仰, yang</note> means that from the Approach Hexagram of the twelfth month, one looks upward and adds another Yang line to form the **Peace Hexagram** <note>original: 泰, Tai</note>, which is the hexagram for the first lunar month. The structure of the Peace Hexagram consists of **Heaven** <note>Qian</note> on the inside and **Earth** <note>Kun</note> on the outside; thus, the firm and yielding are equal in measure, and both are at their peak of prosperity. Regarding **"Yin and Yang intersect; the small departs and the great arrives"**: the "small" refers to Yin, and the "great" refers to Yang. This describes Peace as a hexagram where Yin and Yang meet, and it also symbolizes the retreat of Yin and the growth of Yang. The *I Ching* says: "In Peace, the small departs and the great arrives; this is lucky and pervasive." This is because Heaven and Earth intersect, and all things communicate. **Spokes** <note>original: 輻, fu</note> are the rods in the center of a wheel; **converging** <note>original: 輳, cou</note> means to meet at a point. This also references the pitch-pipe of the first month, called the **Great Cluster** <note>original: 太蔟, Taicu - a pun on the word for converging</note>. It means that when the Yang energy reaches the month of the **Tiger** <note>Yin</note>, it is like spokes converging at the hub of a wheel, beginning its motion.</gloss>

## Gradually passing through the Great Invigorator, standing aligned with the Gate of the Rabbit. The elm seeds fall, returning to their roots. Punishment and Virtue rely on one another; day and night are equal at this time.

<gloss>The character for **Aligned** <note>original: 俠, xia</note> is pronounced *jia*. The character for **Seeds** <note>original: 莢, jia</note> is pronounced *jie*. ○ "Gradually passing through the Great Invigorator" <note>original: 大壯, Dazhuang</note> means that from the previous hexagrams of Return, Approach, and Peace, we now arrive at the **Great Invigorator Hexagram**, which represents the second lunar month. **Aligned** means to be side-by-side; it is also a loan-word for the name of the musical pitch-pipe of the second month, the **Pressed Bell** <note>original: 夾鐘, Jiazhong</note>. In the middle of the second month, Yin exists within Yang; thus, Life and Death <note>Virtue and Punishment</note> overlap. This is why some things die while others are born. The second month contains the **Spring Equinox** <note>original: 春分, Chunfen</note>, the time when day and night are divided equally. The *Book of Rites* says: "In the second month of spring, day and night are equal."</gloss>

## In Breakthrough, Yin retreats as Yang ascends forward. Washing the feathers and wings, shaking off the old dust.

<gloss>The character for **Breakthrough** <note>original: 夬, Guai</note> is pronounced *guai*. The character for **Washing** <note>original: 洗, xi</note> is pronounced *xuan*. The character for **Shaking** <note>original: 索, suo</note> is pronounced *se*. ○ **Breakthrough** is the hexagram for the third lunar month. This hexagram consists of five Yang lines and one Yin line at the very top. This signifies that Yin is about to be completely pushed out, and Yang is ascending to its fullness. **Washing** and **Rinsing** describe the action of cleansing. **Old Purified** <note>original: 姑洗, Guxi</note> is the name of the pitch-pipe for the third month. **Shaking** and **Searching** mean to tidy and clear away. This describes the rising Yang energy as being like a bird washing its feathers and shaking off the dust of winter, preparing to soar into the high sky. These two lines are also used to explain the hidden meaning of the "Old Purified" pitch-pipe.</gloss>

## The Creative is strong and brilliantly clear, widely covering the four neighbors. Yang reaches its conclusion in the month of the Snake, and at its peak, it is confronted.

<gloss>**The Creative** <note>original: 乾, Qian</note> is the hexagram for the fourth lunar month. The **four neighbors** refer to the four directions. The nature of the "Creative" body is firm and strong, and its power is bright and vast. As the *I Ching* says: "Great is the vastness of the Creative! All things owe their beginning to it; it governs all of heaven... the clouds move and the rain falls, and all things flow into their forms." This is the meaning here. **Yang reaches its conclusion in the month of the Snake** <note>original: 已, Si</note> refers to how the Yang energy, which began in the month of the Rat <note>11th month</note>, reaches its ultimate peak in the month of the Snake. **Peak** <note>original: 中, zhong - literally 'middle'</note> refers to Yang energy reaching its absolute center or maximum. **Confronted** <note>original: 干, gan</note> means to be interfered with. The *I Ching* says: "When the sun reaches the center, it begins to set; when the moon is full, it begins to wane." Once something reaches its peak, it must begin to decline. Since the month of the Snake is the peak of Yang, and the Creative hexagram is Pure Yang, the energy is so full that Yin is about to emerge and "confront" or interfere with it. Furthermore, the word **Peak** <note>middle</note> is used as a pun for the pitch-pipe of the fourth month, the **Middle Lute** <note>original: 仲呂, Zhonglü</note>, as noted in the *Book of Rites*.</gloss>

...is pronounced *shui*. ○ **Coming to Meet** <note>original: 姤, Gou</note> is the hexagram for the fifth lunar month. **Record** <note>original: 紀, ji</note> means to note down. This says that "Coming to Meet" begins the recorded sequence of the energy of the "birth of the single Yin." **First** <note>original: 先, xian</note> means a portent or early sign. This suggests that although "Coming to Meet" is a hexagram where only one Yin line has just been born, its momentum will inevitably lead to a state of "Pure Yin" before it stops. Therefore, is this "Coming to Meet" not the early portent of **treading on hoarfrost**? The *I Ching* says: "When you tread on hoarfrost, solid ice is not far off." This means that as Yin begins to condense and follows its natural path, it will eventually reach the state of solid ice. This is exactly the meaning here. The image of "Coming to Meet" in the fifth month consists of five Yang lines on top and one Yin line at the bottom. During the fifth month of the Luxuriant Guest, the single Yin line is subtle and hidden below, while the five Yang lines are still vigorous and active above. However, that which is vigorous is about to retreat and end, becoming a "guest," while that which is subtle has already arisen and begun to act as the "host." This is also an explanation of the meaning of the "Luxuriant Guest" pitch-pipe.

## Retreating from the world and leaving one’s position to gather the essence; harboring virtue and awaiting the right time, resting in the dim darkness.

<gloss>**Retreat** <note>original: 遯, Dun</note> is the hexagram for the sixth lunar month. The pitch-pipe of the sixth month is called the **Forest Bell** <note>original: 林鐘, Linzhong</note>. "Retreat" represents the two Yin lines gradually growing. Yang should now retreat and avoid them, much like a **gentleman retreating from the world** and leaving his official position. The *I Ching* says: "Things cannot remain forever in their place; therefore, 'Retreat' follows." To retreat means to withdraw. **Essence** refers to the vital bloom. This means that at this time, all things are about to gather their vital essence into their seeds and kernels. **Virtue** refers to the "Yang-Virtue" <note>the life-force</note>. **Resting** <note>original: 棲遲, qichi</note> means to stop and take a break. **Dim darkness** refers to the hidden or obscure. This means one should harbor and hide the bright virtue of Yang, awaiting the proper time to use it again, while currently resting in a hidden place. The *I Ching* says: "Things cannot remain in retreat forever." This is the meaning. This section reveals the timely significance of the "Retreat" hexagram.</gloss>

## Blocked and obstructed, no passage is found; those things about to sprout do not grow. Yin stretches as Yang bends, and the name of Yang is submerged.

<gloss>The character for **Obstruction** <note>original: 否, Pi</note> is pronounced *pi*. For **Submerged Yang**, one version of the text reads "destroyed and injured." ○ **Obstruction** is the hexagram for the seventh lunar month. The pitch-pipe for the seventh month is called the **Equalizing Rule** <note>original: 夷則, Yize</note>. "Obstruction" is an image of being closed off and without passage. The *I Ching* says: "The great departs and the small arrives," which means Heaven and Earth do not commune, and thus the myriad things do not find passage. **Sprouting** refers to the buds of plants. This means that when the time reaches "Obstruction," the buds and sprouts of plants and trees will not grow. **Yin stretches and Yang bends** means that although "Obstruction" is a hexagram where Yin and Yang are equal <note>three lines each</note>, the Yin energy is the "advancing energy" and thus stretches forward, while the Yang energy is the "retreating energy" and thus bends or contracts. This is what the *I Ching* means by "that which departs is bent, and that which comes is stretched." As for **the name of Yang is submerged**, this means that as the Yin energy is currently flourishing, the nature and character of "Yang-Virtue" are gathered and hidden, much like a person’s name being buried or forgotten. The *I Ching* says: "The way of the small man grows; the way of the gentleman fades." It also says: "Heaven and Earth do not commune: Obstruction. The gentleman uses his frugal virtue to avoid hardship." This is the meaning.</gloss>

## Observe the weights and measures, and examine the mood of mid-autumn. Entrust the care of the tiny and young; while the old wither, they shall flourish again. Aligned with the wheat sprouts, they emerge because they are covered.

<gloss>The character for **Observe** <note>original: 觀, Guan</note> is pronounced *guan*. The character for **Sprouts** <note>original: 蘗, nie</note> is pronounced *nie*. ○ **Contemplation** <note>original: 觀, Guan</note> is the hexagram for the eighth lunar month. The pitch-pipe for the eighth month is called the **Southern Lute** <note>original: 南呂, Nanlü</note>.</gloss>

<summary>This page describes the transition from the height of summer into autumn, focusing on the hexagrams of Coming to Meet, Retreat, and Obstruction. It explains how Yang energy begins to withdraw and hide while Yin energy becomes the "host" of the natural cycle.</summary>

**Weights** <note>original: 權, quan</note> refers to the counterweight of a scale. **Measures** <note>original: 量, liang</note> refers to dry-measure vessels like the peck or bushel. The *Monthly Ordinances* <note>a classic ritual calendar</note> states that in the **mid-autumn month** <note>the 8th lunar month</note>, the days and nights are of equal length. Therefore, one should standardize the measures of capacity and weight, and level the scales. This is because in the eighth month, Yin and Yang are perfectly balanced. One should follow the seasonal timing to calibrate and fix these instruments of measurement. Thus, this passage says that by displaying these weights and measures, one can observe and understand the "mood" or character of mid-autumn. **Entrust** <note>original: 任, ren</note> means to be capable of sustaining. **Care** <note>original: 蓄, xu</note> means to nurture. This says that mid-autumn is a time of peace between Yin and Yang, capable of nurturing tiny, delicate things. Even those things that are **old and withered** shall once again find the strength to flourish. The **shepherd’s purse** <note>original: 薺, qi</note> is a sweet herb. The *Huainanzi* says: "When the water of the shepherd’s purse flourishes, it is born of winter water and dies in summer earth." This is what is meant here. **Sprouts** <note>original: 蘗, nie</note> refers to new shoots growing from the side of an old root. This means that under the mid-autumn decree, the delicate wheat begins to sprout, and the old, withered shepherd’s purse puts forth new shoots; both emerge from the ground at this time. Because the eighth month is the midpoint where Yin and Yang are equal, there is "life within the killing frost" and "virtue within the punishment" <note>in traditional thought, autumn is the season of "punishment" or contraction, yet it holds the seeds of new life</note>.

## The transforming energy is already exhausted and the supreme spirit is lost; the limbs and body rot away and the physical form is annihilated.

<gloss>**Peeling Away** <note>original: 剝, Bo</note> is the hexagram for the ninth lunar month. The pitch-pipe of the ninth month is called the **Invisible Echo** <note>original: 無射, Wuyi</note>. The *I Ching* says: "Peeling means rotting." It also speaks of the "bed being peeled away at its legs" and "at its skin." Generally, "Peeling Away" represents a state where Yin is flourishing and Yang is declining; it is a time when the **small man** is strong and the **gentleman** is ailing. Now, to say the **limbs and body rot away and the form is annihilated** is because "Peeling Away" is the hexagram of late autumn. When things reach this point, they all rot and fall away. Once the limbs rot, the physical form is destroyed. The *Musical Records of the Jin Dynasty* says: "The station of the ninth month is called *Xu* <note>the Dog</note>. *Xu* means extinction." This refers to the time when all things wither and perish. This is the meaning. **Transforming energy is exhausted** means that at this time, the life-giving energy of Heaven and Earth is about to come to a complete end. **The supreme spirit is lost** refers to the image of "Peeling Away" having five Yin lines flourishing and only one Yang line remaining at the very top. This suggests that the ultimate, primordial spirit is on the verge of disappearing.</gloss>

## Constantly follow the principles of the Earth to receive and spread Heaven’s decree; when the Way reaches its limit, it reverses and returns to the Earth Principle.

<gloss>**When the Way reaches its limit, it reverses** means that as the twelve hexagrams are distributed across the twelve months, the cycle goes from **Return** <note>original: 復, Fu</note> to **Heaven** <note>original: 乾, Qian</note>, at which point Yang is exhausted. From "Heaven" it transforms into **Coming to Meet** <note>original: 姤, Gou</note>, and Yin begins to circulate. From "Coming to Meet" it moves to **Earth** <note>original: 坤, Kun</note>, at which point Yin is exhausted. From "Earth" it changes back into "Return," and Yang circulates again. Therefore, the "Way" involves treading through these transitions; the cycle of exhaustion and passage repeats without end. The *I Ching* says: "Repeatedly following the Way." It also says: "When a path is exhausted, it changes; through change, it finds passage; through passage, it lasts long." **Returning to the Earth Principle** <note>original: 坤元, Kunyuan</note> means that when the path of Yin is exhausted, it returns to the "Primordial Earth," which is the hexagram for the tenth lunar month. The pitch-pipe for the tenth month is called the **Responsive Bell** <note>original: 應鍾, Yingzhong</note>. **Constantly follow the principles of the Earth to receive and spread Heaven’s decree** refers to how Earth <note>Kun</note> follows the Way of the Earth, which is to be soft, yielding, and enduring. The virtue of Earth is to receive the influence of Heaven and spread its decree. The *I Ching* says: "Great indeed is the Primordial Earth! The myriad things owe their birth to it, as it obediently receives the influence of Heaven." In the **Alchemical Way** <note>original: 丹道, dandao</note> of managing the "Internal Fire," the process of **advancing the Yang-fire** begins at "Return" <note>the 11th month</note> and reaches its peak at "Heaven" <note>the 4th month</note>. The process of **withdrawing the Yin-tally** begins at "Coming to Meet" <note>the 5th month</note> and ends at "Earth" <note>the 10th month</note>. It goes around and begins again, like a ring without an end. This is what Chapter 15 of the first volume means by: "The twelve segments revolve in a circle; when the segments end, one must begin again." However, regarding these eleven hexagrams, while they represent the months of the year, if they are concentrated into a single...</gloss>

## The profound mystery is distant and hazy, yet the obstacles are interconnected; responding to the cycles to nourish the seeds, the origin of Yin and Yang is vast and indistinct, with no known beginning.

<gloss>**Obstacle** <note>original: 閡, he</note> is the same as a barrier. **Vast** <note>original: 廓, kuo</note> is pronounced *kuo*. ○ **The profound mystery is distant and hazy, yet the obstacles are interconnected** means that the Way of Heaven is supremely profound and infinite, and the Way of Earth is distant and boundless. Though their upper and lower physical forms appear to have barriers between them, the movement of their spiritual energy is interconnected without any gap. When the Yang energy rises, it becomes Spring and Summer, and things grow. When the Yin energy descends, it becomes Autumn and Winter, and things are stored away. How could there ever be a distant barrier? **Responding to the cycles to nourish the seeds** means that although Heaven and Earth are vast, the back-and-forth movement of the One Qi <note>the primordial breath/energy</note> responds to the specific timing and degrees of the calendar to transform and nourish every species of life. **The origin of Yin and Yang** means that Yang energy is the start of the **Heavenly Origin** <note>original: 乾元, Qianyuan</note> and Yin energy is the birth of the **Earthly Origin** <note>original: 坤元, Kunyuan</note>. **Vast and indistinct, with no known beginning**: "Vast" refers to the great emptiness. "Indistinct" <note>original: 恍惚, huanghu</note> is like a state of blurred confusion. This says that the height and breadth of Heaven and Earth are so empty and vast that they are difficult to observe. The coming and going of Yin and Yang are so blurred that they are hard to see. Therefore, one cannot know their starting point. This section summarizes the text above to expand on the essential meaning of the twelve-month cycle of transformation.</gloss>

## At first lost and off the tracks, later becoming the sovereign lord; there is no level ground without a slope, for such is the Way of Nature. Transformations flourish in turn, as waxing and waning depend on each other; ending with the Receptive and beginning with Return, like a rotating cycle, the Emperors govern and it endures for a thousand years.

<gloss>**Slope** <note>original: 陂, bei</note> is pronounced *bi*. ○ The *I Ching* says: "The gentleman has a destination. If he leads, he is lost; if he follows, he finds his path." Generally, in the actions of a gentleman, there is difficulty at first and achievement later; thus, he is "lost" at first and "finds his way" by following. Now, the phrase **at first lost and off the tracks, later becoming the sovereign lord** draws on this meaning from the *I Ching* to explain how Yin and Yang take turns acting as "guest" and "host." **Tracks** <note>original: 軌, gui</note> refers to the ruts left by a carriage. For example, in the tenth month, which is the **Receptive** <note>original: 坤, Kun; pure Yin</note>, the Yang energy is almost extinguished—this is "losing the path." When we reach the eleventh month, **Return** <note>original: 復, Fu</note>, a single line of Yang is first born; therefore, the "latecomer" becomes the lord. Similarly, in the fourth month, which is the **Creative** <note>original: 乾, Qian; pure Yang</note>, the Yin energy is nearly exhausted—this is "losing the tracks." When we reach the fifth month, **Coming to Meet** <note>original: 姤, Gou</note>, a single line of Yin begins to grow; therefore, the "latecomer" becomes the master. The retreat and advance of the firm and the yielding follow this same principle. **There is no level ground without a slope, for such is the Way of Nature**: "Slope" means a tilt or slant. This means the movement of Yin and Yang depends on them leaning on or hiding within one another. There is no state of permanent "levelness" that does not eventually tilt, and nothing that constantly goes away without returning. This is the natural Way of Heaven and Earth, not something created by humans...</gloss>

# Chapter Four Concluded

This chapter uses the twelve Sovereign Hexagrams as proof of the waxing and waning of Yin and Yang. Although Heaven and Earth are supremely vast, the coming and going of their energy and the alternation of fullness and emptiness—which nourish all living things throughout the seasons—possess a subtle wonder that occurs naturally. Therefore, an Emperor can use this Way to establish a legacy of a thousand years, and a practitioner of "Nourishing Life" <note>Chinese health and longevity practices</note> should understand this principle to guide the **Fire Phasing** <note>original: 火符, huofu; the rhythmic timing of internal alchemy</note>. Truly, cultivating the self and governing a nation follow the exact same principle.

<margin>
**Nature and Life** <note>original: 性命, xingming</note>: There is the "nature" endowed by Heaven and the "nature" of one's physical temperament; there is the "life" allotted by fate and the "life" of the physical body. A student of the Way should nourish their heavenly nature and find peace in their allotted fate, while overcoming their temperamental nature and cultivating their physical body. Thus, "Nature and Life" are the ultimate treasures of our bodies and the pivot of cultivating the Way. 

In terms of the **Alchemical Way** <note>original: 丹道, dandao</note>, Nature is **Spirit** <note>original: 神, shen</note> and Life is **Vital Energy** <note>original: 氣, qi</note>. There is a distinction between the "Pre-Heaven" <note>innate/primordial</note> and "Post-Heaven" <note>acquired/physical</note> states. Students must refine and nourish the Post-Heaven to restore the Pre-Heaven; then the **Restored Elixir** <note>original: 還丹, huandan</note> can be completed and long life attained. As the *Song of the Great Way of the Spiritual Source* says: "Spirit is Nature, and Energy is Life; when Spirit does not wander outward, Energy naturally stabilizes." This is the meaning. It also says: "Internal movement of the **Primordial Harmony** <note>original: 元和, yuanhe</note> achieves the Truth; external breath-work alone never reaches the end." This also refers to the path of Pre-Heaven and Post-Heaven. Therefore, to nourish nature and extend life to forestall the time of death, one must reflect on achieving longevity later by prioritizing the planning of cultivation first. This section starts with the two words "Nature and Life" to introduce the meaning of the following text.

# 1. From the nothingness, the Original Essence spreads like clouds; relying on the Vital Energy, it finds its first home. Yin and Yang serve as the measure, and the souls take up their residence.
<note>The way of cultivating the **Internal Elixir** <note>original: 丹, dan</note> and the source of the physical body's birth follow the exact same principle. This means that for the body we are endowed with, before our parents gave us life, the physical form was originally nothing at all. At the moment the body is born, the **Pre-Heaven Original Essence** <note>original: 元精, yuanjing; the primordial spark of life</note> spreads out like drifting clouds. Relying on the interaction of the two energies <note>Yin and Yang</note> to establish its beginning, Yin and Yang then unite to form the standard of the body, and the **Ethereal and Corporeal Souls** <note>original: 魂魄, hun-po</note> each find their place to dwell within. Then, the physical matter is complete, and **Nature and Life** <note>Spirit and Vitality</note> are made whole. The principle of refining the Elixir is just like this. However, that which uses matter to produce matter results in humans and animals; that which uses the "formless" to produce "form" results in the Elixir and Immortality. **The Perfected Man Lü** <note>original: 呂眞人, Lü Zhenren; the immortal Lü Dongbin</note> said: "Exhaustively seek the beginning of how the body receives energy; do not wonder why the celestial secrets are fully revealed." ## The Yang Spirit is the Ethereal Soul of the Sun; the Yin Spirit is the Corporeal Soul of the Moon. The Ethereal and Corporeal Souls serve as each other’s dwelling.
<note>Heaven is Yang and Earth is Yin. The Sun is the essence of Yang, and the Moon is the essence of Yin. The **Ethereal Soul** <note>original: 魂, hun</note> is the spirit of Yang, while the **Corporeal Soul** <note>original: 魄, po</note> is the spirit of Yin. This matches what is said in **The Master of Huainan** <note>original: 淮南子, Huainanzi</note>: "The energy of Heaven becomes the Ethereal Soul, and the energy of Earth becomes the Corporeal Soul." Therefore, the Sun is treated as the Ethereal Soul of the Yang Spirit, and the Moon as the Corporeal Soul of the Yin Spirit. These two souls represent the substance and function of Yin and Yang. Without the Corporeal Soul, the Ethereal Soul has no way to move or transform; without the Ethereal Soul, the Corporeal Soul lacks spiritual brilliance. Thus, they "serve as each other's dwelling," and Yin and Yang act as each other's substance and function. This creates the imagery of the **Water and Fire** hexagrams <note>original: 坎離, Kan and Li</note> to complete the process of creation. In the Alchemical Way, the Ethereal Soul of the Sun belongs to the element of Wood; it resides in the East and governs rising. The Corporeal Soul of the Moon belongs to the element of Metal; it resides in the West and governs falling. When rising reaches its limit, it falls; when falling reaches its limit, it rises. This endless circulation of the souls joins the Spirit and Energy together to congeal the "seed" of the Elixir. **The Yellow Court Classic** <note>original: 黃庭經, Huangting jing</note> says: "The Ethereal Soul wishes to rise to Heaven, the Corporeal Soul enters the springs; returning the souls to one another is the natural Way." This is the meaning. An ancient song also says: "If anyone recognizes the Ethereal Soul of the Sun and the Corporeal Soul of the Moon, they are a true Immortal." This refers to the formless Sun and Moon within our own bodies, not the visible souls in the sky; this is why so few recognize them.</note>

# At this time, Emotion joins with Heaven and Earth; Heaven moves and acts directly, spreading Energy and flowing Essence; Earth is still and receptive, serving as a lodge for the Way.

<gloss>The phrase "At this time" continues the explanation from the previous text. "Emotion joins with Heaven and Earth" means that the human disposition and nature align with the virtues of the **Qian** <note>Heaven/Creative</note> and **Kun** <note>Earth/Receptive</note> hexagrams. "Heaven moves and acts directly" means the nature of the Heavenly Yang is characterized by movement; it proceeds straight ahead without bending or wavering. **The Book of Changes** <note>original: 易經, Yijing</note> says: "As for the Creative (Qian), in its stillness it is focused, and in its motion it is direct; thus the Great Beginning is born." This is the meaning. "Spreading Energy and flowing Essence" refers to the virtue of Heaven, which governs dispersal and bestowing. Therefore, its Energy is like the spreading of clouds, and its Essence is like the flowing of rain. As the *Book of Changes* says: "The clouds move and the rain is bestowed; all things flow into their forms." "Earth is still and receptive" means the nature of the Earthly Yin is characterized by stillness; it gathers and closes rather than scattering. The *Book of Changes* says: "As for the Receptive (Kun), in its stillness it is closed, and in its motion it opens; thus the Vast Birth is produced." "Serving as a lodge for the Way" uses the metaphors of a "lodge" <note>a town house</note> and a "hut" <note>a country shelter</note>. This means the virtue of Earth is to contain and receive; its path is like a dwelling where people and objects can be stored and protected. The *Book of Changes* says: "The Earth is thick and carries all things; its virtue aligns with the boundless." In the Way of the Elixir, using the "Heavenly" principle means moving healthily without ceasing; thus, Energy spreads in a complete cycle and transforms into the "Water of Essence," flowing to nourish the **Cinnabar Field** <note>original: 丹田, dantian; the energy center in the lower abdomen</note>. Using the "Earthly" principle means carrying things with depth and magnanimity; thus, Spirit congeals and Energy gathers, acting as a lodge to nurture the spiritual embryo. However, one must understand that "Essence" in alchemical practice is a substance of ultimate purity and clarity; it is not the physical fluid stimulated by lust or desire. Do not misunderstand this, lest you commit a grave error.</gloss>

# The Hard bestows and then retreats; the Soft transforms to nourish. Nine returns, Seven reverts, Eight comes home, and Six stays.

<gloss>The "Hard" refers to **Qian** <note>Heaven</note> or Yang. It means the energy of Heavenly Yang spreads upon the Earth and then retreats back to Heaven. The "Soft" refers to **Kun** <note>Earth</note> or Yin. It means the essence of Earthly Yin transforms in Heaven and then returns to nourish the Earth. **Nine** is the "completed number" of Metal; if it returns to its source, it becomes the "generating number" Four. **Seven** is the "completed number" of Fire; if it reverts to its origin, it becomes the "generating number" Two. **Eight** is the "completed number" of Wood; if it comes home to its source, it becomes the "generating number" Three. **Six** is the "completed number" of Water; if it stays at its origin, it becomes the "generating number" One. Thus, the numbers One, Two, Three, and Four represent the original, primordial substance of Water, Fire, Wood, and Metal at their birth. The numbers Six, Seven, Eight, and Nine represent these same elements in their functional, active, and "completed" state. This describes the path of Yin and Yang transforming, Hard and Soft alternating, and the cycle of retreating when growth reaches its peak and returning when decay reaches its limit. The terms "return," "revert," "come home," and "stay" all signify the process of the **Post-Heaven** <note>acquired/physical</note> returning to the **Pre-Heaven** <note>primordial/spiritual</note> state. This is the most essential secret in the Way of the Elixir; students should investigate it deeply.</gloss>

# Constraining Water to Stabilize Fire: The Beginning of the Five Elements.

The **Male** <note>original: 男者, nanzhe</note> refers to the **Kan** <note>original: 坎, Kan; the trigram representing Water and the moon</note> or the "Male." The **Female** <note>original: 女者, nüzhe</note> refers to the **Li** <note>original: 離, Li; the trigram representing Fire and the sun</note> or the "Female." Kan is associated with the Moon, and its color is white. Li is associated with the Sun, and its color is red. Therefore, it is said: "The male is white and the female is red." However, "white" represents **Metal** <note>original: 金, jin</note> and "red" represents **Fire** <note>original: 火, huo</note>. When Metal encounters Fire, it is forged into a vessel; when Fire refines Metal, it creates a finished object. This is why it is said that "Metal and Fire constrain one another." To "constrain" or "standardize" <note>original: 則, ze</note> means that Metal is the mother of Water, and Water is the child of Metal. By standardizing the Water, one is able to control and stabilize the Fire. Furthermore, Water is the beginning of the **Five Elements** <note>original: 五行, wuxing; the five phases of Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, and Water</note> and the primary of the "Three Grades of Great Medicine." Thus, the text says: "Constrain the Water to stabilize the Fire; this is the beginning of the Five Elements." This refers to the three substances—Metal, Water, and Fire—which must rely on one another to be used as the essential ingredients for refining the **Elixir** <note>original: 煉丹, liandan</note>. In the context of the Elixir's ingredients, Metal and Water combined with Fire result in a warm harmony that generates life. Water and Fire combined with **Earth** <note>original: 土, tu</note> result in a balanced regulation that aids the process. This is the Way of Nature and an unchangeable principle. Some mistakenly believe that Metal, Water, and Earth are the three ingredients, but this is an error. Without Fire, the Metal remains cold and the Water remains chilled; how could they then complete the process of creation and congeal the **Elixir Embryo** <note>original: 丹胎, dantai</note>?

## The highest excellence is like water—pure and without flaw, the form of the Way.

## The image of the True One is hard to depict; it transforms and distributes, with each dwelling alone, like a chicken egg where the black and white correspond.

The **Tao Te Ching** <note>original: 道德經, Daodejing</note> says: "The highest excellence is like water. Water excels at benefiting all things without struggling for position; it dwells in places that the multitude of people dislike, and thus it is close to the Way." "Highest excellence" refers to ultimate goodness. The virtue of ultimate goodness is just like water, because water can benefit and nourish all things while its nature is to flow downward without conflict. Its substance is soft, weak, clear, and clean. Whatever is filthy or turbid, when placed in water, becomes pure and white. This is its "excellence at benefiting things while dwelling in base places," which is why it is close to the Way's essence and function. When the text now says "The highest excellence is like water, pure and without flaw," it uses this meaning. It says that the essence of Water is most beautiful; its function is to benefit things and dwell in lowliness, while its substance is transparent and flawless. This reaffirms the virtue of Water mentioned previously. "The image of the Way, the True One is hard to depict" refers to the fact that Water, as a substance, is the source of the **Heavenly One** <note>original: 天一, tianyi; the primordial unity</note> and the beginning of the Five Elements. It serves as the physical manifestation of the Way. It is transformed from the **True One Energy** <note>original: 眞一氣, zhenyiqi</note> and is born within the **Dark Mystery** <note>original: 玄冥, xuanming; the primordial void</note>. It is difficult to measure its beginnings; how could one possibly draw its shape? This carries the same meaning as the first chapter of this book, which says: "It stands in the dark and is hard to measure; it cannot be fully depicted." "It transforms and distributes, with each dwelling alone" means that the True One Energy divides into Yin and Yang and transforms into Water and Fire. That which is light and clear rises upward, and that which is heavy and turbid sinks downward, so that each is distributed to dwell in its own place. This is the transformation and division of the Way. The *Tao Te Ching* says: "These two emerge together but have different names." The **Chapters on Returning to Destiny** says: "One thing divides into two; he who can know the 'One' is famous." These all share this meaning. "Like a chicken egg, where the black and white correspond" uses the **chicken egg** <note>original: 雞子, jizi</note> as a metaphor for the physical form of the universe. This refers to the **Celestial Sphere Theory** <note>original: 渾天說, Huntianshuo</note>, which says: "The shape of the heavens is like a bird's egg, and the earth dwells within it, just as the shell wraps around the yolk." The model of the Elixir Embryo is exactly like this. The two energies of Yin and Yang are distributed...

# One inch in length and width as the beginning; the four limbs, five viscera, tendons, and bones are then all present. After ten months, it emerges from its womb; the bones are soft enough to be rolled and the flesh is smooth like lead.

# The burning mirror is used to gather fire; without the Sun, no light is born. The moon-vessel is not the stars or moon; how could it obtain water? These two energies are established and far apart, yet their influence still resonates through connection. How much more so for what resides close within the body, held deep within the heart and chest? Yin and Yang correspond to the Sun and Moon; Water and Fire serve as the proof of their efficacy.

The **burning mirror** <note>original: 陽燧, yangsui; a concave bronze mirror used to focus sunlight to start fires</note> is a fire-pearl. It is also called a "fire-vessel." When held against the Sun, it can capture fire, much like the burning lenses used today. The **moon-vessel** <note>original: 方諸, fangzhu; a ritual bronze vessel or mirror used to collect "clestial dew" or water from the moon's atmosphere at night</note> is a type of mirror. It is also called a "Yin-mirror." When turned toward the Moon, one can obtain water, much like the "water mirrors" used today. As recorded in the "Officers of Fire" section of the **Rites of Zhou** <note>original: 周禮, Zhouli; a classic text on ancient bureaucracy</note>: "The Director of Fire is in charge of using the wooden drill to produce fire, and the burning mirror to take 'bright fire' from the Sun, and the vessel to take 'bright water' from the Moon."

This refers to the fact that the fire gathered by the burning mirror and the water obtained by the moon-vessel originate from the essential light of the Sun and Moon; only then are the Water and Fire produced. Consider how the glorious light of the Sun and Moon is established so far away, and yet the influence of their energy resonates and connects without any obstruction. How much more so for the methods of internal cultivation, which reside nearby within the body and mind and are held closely within the chest? By taking the Yin and Yang energies of one's own self and pairing them as the Sun and Moon to operate as Water and Fire, the resulting efficacy is reached most intimately. What difficulty could there possibly be?

This passage uses distant objects to illustrate the principle, then applies it to the body to encourage the student's progress. However, when using the burning mirror or moon-vessel to capture Water and Fire, one must be still so that the light may gather; if there is movement and the light is scattered, nothing is gained. Therefore, in cultivating the **Elixir** <note>original: 丹, dan</note>, when the Spirit is settled and the Energy is harmonious, the "Medicine" is produced; if the Spirit is agitated and the Energy is chaotic, no progress is made. ## The Realized Man hides in the deep abyss, floating and wandering, he guards the Center of the Compass.

The **Tao Te Ching** <note>original: 道德經, Daodejing</note> says: "I have three treasures which I hold and prize: the first is compassion, the second is frugality, and the third is not daring to be first in the world." This describes the way of governing a country. Here, however, the **Three Treasures** <note>original: 三寶, sanbao</note> refer to the ears, eyes, and mouth; this clarifies the method of cultivating the self. Since the ears and eyes govern hearing and seeing, and the mouth governs the intake and output of breath and speech, are these three not the treasures of our body? This is what the **Scripture of the Hidden Accord** <note>original: 陰符經, Yinfujing</note> means when it says: "The corruption of the nine orifices lies in the Three Essentials."

"Blocking and not allowing them to vent" means that during the time of creating the Elixir, one sits upright with legs crossed, body and mind merging in darkness. One causes the functions of the ears, eyes, and mouth to be blocked so they do not communicate with the outside, but are instead all drawn back into the interior. 

"The **Realized Man** <note>original: 眞人, zhenren; a perfected spiritual being</note> hides in the deep abyss": "Realized Man" is a metaphor for **True Lead** <note>original: 眞鉛, zhenqian</note>, and the "Seed of the Elixir" is also symbolized as a Realized Man. To "hide" means to conceal. The "abyss" refers to still water. This says that the concealment of the True Lead occurs within deep water; this is exactly what the **Mirror of Medicine** <note>original: 藥鏡, Yaojing</note> means by "Lead from the Water Village, just a single flavor."

The **Center of the Compass** <note>original: 規中, guizhong</note> refers to the **Elixir Field** <note>original: 丹田, dantian</note>, the **Spirit Chamber** <note>original: 神室, shenshi</note>, the **Yellow Court** <note>original: 黃庭, huangting</note>, or the **Earthen Cauldron** <note>original: 土釜, tufu</note>—these are all metaphorical names for the same place. It means the True Lead floats and wanders up, down, left, and right, while firmly guarding the Seed of the Elixir in the Center of the Compass.

# Embracing one another, awaken to the watch of preservation and loss; the complexion becomes gradually moistened, and the joints grow ever stronger; cast out the various yin evils, and then establish the True Yang.

<gloss>**"Proofs that are difficult to shift"** refers to when one is practicing in the chamber. Even while sleeping, the Spirit and Energy must remain embraced and never be separated for even a moment.</gloss>

<gloss>**"Awaken to the watch of preservation and loss"** means that throughout the twelve periods of the day, one must be mindful and present, observing the **fire-timing** <note>original: 火候, huohou; the precise management of internal heat and breath</note>—its advancement and retreat, its presence and absence—without making any errors. The *Understanding Reality* <note>original: 悟眞篇, Wuzhen pian</note> says: "The whole process depends entirely on the power of cultivation; a hair's breadth of error will fail to produce the Elixir." The *Emerald Void* <note>original: 翠虛篇, Cuixu pian</note> says: "By day, move the spirit-flag; by night, tend the fire-fungus. In the process of adding and subtracting, guard against danger." These all carry this meaning. 

Thus, if one cultivates according to this, through long-accumulated effort, the complexion will gradually become moist and lustrous, and the skin will become like ice and snow. The bones and joints will grow stronger day by day, becoming "golden sinews and jade bones." The *Emerald Void* text says: "The joints open of their own accord, flowing freely; the appearance is lustrous like that of an infant." Furthermore, the "Yin evils" <note>internal imbalances or negative influences</note> within the body are cast out by refining the **True Energy** <note>original: 眞氣, zhenqi</note>, while the **True Yang** <note>original: 正陽, zhengyang; the pure, creative primordial energy</note> of the Elixir Embryo is established by directing the internal breath cycles. *Understanding Reality* says: "When the multitude of Yin is stripped away, the Elixir is mature." Xiao Zixu <note>a Daoist master</note> said: "Refine the Yang-Spirit to dissolve the various Yin." These all share this meaning.</gloss>

## Returning is the proof of the Dao. Weakness is the handle of Virtue.

# Hoe away the accumulated impurities of the past so the subtle pathways may become harmonious and clear; the path to clearing the turbid is found when long-standing darkness yields to bright illumination.

<gloss>"Returning" means to go back and forth or to recur. The *Book of Changes* <note>original: 易, Yi; the I Ching</note> says: "The Way involves returning and repeating." The *Book of the Way and its Virtue* <note>original: 道德經, Daodejing</note> says: "Returning is the movement of the Dao." This refers to the alternating growth and fading of **Yin and Yang**, and the way that movement and stillness serve as each other’s foundation. Therefore, the "Way of Returning" is a natural proof and verification; it does not require forced effort.</gloss>

"Weakness" refers to being soft and yielding. The *Book of Changes* says: "Humility is the handle of Virtue." The *Book of the Way and its Virtue* says: "Weakness is the utility of the Dao." Generally, strength and weakness rely on each other, and hardness and softness alternate in expanding and contracting. However, softness overcomes hardness, and weakness overcomes strength. Therefore, the qualities of being soft, weak, humble, and yielding are the "handle" of the Dao and its Virtue, and one should hold fast to them in practice. Thus, the practitioner of the **Internal Elixir** <note>original: 修丹, xiudan</note> uses the "effort of softness and yielding" <note>the path of non-forcing</note> to transform their rigid, "Post-natal" <note>original: 後天, houtian; the physical state acquired after birth</note> temperament and return to their "Pre-natal" <note>original: 先天, xiantian; primordial</note> nature and life-destiny. By concentrating the spirit and gathering energy, one "cooks and refines" the accumulated dregs and impurities of the past. This is like a farmer hoeing and weeding a field to remove the grass and weeds; afterward, every part of the body, from the large structures to the most hidden and subtle points, becomes harmonious and flows freely. Therefore, the merit of cultivation and the method of gentle nurturing allow that which is turbid to find the path to clarity, and that which has been long darkened to find the way to brilliant light. <gloss>This section serves as a summary of the meanings discussed above.</gloss>

<note>Pronunciation guide: "Love" (hào) is in the departing tone. "Blockage" (què) is pronounced *bì*. "Search" (suǒ) is pronounced *sè*. "Harvest" (huò) is pronounced *huò*. "Ingest" (shí) is pronounced *sì*.</note>

**Mencius** <note>A famous Confucian philosopher (4th century BCE) who emphasized the innate goodness of humanity and the accessibility of virtue.</note> said: "The Way is like a great road. Regardless of whether a person is wise or foolish, all are capable of learning it.

However, worldly people do not examine the truth or falsehood of a path. Instead, they **love the "small arts"** because they seem immediate and easy to grasp; they do not investigate the true depth of the practice and remain ignorant of the refined essence of the **Great Way** <note>original: 大道, dadao</note>. How could they know that the alchemical method of "ingesting the Elixir" is actually a **concise and non-complex matter**? Even a simple man or woman is capable of knowing and practicing it; the only "sickness" is that people do not seek it. Therefore, the Way remains obscured. ## To the Right is the Sixth Chapter

This chapter discusses the **Solar Mirror** and the **Lunar Mirror** <note>original: 陽燧, yangsui and 方諸, fangzhu; ancient ritual tools used to "capture" fire from the sun and water from the moon</note> and how they gather fire and water. Although Heaven and Earth are separated by a vast distance, their **Energy** <note>original: 氣, qi</note> remains in constant communication. How much more so is this true for the Way of cultivation, which is located right here within our own body and mind?

One only needs to "lock" the **Three Treasures** <note>original: 三寶, sanbao; Vital Essence (jing), Energy (qi), and Spirit (shen)</note> and utilize the movement of "Water and Fire" to create the Elixir. Afterward, one enters the "Chamber of Nurturing" to cultivate and protect the **Spiritual Embryo** <note>original: 靈胎, lingtai; the new, immortal self formed through meditation</note>. Then, the physical form will naturally become moist and lustrous; the **Yin** <note>passive/dark principle</note> will be exhausted and the **Yang** <note>active/light principle</note> will be pure, allowing one to transcend the world as a **True Being** <note>original: 眞, zhen; an immortal or perfected person</note>.

But worldly people do not understand this correct path and instead enter crooked "side doors." It is no wonder they never succeed. How could they know that ingesting the **Returned Elixir** <note>original: 還丹, huandan</note> is a concise and non-complex method that every person can perform and every individual can learn? Mencius said: "To leave the peaceful dwelling empty and not reside in it, to abandon the straight path and not follow it—how sad!" This is exactly what is meant here.

# The Flowing Pearl of the Sun always wishes to leave man. Suddenly obtaining the Golden Flower, they turn and depend on each other. They transform into White Liquid, condensing until they reach extreme hardness. <gloss>The word "Suddenly" (卒) is pronounced *cui*.</gloss>

The **Flowing Pearl** refers to **Wood Mercury** <note>original: 木汞, mugong; a metaphor for the volatile, moving aspect of the mind or spirit</note>. Its nature is like flowing water, and its shape is round like a pearl. It bears the image of the Sun and is transformed from **True Energy** <note>original: 眞氣, zhenqi</note>. However, while the "Flowing Pearl" can refer to external substances, the **Spiritual Mercury** <note>original: 靈汞, linggong</note> within the human body also flows and rolls like a pearl; it is difficult to capture and easy to lose. As the *Song of the Great Way of the Spiritual Source* says: "How could this thing have a fixed position? It changes with the time..."
