### The Golden Flower

This is **True Lead** <note>original: 眞鉛, zhenqian; the stable, "heavy" counterpart to the volatile Mercury</note>. It means that when the Flowing Pearl obtains the Golden Flower, the **Lead and Mercury** <note>the two primary alchemical metaphors for Yin and Yang, or body and spirit</note> depend on each other, melting and transforming into **White Liquid**. Afterward, they condense and become hard and stable, preventing any further "flowing away." *The Chapters on Awakening to the Truth* <note>original: 悟眞篇, Wuzhen pian; a seminal 11th-century alchemical text</note> says: "The Golden Tripod wishes to retain the Mercury within the Vermilion; the Jade Pool first lets down the Silver within the Water." It also says: "Simply use the **Earthly Soul** to capture the **Vermilion Mercury**; then the **Heavenly Spirit** will naturally control the **Watery Gold**." These all share the same meaning.

# The leader sings, and in a brief interval, it dissolves and transforms into water, like "Horse-teeth" and "Langgan" stones. The Yang then goes to harmonize; emotion and nature follow their natural course. <gloss>The word "harmonize" (和) is in the departing tone.</gloss>

The **Golden Flower** acts as the "leader who sings" <note>the initiating force</note>. Regarding the phrase "in a brief interval": the Golden Flower is the **Yellow Sprout** <note>original: 黃芽, huangya; another term for the first sign of the Elixir forming</note>, which is True Lead. This means that in the cultivation of the Elixir, one first uses the **Energy** of the True Lead. It moves back and forth within the alchemical vessel, circulating completely within a single moment. 

As for "dissolving into water" and "**Horse-teeth and Langgan**": a horse has no lower teeth, only upper teeth. **Langgan** <note>original: 琅玕</note> is a beautiful stone resembling jade that grows at the foot of mountains. This describes the use of the medicinal ingredients: in the beginning, they are nothing but a single Energy. When refined by the **True Fire**, the True Lead melts into water and moves from below to above, and from above back to below. This is called "White Snow" or "**Jade Fluid**." It is compared to "Horse-teeth and Langgan" because it represents the image of an upper and lower exchange. 

The third chapter of the later section says: "Its shape is like mid-winter ice, or Langgan spitting out stalactites." This is the same meaning. "The Yang then goes to harmonize; emotion and nature follow their natural course" means that the Golden Flower is refined first, and the Jade Fluid is cooked afterward. This is the "calling and responding" between **Yin and Yang**, the natural path where emotion and nature rely on one another. The third chapter of this text says: "Push emotion to join with nature, turning to interact with each other." It is the same principle.

This is what the *Chapters on Returning to Life* mean by: "When the season is exactly right, you must harvest quickly."

"Restraining and storing in the **Forbidden Gate**": "Restraining" means the act of harvesting. "Storing" means sealing it away. The "Forbidden Gate" is like the inner palace, a metaphor for the **Central Palace** <note>original: 中宮, zhonggong; the center of the body's energy system, also called the Yellow Court</note>. It means harvesting the medicinal ingredients at the right time and sealing them within the "Yellow Court" of the Central Palace. This is what the *Chapters on Awakening to the Truth* mean by: "Send it back to the **Earthen Pot** and seal it firmly."

"The **Compassionate Mother** nurtures": The Compassionate Mother is the **Kun Mother** <note>the trigram Kun, representing Earth and the receptive principle</note>. It means that within the "Earthen Pot" of the Kun Mother, the **Golden Embryo** is hidden and nurtured.

This means the six children transport Yin and Yang, rotating them in and out of the Kun Mother's chamber. This is like a young crow feeding its parents in return for its upbringing; it is the "Filial Son" repaying the debt. 

"The **Strict Father** issues commands, instructing the children": The Strict Father is the **Qian Father** <note>the trigram Qian, representing Heaven and the active principle</note>. The child...

# Using the nature of Fire to melt Metal; Metal fells Wood to make it flourish.
# The Five Phases alternate in prosperity and rely upon one another.

Prosperity <gloss>pronounced 'wang', meaning flourishing</gloss>. ○ "Alternating" [錯] means to take turns. "Prosperity" [王/旺] refers to the cycle of decline and flourishing. "Relying" [據] means to depend on. "Birth" [生] refers to the cycle of generation and overcoming. This refers to the principles of the **Five Phases** <note>original: 五行, Wuxing; Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, and Water</note> regarding their decline, flourishing, generation, and overcoming. For example, Wood is prosperous in the spring while Water declines; Fire is prosperous in the summer while Wood declines; Earth is prosperous in late summer while Fire declines; Metal is prosperous in autumn while Earth declines; Water is prosperous in winter while Metal declines. They circulate without exhaustion. This is the alternation of the Five Phases' decline and prosperity. 

Furthermore, Metal generates Water but overcomes Wood; Water generates Wood but overcomes Fire; Wood generates Fire but overcomes Earth; Fire generates Earth but overcomes Metal; Earth generates Metal but overcomes Water. They cycle without end. This is the mutual dependence, generation, and overcoming of the Five Phases. This is what the *School Sayings of Confucius* means by "the Five Phases alternating in prosperity, generating each other from beginning to end." 

However, although the nature of Fire is to "melt Metal," when Metal encounters Fire, it is transformed into a useful object and becomes valuable. Although the substance of Metal can "fell Wood," when Wood encounters Metal, it is shaped into a vessel and becomes a thing of pride. Therefore, in the **Way of Cultivation**, one uses Lead to control Mercury to create the medicine, and uses Fire to refine Metal to form the Elixir. This is because the principles of generation, overcoming, control, and transformation are utilized in this way.

# Difficult to transmit in writing
# The Three, the Five, and the One: the ultimate essence of Heaven and Earth. They can be explained by oral instructions.

"Three" refers to Water (one) and Fire (two). "Five" refers to Earth (five). This is what Chapter Eleven of the first section means by: "**Zi and Wu** <note>Midnight/North and Noon/South</note> join to make three; **Wu and Ji** <note>two aspects of Earth</note> are called five." "One" is the **Single Energy** <note>original: 一氣, yiqi; the primordial source of all things</note>. This is what Chapter Six of the first section means by: "The One is used for sealing and closing; the people of the world do not know it." Therefore, when combined, they are called "Three-Five-One." 

Furthermore, *The Chapters on Awakening to the Truth* considers Wood (three) and Fire (two) joining to make five; Water (one) and Metal (four) joining to make five; and Earth itself being five. This makes "Three Fives." Together with the **Infant’s Single Energy**, it is also called "Three-Five-One." However, these are all metaphorical descriptions of external symbols. In the **Internal Elixir**, the "Three-Five" are the divided functions of the Single Energy, and the "Single Energy" is the unified substance of the Three-Five. These are the stages of "adding and subtracting" the Fire-timing, the measurements for breathing the **Great Harmony** <note>original: 太和, taihe; a state of primordial balance</note>. Therefore, they are called the most refined and secret treasures of Heaven and Earth; one must seek the true explanation through the **oral instructions** <note>original: 口授, koushou; direct transmission from a master</note> of a perfected person, for it is difficult to transmit such mystery and subtlety through brush and paper. *The Chapters on Awakening to the Truth* says: "Three, Five, and One are but three words, yet those who have understood them from ancient times to now are truly rare." This is the meaning.

# Zi should turn to the right, and Wu then rotates to the East; Mao and You are the boundaries separating the names of Host and Guest.

Generally, the Way of cultivating reality and refining the Elixir takes the principles of Heaven and Earth as its model. Therefore, in the method of harmonizing the "Elixir-head" <note>the initial seed of the elixir</note>, the operation of the Fire Tallies revolves to the left from **Zi** <note>the North/Midnight position</note> and turns to the right from **Wu** <note>the South/Noon position</note>, imitating the way the Heavenly Path favors the left. This is the "natural order" of the Elixir method. This is what *The Chapters on Awakening to the Truth* means by: "Who recognizes the floating and sinking that determines host and guest?" Now, when it is said that "Zi should turn to the right and Wu rotates to the East," this refers to the method of the **inner chamber for warm nourishment** <note>a more advanced, internal stage of the process</note>...

<meta>Page 98 continues the technical explanation of "reversal" in alchemical practice, specifically how the directional movements of the internal energies (Zi, Wu, Mao, You) shift roles between "Host" and "Guest." ...models the **Way of Earth** which favors the right. This is the **reversal** <note>original: 逆, ni; a fundamental concept in alchemy where the practitioner reverses the natural flow of energy to return to a primordial state</note> of the Elixir method. This is what *The Chapters on Awakening to the Truth* <note>original: 悟眞篇, Wuzhen pian</note> means by: "Yield to him as the Host while I act as the Guest." The *Book of Changes* says: "Counting what has passed follows the natural order; knowing what is to come is reversal. Therefore, the **Changes** <note>the I Ching</note> is a system of reversed numbers." 

The Way of cultivating the Elixir is the same. Thus, following the natural order and the reversal are both required; Yin and Yang must interact, and only then is the creative transformation inexhaustible. *The Chapters on Awakening to the Truth* says: "When the Elixir-head is harmonized, the types are the same; the warm nourishment has two different applications." This is the principle. 

As for "**Mao and You are the boundaries separating the names of Host and Guest**," it means that **Zi** <note>Midnight/North</note> is in the North and resides below; **Wu** <note>Noon/South</note> is in the South and resides above; **Mao** <note>Dawn/East</note> is in the East and resides on the left; and **You** <note>Dusk/West</note> is in the West and resides on the right. That which moves forward first to take charge is the **Host**, and that which follows after is the **Guest**. Now, when Zi should turn to the right, then You becomes the Host and Mao becomes the Guest. When Wu rotates to the East, then Mao becomes the Host and You becomes the Guest. Therefore, Mao and You act as the boundaries between North and South, taking turns to hold the two titles of Host and Guest. 

**Yu Quanyang** <note>Yu Yan, a famous 13th-century alchemist and commentator</note> says: "East and West, along with Mao and You, are not simply the physical directions established by Heaven and Earth, nor are they literally the left and right sides of the human body. Yet, one cannot abandon one's own body to seek them elsewhere." 

Therefore, students must investigate and study this with the utmost refinement; only then can they understand the general outline.

# The Dragon exhales to the Tiger, and the Tiger inhales the Dragon’s essence; the two feed upon one another, both greedily merging, following each other to bite, swallow, chew, and gulp.

<gloss>The word "merging" [併] is written as "then" [便] in one version. "Bite" [銜] is pronounced *xian*. "Chew" [咀] is pronounced *ju*. ○ Exhaling creates the **Dragon** <note>symbolizing the Wood element and the spirit/breath</note>, yet it is rooted in the exhalation itself; thus, the **Tiger** <note>symbolizing the Metal element and the physical essence</note> inhales the Dragon’s essence. Therefore, these two serve as each other’s foundation, alternating between the use of the "hard" and the "soft." This is the meaning behind them feeding upon and greedily merging with one another. The image of Yin and Yang intersecting, swallowing and spitting into one another, is represented by biting, swallowing, and chewing. # Harmonizing the Condensed Essence and Shaping the Form. Metal and Stone Do Not Decay. Examining Faithfully Without Leakage. Attaining Success in the Way.

The preceding text explained how failing to understand the underlying principles leads to deceiving oneself and others. Now, it suggests that if one carefully examines their circumstances and encounters the Great Way <note>original: 大道, Dadao</note>, one can observe its first signs and clues. By tracing the origins through similar categories and weighing the beginning and end of all things, one finds that every path leads to the Truth, and the distinction between the false and the correct becomes clear as day. 

Consider the way the **Five Elements** <note>original: 五行, Wuxing; Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, and Water</note> interact through the laws of generation and overcoming: Water overcomes Fire, yet Fire produces Earth, which in turn restrains Water. Fire overcomes Metal, yet Metal produces Water, which in turn restrains Fire. Wood overcomes Earth, yet Earth produces Metal, which in turn restrains Wood. Metal overcomes Wood, yet Wood produces Fire, which in turn restrains Metal. Earth overcomes Water, yet Water produces Wood, which in turn restrains Earth. 

In this way, the elements mutually overcome and prune one another to achieve the work of regulation. They take turns acting as "Mother" and "Father" to one another, serving as the very foundation of birth and growth. Thus, the Mother is symbolized by **Earth**, presiding over the containment of Breath and Fluids. The Father is symbolized by **Heaven**, presiding over the endowment of Spirit and Essence. This is why pure Essence is condensed in Heaven, and the various categories of things take shape upon the Earth. The Sun and Moon obtain this to shine with eternal brightness; **Metal and Stone** <note>symbols of permanence in alchemy</note> persist because of this and do not decay. 

The principle of refining the Elixir is exactly like this. One must simply examine the way Heaven and Earth create and transform, and deeply investigate the mechanism by which the Five Elements generate and overcome one another. Focus the mind without forgetting, and guard the body so the energy does not leak away; then the Elixir can be obtained, and the Way can be naturally completed.

# The Male "Kan" is the Moon. The Female "Li" is the Sun. The Sun bestows its virtue; the Moon spreads its light. The Moon receives the Sun’s transformation, yet its substance is not harmed or diminished.

<gloss>The character for "Bestow" [施] is pronounced in the departing tone. ○ In the *Treatise on Explaining the Trigrams* <note>a commentary on the I Ching, or Book of Changes</note>, the **Kan** <term>The "Water" trigram, representing the internal male energy</term> is called the "Middle Son" and is associated with the Moon. ### Chapter Sixteen. What is called the "mutual encroachment and eclipse of the Sun and Moon" always occurs during the period of the new moon. Therefore, **Lord Wei's** <note>Wei Boyang, the legendary 2nd-century author of the *Cantong qi*</note> intention covers both aspects, using these metaphors to teach students the principles of both governing a country and cultivating the self.

## Men and women need each other, containing and spitting out to nourish; male and female mix together, seeking their own kind.

"Men and women needing each other" refers to the Sun and Moon of the "Male Kan" and "Female Li"; Yin and Yang require each other to function as "essence and application." "Containing and spitting out to nourish" means the Sun contains within it the Yin energy, while the Moon "spits out" or reflects its Yang light. They interact in this way to mutually benefit and nourish one another. As for "male and female mixing together," male and female are simply Yin and Yang. The Sun is Yang, yet it contains a "female bird" <note>the Three-Legged Crow, a symbol of the Yin within the Yang</note>; the Moon is Yin, yet it contains a "male rabbit" <note>the Jade Rabbit, a symbol of the Yang within the Yin</note>. Furthermore, the **Kan** trigram is Yang on the inside but Yin on the outside, while the **Li** trigram is Yin on the inside but Yang on the outside. This is how Yin and Yang are "mixed together" and contained within one another. "Seeking their own kind" refers to the bestowal and transformation of the Male Kan and Female Li, and the mutual containment of the Sun and Moon; they seek each other out based on their corresponding categories. Thus, practitioners of the Way must also seek the "male and female" (the Yin and Yang) within their own bodies as the fundamental basis for cultivation.

## Gold transforms into water, and the nature of water is to overflow; fire transforms into earth, so that water cannot wander. <gloss>The One Qi of the Pre-Heaven state.</gloss>

This refers to "True Gold," and Gold (Metal) has the capacity to produce Water. The nature of that Water is to "overflow" and spread widely. However, energy also acts as Fire, and Fire has the capacity to produce Earth. Therefore, when Water meets Earth, it is contained and does not overflow or move recklessly. This describes the functions of these three—Water, Fire, and Earth; they are all ultimately nothing more than the transformations of the **Single Qi** <term>the primordial breath or life force</term>. The essences of the Sun, Moon, Yin, and Yang are also this Single Qi, divided into two and yet containing three. For the Sun is the essence of Wood and Fire, yet it contains "Self-Earth" <note>Ji-Earth</note> within it; the Moon is the essence of Metal and Water, yet it contains "Mountain-Earth" <note>Wu-Earth</note> within it.

## Thus the male moves and bestows outside, while the female is still and hides inside; if the overflow exceeds the limit, it is restrained by the female.

"Male and female" are metaphors for Yin and Yang. Therefore, Yang governs movement and bestows its influence outwardly. Yin governs stillness and remains hidden within. This is like a man being "restrained" or stabilized by a woman. For example, the **Qian** <term>The "Heaven" hexagram, representing pure Yang</term> of the fourth lunar month represents Yang at its peak, exceeding its limit. By the fifth month, the **Gou** <term>The "Meeting" hexagram, where one Yin line appears at the bottom</term> arrives, where the birth of Yin begins to restrain the Yang. This is the meaning. This section follows the previous discussion of the mutual need of male and female and the mutual restraint of Water, Fire, and Earth, to further clarify the transformation of Kan and Li and the eclipses of the Sun and Moon. Such is the principle of the mutual use of Yin and Yang.

## The Po-soul acts as a bell for the Hun-soul, preventing excess or extravagance; neither cold nor hot, advancing and retreating at the proper time, each achieves harmony by "spitting out" this essence.

<gloss>The word for "bell" here functions as a "clamp" or restraint.</gloss> The **Po-soul** <term>the corporeal soul associated with the physical body and Yin</term> is Yin; it is the **Qi** <term>vital breath or energy</term> of Metal. # Cinnabar is the essence of Wood; meeting Metal, they merge. Where Metal and Water meet, Wood and Fire are companions.

<gloss>**Cinnabar** is vermilion. Among the **Five Elements** <term>the five phases of energy: Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, Water</term>, it belongs to Fire, while Water is the Qi of Metal. Thus, when Water and Fire intersect, they generate life; when Metal and Wood merge, they form a "vessel" or tool. Here it says, "Cinnabar is the essence of Wood; meeting Metal, they merge," but it does not explicitly mention **Black Lead** <note>the symbol for the Yin-within-Yang</note> or Water—this is a "shorthand" in the writing. This is what the master **Yuanyangzi** <note>a Tang dynasty alchemist</note> meant when he said: "If you wish to know Cinnabar, it is the essence of Wood; move it to the Western position to merge with Metal." Furthermore, the *Fuming pian* <note>"Chapters on Returning to Life"</note> says: "Once the Dragon and Tiger meet, they cling to one another; as soon as Kan and Li copulate, the embryo is formed." This carries the same meaning. Since Metal can produce Water, Metal is also hidden within Water. Since Wood can produce Fire, Wood is naturally contained within Fire. Therefore, they are called "Metal and Water meeting" and "Wood and Fire being companions." Within the Way of the Elixir, this corresponds to "Silver hidden within Lead" and "Mercury contained within Cinnabar." In the human body, this corresponds to "**Qi** within the Essence" and "**Fluid** within the Blood." Students should expand upon this and apply these categories; then the Great Work of the Alchemical Method will be complete.</gloss>

...the **Azure Dragon**. The position of Metal is in the West, and its symbol is the **White Tiger**. But why are only the Dragon and the Tiger mentioned? It is because North and South represent the "longitude" <note>the vertical axis, or *jing*</note>, while East and West represent the "latitude" <note>the horizontal axis, or *wei*</note>. The longitude represents the "body" or essence and remains still; the latitude represents the "function" and is in constant motion. Therefore, the text speaks only of the Dragon and Tiger and does not mention the **Vermilion Bird** or the **Black Tortoise**. This is what the elder **Zhang Ziyang** <note>the 11th-century author of the 'Chapters on Understanding Reality'</note> meant when he said: "The Four Symbols do not depart from the two bodies." There is also an old saying: "The Dragon emerges from the fire; the Tiger is born within the water." This carries the same meaning. The Dragon's Yang number is odd and the Tiger's Yin number is even because the Dragon is Yang and belongs to Wood; the generative number of Wood is three, which is an odd number. The Tiger is Yin and belongs to Metal; the generative number of Metal is four, which is an even number.

## The Liver’s Green is the Father; the Lungs’ White is the Mother; the Kidneys’ Black is the
## Son; the Heart’s Red is the Daughter; the Spleen’s Yellow is the Ancestor. <gloss>The heavens and earth have the Five Elements; the human body has the five internal organs.</gloss>
## The Son is the beginning of the Five Elements; the three things are one family, all passing through the Earth-elements.

As the liver belongs to Wood, its color is green. The lungs belong to Metal, so their color is white. The kidneys belong to Water, so their color is black. The heart belongs to Fire, so its color is red. The spleen belongs to Earth, so its color is yellow. This is how the **Five Elements** <term>the five phases of energy</term> are paired with the human body. 

If we speak of the Five Elements in terms of "Creation and Transformation" <note>the natural order of the universe</note>, then Wood is Yang and is the "father" of Fire. Metal is Yin and is the "mother" of Water. Water is Yang and is the "son" of Metal. Fire is Yin and is the "daughter" of Wood. Earth is also Yang; both Metal and Wood are born and nourished within Earth. Therefore, Earth is called the "ancestor" of Water and Fire and the sovereign of the Five Elements. 

The numbers of the creation of Heaven and Earth begin with One. The cycle of the Five Elements begins with Water. Thus, "Heaven creates One as Water," and Water is the "son" of Metal. This is why the Son is called the beginning of the Five Elements. However, when Metal and Water combine into one, and Wood and Fire partner as one, and Earth stands as its own unit, they form "three things" that share one family. This means the Four Symbols all return to the **Wu and Ji Earth** <term>the two aspects of the central element Earth, representing the stabilizing center</term>. This is what the *Wuzhen pian* means by: "The Four Symbols and Five Elements all rely on Earth." Similarly, Chapter Eleven of the first volume says: "Once the three natures have met and merged, the original nature shares the same ancestor." 

According to the *Cuixu Yin* <note>"Chant of Emerald Emptiness," a famous alchemical poem</note>: "The liver, heart, spleen, lungs, and kidneys are merely minced meat; they are but the old fences of an empty house." This means that the **Way of the Golden Elixir** is a divine transformation of "something born from nothing." It is not a physical action involving tangible matter or fleshly organs. Therefore, the organs are called an "empty house" or "old fences." When **Master Wei** <note>Wei Boyang, the legendary author of the text</note> speaks of the five organs, he is merely using them as metaphors for the Five Elements as they exist in the human body. He wants students to clearly understand the movement of Yin and Yang, not to stubbornly cling to the physical organs as the focus of the work.

## Hardness and softness arise in turns, further arranged in their respective divisions; the Dragon in the West and the Tiger in the East establish the axes of the dawn and sunset.

# Punishment and Virtue meet together in joyful greeting.

As the *I Ching* <note>The "Book of Changes"</note> says: "Hardness and softness push against each other, and thus change and transformation are born."</gloss>

# Punishment governs killing and lies hidden; Virtue governs life and rises. In the second month, the elms fall as the "River Chief" <note>He-kui, a star in the Big Dipper associated with the sign of the Dog/Metal</note> descends upon the East; in the eighth month, the wheat sprouts as the "Heavenly Pivot" <note>Tian-gang, the handle of the Big Dipper associated with the sign of the Dragon/Wood</note> takes its place in the West.

<gloss>*Gang* is pronounced like "hard."</gloss> ○ Master **Dong Zhongshu** <note>a famous Han Dynasty scholar who connected natural cycles to human ethics</note> said: "The greatest aspect of the Way of Heaven lies in Yin and Yang. Yang is Virtue, and Yin is Punishment." Punishment governs killing, and Virtue governs life. Thus, it is said that Punishment governs "killing and hiding," while Virtue governs "life and rising." All things sprout and grow when spring arrives; however, only the seeds of the elm tree fall at this time. This is because in the second month (the position of *Mao*), the "River Chief" star arrives. This star belongs to the sign of *Xu* (the Dog) and contains the energy of "Sovereign Metal" <note>Xin Metal</note>. Since Metal represents the energy of killing, the elms drop their leaves because the "killing energy" of the River Chief has descended upon the East. 

Conversely, all things are pruned and killed when autumn arrives; however, only the wheat sprouts at this time. This is because in the eighth month (the position of *You*), the "Heavenly Pivot" star arrives. This star belongs to the sign of *Chen* (the Dragon) and contains the energy of "Girder Wood" <note>Yi Wood</note>. Since Wood represents the energy of life, the wheat sprouts because the "life energy" of the Heavenly Pivot has taken its place in the West. This illustrates the meaning of "Punishment and Virtue" alongside the previous discussion of "Hardness and Softness arising in turns."

# Zi in the South and Wu in the North mutually act as the guiding principles; the numbers One and Nine come to an end and begin again; containing the Primal Essence within the Void and Danger stars, sowing the seed at the Zi hour.

In the movement of the Way of Heaven and Earth, the Yin of the Earth transforms into Yang, and its energy rises toward Heaven—this is moving from the North (*Zi*) toward the South. The Yang of Heaven transforms into Yin, and its energy descends toward the Earth—this is moving from the South (*Wu*) toward the North. This back-and-forth movement is endless, and the shifts between upper and lower are infinite. This interaction of Yin and Yang forms the "guiding principles" <term>the fundamental grid or structural threads</term> of Heaven and Earth. ## Conclusion of Chapter Eleven

This chapter explains how the **Four Images** <note>the symbolic animals of the four directions</note> merge to become the Dragon and the Tiger. These "three things" all return to become a single family. Hardness and softness take turns; Punishment and Virtue appear together. The North and South (*Zi* and *Wu*) serve as the vertical structural threads, while the numbers One and Nine represent the beginning and end of the North and South. The root of "containing the essence and sowing the seed" is nothing other than the transformations of a single, unified energy. The *Four Hundred Words on the Golden Elixir* says: "The Great Primordial Chaos contains the Great Void; the Great Void encompasses the three realms. But when you seek its source, it is but a single grain as small as a millet seed." These are truly honest words.

# [With] thinning hair and rotting teeth, they would never know each other.
<gloss>The pronunciation of *ju* is like *ju*. *Yao* is pronounced *miao*. *Tiao* is pronounced *tiao*. *Su* is pronounced *qiu*. *Qiu* is pronounced *qiu*. *Shu* is pronounced *shu*. <note>These are traditional phonetics for the classical Chinese characters.</note> This section cites the meaning of the "virtuous lady as a fit mate for the gentleman" from the *Book of Songs*. It clarifies that the "Way" (*Tao*) refers to Yin and Yang finding their correct match. Just as animals have male and female and do not live in isolation, and just as the symbol of the **Dark Warrior** <term>Xuanwu, the deity of the North</term> consists of the tortoise and snake entwined and supporting each other, this illustrates the principle of Yin and Yang needing one another. This is true for both humans and all living things. As the *Book of Changes* (*Yijing*) says: "One Yin and one Yang interacting is called the Way." 

Suppose two women lived together in the same room; despite their beauty, even if you ordered the great orators **Su Qin or Zhang Yi** <note>famous diplomats from the Warring States period</note> to act as matchmakers and use their most persuasive and harmonious speech to join them as husband and wife, they would reach the age of thinning hair and rotting teeth <note>extreme old age</note> without ever "knowing each other" in a way that creates life. This is what the *Book of Changes* means by: "Two women living together, but their wills move in different directions." 

**Master Yu Quanyang** <note>a famous Taoist commentator</note> says: "Some people get stuck on the literal meaning of 'the male does not dwell alone' and 'the female does not live in solitude.' They claim that the 'cultivation of the elixir' cannot be done without a woman, otherwise it is 'solitary Yang.' They then falsely cite this chapter to justify their deviant and perverse theories, while mocking the true Path as being too impractical. This shows a great lack of self-awareness." How significant these words are!</gloss>

# If the ingredients are not of the right species, their names and categories differ, the timing is off, and the governing principles are lost, then even if the Yellow Emperor stood over the furnace, the Great One held the fire, the Eight Lords pounded and refined, and the Prince of Huainan mixed the brew; even if you built a grand temple with a high altar and jade steps, and offered dried qilin meat and phoenix jerky; even if you held the scrolls and knelt for a long time, praying to the gods above and pleading with the ghosts below, or bathed and fasted in hopes of success—it would be like using glue to patch a cooking pot or applying salmiac <term>ammonium chloride, a harsh mineral</term> to a wound. It would be like adding ice to remove cold, or using boiling water to remove heat. The tortoise would fly and the snake would dance—everything would become increasingly chaotic.
<gloss>This means that in the Path of cultivating the elixir, if the "medicines" <note>the internal energies of the body</note> are not of the correct species and the timing of the process is lost, even the holiness of the **Yellow Emperor** or the **Great One** <note>high deities/ancestors of alchemy</note> cannot save the process, even if they personally tended the furnace. Even if the **Eight Lords** or the **Prince of Huainan** <note>legendary immortals associated with the text *Huainanzi*</note> refined the ingredients; even if you built a temple with stairs made of gold and jade, offered the most exotic ritual meats, and showed the utmost devotion by kneeling and praying to every spirit and ghost; even if you purified yourself through fasting—it would all be in vain. 

It would be like a leaky pot: if you use glue to fix it, it will only melt and leak more. If you use salmiac on a sore, it will only worsen. If you want to get rid of cold but add ice, or get rid of heat but use boiling water, the result is the opposite of the intent. Even if you could make the "tortoise fly and the snake dance" <note>a metaphor for unnatural, chaotic movements</note>, it would only show how disordered things have become. This is not only useless; it is harmful to one's body and family. Can one afford not to be careful?</gloss>

## Chapter 12 (to the right)

This chapter explains that the mutual necessity of Yin and Yang is what is called the **Way** <term>Tao</term>. Solitary Yin or lone Yang cannot achieve the "transformation and creation" <note>the process of generating new life or the spiritual elixir</note>. Therefore, even with the persuasive eloquence of **Su Qin and Zhang Yi** <note>legendary diplomats known for their ability to form alliances through speech</note>, they could not make two women "know each other" <note>a metaphor for the inability of two similar poles—two Yins—to create life</note>. Even if immortals, perfected beings, and holy sages were involved, if one departs from the correct "species" of **medicines** <note>the internal energetic ingredients</note>, then all the bustling activity and effort would ultimately be of no benefit. As the *Chapters on Understanding Reality* <term>Wuzhen pian, a seminal text on internal alchemy</term> says:

> Only when Yin and Yang find their own kind can they resonate and interact; when the "two-eights" <note>a technical term for the balanced proportions of ingredients, totaling sixteen ounces/a full pound</note> match, they naturally harmonize and become close.

It also says:

> A message to all you gentlemen who study the Way: if you do not recognize Yin and Yang, do not act recklessly.

How profound these words are!

# The Rectified Meaning of the *Tally of the Three in Accordance with the Book of Changes*, Volume Three

## Lower Part

### Annotated by Dong Dening (styled Yuanzhenzi), a later scholar from Kuaiji

In ancient times, the sages and worthies held fast to their purpose and embraced the Truth. They refined the **Nine Tripods** <note>a reference to the "Nine Cauldrons," symbolizing the advanced stages of alchemical transformation</note>, and their worldly traces faded into the hidden realms. They contained their essence and nourished their spirit, harmonizing their virtue with the **Three Primals** <term>Sanyuan: the three fundamental energies of Heaven, Earth, and Humanity, or the three "dantian" energy centers in the body</term>. Their vital fluids permeated the **interstices of the skin** <note>original: *couli*, the space between the skin and muscles</note>, and their tendons and bones became dense and firm. All harmful influences were expelled, while righteous energy <term>qi</term> remained forever. Through long accumulation and practice, their physical forms were transformed, and they ascended as immortals. <gloss>"Vital fluids" is written as "overflowing essence" in one version. The annotations here provide specific pronunciations for the Chinese characters for "interstices," "dense," "expel," and "accumulate."</gloss>

○ The Way of the Immortals requires a person of benevolence and a gentleman of noble character to apply effort for a long duration with deep dedication before it can be achieved. Thus, the sages and worthies of old embraced the mysterious and subtle Way, holding the essence of the "True One." They subdued the **Primal Energy of the Pre-heaven** <note>the pure, undifferentiated energy existing before physical birth</note> and refined the **Fire Tallies of the Nine Cycles** <note>the specific timing and intensity of the internal alchemical heat</note>. They transformed their old, tainted physical traces and retreated into the daily-renewed mysterious mechanism. They harbored their essence and spirit within the **Two Energies** <note>Yin and Yang</note> and channeled their virtue through the Three Primals. Consequently, their vital fluids filled the spaces between skin and muscle. <gloss>Their tendons and bones became robust and dense. They used the metaphorical "fire" of practice to expel the "cold" evils of excessive Yin, and refined their spirit to preserve the energy of the "Pure Yang." By accumulating merit and performing good deeds over a long period, they transformed their physical form and essence to attain the Truth. Their names were then recorded in the "Green Registers" <note>the celestial records of the immortals</note> and their spirits returned to the "Azure Heavens." The "interstices" refers to the space within the layers of the skin.</gloss>

Out of compassion for later generations and those who love the Way, [the sages] observed how people followed superficial trends or merely "pointed at and sketched" ancient texts <note>interpreted them superficially or literally</note>. They produced diagrams and records to instruct future descendants. However, they only revealed the "branches and leaves" while concealing the "root." They used various names and aliases to mask their meanings, deliberately obscuring the texts. When students obtained these works, they would treasure them in storage boxes for their entire lives [without understanding them]. Children would inherit their fathers' "trade," and grandsons would follow their ancestors, yet they remained lost in confusion for generations, never truly seeing or hearing the truth. Consequently, this caused—

# The official no longer serves. The farmer neglects his weeding. The merchant abandons his goods. The dedicated seeker finds his family impoverished.
<gloss>The characters for "to like" and "beside" are both in the departing tone. "To reveal" is pronounced as "to appear." "To cover" is pronounced as "fujiu." "To accumulate" is pronounced "zan." "To follow" is pronounced "zhong." "Official" is pronounced "huan."</gloss>

○ After the sages and worthies attained the Way for themselves, they felt concern for later generations who loved the Way but had no gate or path by which to enter. Consequently, they followed the general appearance of the truth and "sketched out" ancient texts <note>interpreted them superficially</note>, creating scriptures and producing diagrams to instruct later students, so that they might follow the "stream" back to the "source." However, in establishing their words and launching their theories, they often revealed only the "branches and leaves" while concealing the "root." They used various aliases and titles to mask the meaning, deliberately making the many phrases of the text deceptive. Unfortunately, students did not examine the true intent and purpose; instead, they spent their entire lives treating these texts like a collection of spokes <note>referring to a wheel, meaning they went in circles or just gathered information</note> to be guarded. Sons followed in the footsteps of their ancestors' "trade," and for generations, they remained lost in confusion, neither seeing nor hearing the truth. As a result, officials lost their positions, farmers abandoned their fields, merchants left behind their goods, and the families of dedicated seekers became poor. This is something I find deeply tragic.

# I have standardized and recorded these words. They are concise and easy to contemplate. The matters are simplified and not complex. I have spread out the specific details; the reality within them is plain to see. The weights and measures are numbered, following one another in order. Therefore, I have composed a "Concluding Song" to serve as an opening and a gate. The wise should ponder this carefully and apply their minds to investigate it.
<gloss>The character for "easy" is pronounced "yi."</gloss>

○ Lord Wei <note>Wei Boyang, the legendary 2nd-century author of the *Cantong qi*</note> saw that the various groups of students of the Way did not possess the true explanation and were lost in error their entire lives. Therefore, he standardized the text of the *Tally of the Three*, making the words concise and easy to reflect upon, and the subject matter focused and not overly complex. By spreading out the "branches and leaves" <note>the specific details of the practice</note>, the "core reality" naturally becomes visible to the reader. Furthermore, the "weights and measures" <term>fenliang: the precise timing and proportions of internal alchemical energy</term> are clearly numbered and follow a logical sequence. Thus, in the final chapter of the lower volume, he summarized everything into a "Concluding Song" <note>original: *luanci*, a term from ancient poetry referring to a concluding summary that "orders" the preceding chaos</note> to open the "apertures" of the refined elixir and unlock the gateway to the Way. If a wise person is truly dedicated to learning, they should use their mind to carefully ponder and investigate these details. I have observed that the final chapters of works concerning "medicines" <note>alchemical ingredients</note> are often called "Luan" (Order/Concluding Song). This is similar to the "Luan" mentioned at the end of the *Guan Ju* in the *Analects*, or the sections marked "Luan says" in the *Songs of the South*. "Luan" means to bring order; its purpose is to express the logic that unifies the chapters and summarizes the essential points. When Lord Wei speaks of a "Concluding Song," he is using it in this sense. Therefore, the meaning of the text that follows describes the stages of the **alchemical work** <term>dangong: the internal process of refining energy</term> in a clear, sequential narrative. It is not like the first two volumes, where information is scattered and appears in different places. As for the "Song of the Cauldron and Vessel," its logic is clear and its stages of practice are exceptionally precise. It is the very marrow and spirit of the *Tally of the Three in Accordance with the Book of Changes*. Students should study and reflect upon it with great care, and they will naturally attain understanding.

<meta>This page serves as a commentary on the transition into the final volume of the "Tally of the Three." It explains the compassionate intent of the author, Wei Boyang, and begins the interpretation of the "Concluding Song," using celestial phenomena like the Milky Way and specific constellations as metaphors for the internal movements of energy during the alchemical process.</meta>

This chapter explains that since the ancient sages and worthies had already completed their own cultivation and ascended <note>original: "feisheng," referring to the Daoist concept of flying to heaven after achieving immortality</note>, they felt pity for later generations who loved the Way but were lost. Because of this, they created diagrams and texts to instruct the "uninitiated" <note>literally "the youthful and ignorant"</note>. How could they have expected that students would fail to investigate the root source? Those students spent their entire lives in confusion, leading to wasted time and the loss of their livelihoods—a situation Lord Wei <note>Wei Boyang</note> found deeply tragic. Consequently, he compiled and recorded the *Tally of the Three in Accordance with the Book of Changes*. The language is concise and the matters described are easy to understand; the stages and details are explained with great clarity. Furthermore, in the final volume, he summarized the essential "apertures" <note>the key points of the practice</note> to serve as a gateway to the Way. His legacy of teaching for later generations is truly profound.

# Of all models and images, none are greater than Heaven and Earth. The Dark Trench spans tens of thousands of miles. When the River Drum approaches the Star Marker, all the people are terrified.

○ All the myriad things that take shape through **energy** <term>Qi: the fundamental life force or breath</term> are "models and images." Among those things whose energy is clear and take the largest form, none surpass Heaven. Among those whose energy is turbid and take the largest substance, none surpass Earth. As the *Book of Changes* says: "Therefore, of all models and images, none are greater than Heaven and Earth." This is the meaning here. "Dark" refers to the color of the Heavens. "Trench" refers to a waterway. The "Dark Trench" refers to the "Heavenly River" <note>the Milky Way</note>. The Heavenly River begins between the constellations of the Tail and the Sieve and reaches the region of the Willow and the Star, dividing the middle of the sky. No one knows how many tens of thousands of miles long it truly is. However, this "Dark Trench" is called the Heavenly River in the sky, and the Yellow River on the earth; they are both connected by a single energy. Therefore, it is used here as a metaphor for the Dark Trench. In terms of the **alchemical path** <term>Dandao: the practice of internal alchemy</term>, this represents the boundary between the Yin and Yang within the cauldron and furnace. The "River Drum" <note>original: "Hegu," the constellation containing the star Altair</note> is a star at the edge of the Heavenly River. The *Astronomical Treatise of the Book of Han* states that the River Drum consists of three stars north of the Ox-Boy, governing military drums and axes. The "Star Marker" <note>original: "Xingji"</note> is one of the twelve stations of the Chinese zodiac, specifically located at the position of the "Ox" <note>the second earthly branch, *Chou*</note>. When the military imagery and killing energy of the River Drum star oversteps its bounds and approaches the Star Marker at the *Chou* position, it signifies that the nation will face the rise of military drums <note>war</note>. How could the people not be terrified? This is a metaphor for the "Metal-Fire" used in refining the elixir: when the movement begins from the direction of the "Ox" and "Mountain" <note>the *Chou* and *Gen* positions of the compass</note>, the **essence and energy** <term>jingqi: the concentrated vitality of the practitioner</term> within the cauldron and furnace naturally stir and rise.

# Now nine years of misfortune are suffered. The Emperor observes it, and the King retreats to reform himself.

# The shadow of the gnomon is neither advancing nor retreating.

<gloss>The character for "gnomon shadow" is pronounced *gui*. ○ The "shadow" refers to the image of the sun. "Neither" means none or without. "Advancing or retreating" is like rising and sinking. When the Yin and Yang of Heaven and Earth are in harmony, the rain and sun follow their proper seasons. If the sun's shadow loses its timing of rising and sinking, and there is constant gloomy, excessive rain, then there will surely be the disaster of a nine-year flood. In the timing of the "fire-phasing" <term>huohou: the precise timing of internal alchemical heat</term> for refining the elixir, if one does not know the measure of advancing and retreating, then the work of the **nine-cycle fire** <note>the stages of alchemical refinement</note> will be deficient. If there is too much Yin and too little Yang, the "Six Calamities" will occur, just as the loss of the sun's shadow leads to a nine-year flood disaster. As the *Preface to the Four Hundred Words of the Golden Elixir* says: "If the 'water-weight' is too high, it will overflow." The "Emperor" represents the Spirit. The "King" <note>or "Minister"</note> represents the energy. In the alchemical path, the Spirit is the ruler and the Energy is the servant. If the fire-phasing is mistaken and leads to the error of "overflowing water," the Original Spirit must observe the fault so that the Original Energy can return to its natural state.</gloss>

# The Key and Latch have their rises and falls; if improper, there is harm.
# Energy pursues its escape; the Yangtze and Huai rivers run dry, and the water flows out into the sea.

<gloss>The character for **Key** <term>Guanjian: literally the bolt and latch of a door, used here for the seals of the alchemical vessel</term> is pronounced *jian*. ○ The "Key and Latch" refer to a door’s lock; they are what secure its entryways. As stated in the first chapter of the middle volume: "The firmness of Heaven and the softness of Earth match and envelop one another"—this is the "Key and Latch" of the universe. If these "rises and falls" are not secure, there is the harm of "leaking energy." How could Heaven and Earth endure for long? In the **cauldron and furnace** <term>dinglu: the physical or meditative space where alchemy occurs</term> used for refining the elixir today, if the "Key and Latch" of the openings are uneven or not tightly sealed, the energy will be harmed and there will be the danger of it escaping. The "Yangtze" originates from Mount Min in the west; the "Huai" is a waterway that winds through Yangzhou in the south; both of these waters eventually empty into the sea. However, water is transformed from energy; this is why it circulates without end. If the "Key and Latch" of the cauldron are not secure, the energy leaks out and the water dries up, much like the waters of the Yangtze and Huai flowing into the sea. If there is no energy to drive the transformation, their sources will surely be exhausted. As the *Preface to the Four Hundred Words of the Golden Elixir* says: "If the 'fire-count' is excessive, it leads to dryness." This is the meaning. # The Female and Male of Heaven and Earth pace 
# back and forth between the *Zi* and *Wu* positions. *Yin* and *Shen* are the ancestors of Yin and Yang; exits and entries return to their start. Following the Dipper and the Star of Vibrating Brilliance, grasping the Balance to determine the Seven Stars.

<gloss>The word "Pacing" <note>original: paihuai</note> is pronounced *pei-huai*. "Return" <note>original: fu</note> is pronounced *fu-hou*. "Pacing" describes the appearance of not yet advancing. The **Zi** position <note>the North, representing midnight and the winter solstice</note> is the center of the Earth; it is the beginning of the birth of Yang and the end of the extreme of Yin. The **Wu** position <note>the South, representing noon and the summer solstice</note> is the center of Heaven; it is the start of the birth of Yin and the final tail of Yang. This means that when the two energies circulate to the *Zi* and *Wu* positions, their momentum must "pace" or pause without advancing, in order to exchange their Yin and Yang energies. When people today say that the moments of *Zi* and *Wu* are longer than other times, this is what they mean. Therefore it says: "The Female and Male of Heaven and Earth pace back and forth between the *Zi* and *Wu* positions." The **Yin** position <note>the Northeast, associated with dawn</note> is the "East" of Heaven and Earth; Yang energy expands and exits from here. The **Shen** position <note>the Southwest, associated with dusk</note> is the "West" of Heaven and Earth; Yin energy withdraws and enters from here. This means the "exiting and entering" of the two energies have *Yin* and *Shen* as their ancestral directions; they alternate and circulate, finishing and then beginning again like a ring without an end. Therefore it says: "*Yin* and *Shen* are the ancestors of Yin and Yang; exits and entries return to their start." Now, while Yin and Yang are the energies of Heaven and Earth, the Sun and Moon are the essences of Yin and Yang. The "exiting and entering" described here includes the movement of the Sun and Moon. Regarding the seven stars of the **Northern Dipper** <note>the Big Dipper</note>: stars one through four form the "Head," also called the **Gems of the Mechanism** <term>Xuanji: the rotating celestial center</term>. Stars five through seven form the "Handle," also called the **Jade Balance** <term>Yuheng: the star used for sighting and measurement</term>. "Vibrating Brilliance" <note>original: Zhaoyao</note> is the star at the very tip of the Dipper's handle...</gloss>

Therefore, the Way of Heaven and the Way of the Elixir share the same fundamental principle. Students should examine this deeply.

# The Second Chapter (to the right)

This chapter discusses the Way of Heaven and Earth’s creation to serve as a metaphor for the laws and measures of the cauldron and furnace. In the cultivation of the elixir, the cauldron and furnace serve as the **Substance** <note>original: ti</note>, the medicinal ingredients serve as the **Function** <note>original: yong</note>, and the Fire-count serves as the **Method** <note>original: fa</note>. When these three are fully prepared, the Way may be hoped for. Thus, it is explained here.

## **Ascending to cook on the Pot-Mountain; fierce fire is spread below.**
<gloss>The character for **Pot** <note>original: zeng</note> is pronounced *zeng*. The character for **Harmony** <note>original: he</note> is in the falling tone. ○ "To cook" <note>original: ao</note> refers to what the ninth chapter of the previous volume called the "Cooking Axis." Here it is a metaphor for the cauldron. "Pot-Mountain" refers to the furnace and stove. This means the cauldron is raised onto the furnace, and a fierce fire is set beneath it.</gloss>

## **The White Tiger leads the way in front; the Green Fluid follows in harmony behind.**
<gloss>The **White Tiger** <term>Baihu: the symbol of the West and Metal</term> is the Essence of Metal; it refers to **Lead**. The **Green Fluid** <term>Cangye: the fluid of the East and Wood</term> is the Fluid of Wood; it refers to **Mercury**. This means using "True Lead" to lead at the front, while "Spiritual Mercury" follows in harmony behind.</gloss>

## **The Vermilion Bird soars and plays; its flying colors show five hues.**
<gloss>The **Vermilion Bird** <term>Zhuque: the symbol of the South and Fire</term> is the Essence of Fire. The "five hues" represent the presence of the **Five Elements** <term>Wuxing: wood, fire, earth, metal, and water</term> within the cauldron. This describes the soaring advance and retreat of the Fire-tally, its colors flying and manifesting the five hues.</gloss>

## **Encountering the net that is cast, it is pressed down and cannot rise. A cry is heard, most sorrowful—it is the tomb of the Infant.**

## **The mother is overturned and enters the boiling cauldron; her feathers are broken and damaged.**

<gloss>The character for **cry** <note>original: ao</note> is pronounced *ao*. ○ The **White Tiger** and the **Green Fluid** <note>metaphors for Lead and Mercury</note> are sealed and secured within the tripod vessel. ## **Before the water clock has passed the half-mark, fish scales and bristling manes arise. The images of five colors dazzle, changing without a constant master. Bubbling and boiling, they race through the cauldron, surging violently without rest. Connected and piled up, interlocking like dog teeth. <gloss>The character for **manes** <note>original: lie</note> is pronounced *lie*. **Dazzle** <note>original: xuan</note> is pronounced *xuan*. **Bubbling** <note>original: jue</note> is *jue*. **Boiling** <note>original: fei</note> is *fei*. **Piled** <note>original: lei</note> is *lei*. This describes the White Tiger and Green Fluid being cooked by the Vermilion Bird; before even half the time on the **water clock** <term>louke: an ancient clepsydra used to time the "Fire-count"</term> has passed, their forms begin to rise up like the scales of fish and dragons or the manes of horses. "Dazzling" refers to the brightness of the fire. Because the cauldron contains the energy of the **Five Elements** <term>Wuxing: Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, Water</term>, its light dazzles with five colors, shifting constantly without a single dominant hue. "Bubbling" describes the appearance of flowing water; it means the Lead and Mercury are simmering in the vessel, their momentum like surging, boiling water that races without stopping. "Interlocking" refers to the spurs of a rooster; it describes the shapes connecting and piling up, crossing over one another like dog teeth or rooster spurs. "Beautiful stones" <note>original: ligan</note> are stones that are second only to jade. **Stalactites** <note>original: zhongru</note> are a medicinal mineral produced in copper mines; they look like hollow goose feathers, are white in color, and hang downward. This means that as the medicinal ingredients congeal in the cauldron, they take the shape of midwinter icicles, crossing up and down like beautiful stones and stalactites. "Towering" refers to rocky earth-covered mountains. "Intermixed" means varied. This describes the state of the accumulation: like the jagged layers of earth and stone on a mountain, they pile up and support one another within the cauldron. Although this section describes "external" appearances, the "internal" reality follows the same principle. The method of the Elixir uses the external to illustrate the internal, and the internal to illustrate the external, using them as mutual metaphors.</gloss>

The **Twenty-Eight Lunar Mansions** <term>Ershiba Xiu: ancient Chinese star groups used as a celestial map</term> are distributed across the four directions. In the East, the seven mansions—Horn, Neck, Root, Room, Heart, Tail, and Winnowing Basket—are called the **Azure Dragon**. In the North, the seven mansions—Dipper, Ox, Girl, Emptiness, Rooftop, Encampment, and Wall—are called the **Black Warrior** <note>the Tortoise and Snake</note>. In the South, the seven mansions—Well, Ghost, Willow, Star, Extended Net, Wings, and Chariot—are called the **Vermilion Bird**. 

Therefore, the Azure Dragon belongs to the East. The "Room" is an Eastern mansion. The number "six" refers to the degrees of the Room mansion. In terms of season, it is Spring; in terms of objects, it is flowers; in the **Trigrams** <term>Bagua: eight symbols used in Taoist cosmology</term>, it is *Zhen* <note>Thunder/Spring</note>; in direction, it is East; in the **Earthly Branches** <term>Dizhi: the twelve divisions of the day/year</term>, it is the hour of the Rabbit <note>5–7 AM</note>. The White Tiger belongs to the West. "Hairy Head" <note>Mao</note> is a Western mansion. The number "seven" refers to the degrees of the Hairy Head mansion. In terms of season, it is Autumn; in terms of objects, it is the awn <note>the beard of grain</note>; in the Trigrams, it is *Dui* <note>Lake/Autumn</note>; in direction, it is West; in the Earthly Branches, it is the hour of the Rooster <note>5–7 PM</note>. Thus it is said: "The White Tiger is in the seventh degree of Hairy Head; Autumn awns are in the West at the hour of the Rooster." 

The Vermilion Bird belongs to the South. "Extended Net" <note>Zhang</note> is a Southern mansion. The number "two" refers to the degrees of the Extended Net mansion. In terms of season, it is Summer; it resides in the height of Yang; in the Trigrams, it is *Li* <note>Fire</note>; in direction, it is South; in the Earthly Branches, it is the hour of the Horse <note>11 AM–1 PM</note>. Thus it is said: "The Vermilion Bird is in the second degree of the Extended Net; at the height of Yang, it is in the South at the hour of the Horse." 

The "three" refers to these three: the Dragon, Tiger, and Bird. "Coming to pay court" means they assemble at the **North Pole Palace** <note>the center of the sky</note>; in the Way of the Elixir, this refers to the center of the **cauldron and furnace** <term>dinglu: the vessel of transformation</term>. This means these three substances—Azure Dragon, White Tiger, and Vermilion Bird—all gather and meet within the vessel, just like family members and close partners living together in one house. Thus it is said: "The three all come to pay court; family members become close partners." The numbers "six" and "seven" used here are the "completion numbers" of Water and Fire; "two" is the "generation number" of Fire. They are simply used to capture the essence of the "One Water and Two Fires"; one should not be stubbornly literal about them.</gloss>

# Chapter Four (Conclusion)

This chapter explains that the Great Way <term>Dadao: The ultimate underlying principle of the universe</term> arises from nature <note>original: ziran</note> and does not rely on forced or artificial effort. Therefore, its effectiveness is as divine as described. This Way remains constant and unchanging, even through thousands of generations. A student must investigate it thoroughly and contemplate it with precision. Through the true accumulation of effort over a long period, the mind and spirit will naturally achieve a sudden awakening and find the correct thread. One must not count the months and years, becoming diligent at the start but lazy at the end. As long as a single breath remains, this ambition must not slacken; only then can one be called a person who studies the Way. Furthermore, during the process of transmission, do not show this to those who are not the right people; it should only be shared with those of good character. Note that the previous three chapters were originally one continuous flow of energy. They are divided into three now simply to clarify the layers of meaning and follow a proper rhythm. The reader should examine this carefully.

# The cauldron is a circle of three-five inches and one minute; the mouth is four-eight and two inches; the lips are one foot two in length; the thickness is even.

"Circle" signifies completeness. "Three" refers to Water being one and Fire being two; combined, they form three. "Five" refers to the number of Earth itself. This corresponds to Chapter Eleven of the first volume, which says: "The numbers of the north and south <note>literally: Zi and Wu</note> combine to three, and the center <note>literally: Wu and Ji</note> is called five." This means that within the cauldron <term>Dingqi: The vessel used for alchemical transformation, representing both a physical pot and the practitioner's body</term> are the medicinal substances of perfected Water, Fire, and Earth. Furthermore, the Three Realms and Five Elements <note>the fundamental forces of wood, fire, earth, metal, and water</note> are all fully contained within it. Therefore, it is called a "circle of three-five."

The Records of Han <note>original: Han Zhi; a reference to the Book of Han's treatises on measurement</note> state: "An inch is a method." It means there are rules and techniques to follow. Now, when alchemical books <term>Danshu: Scriptures on the Elixir</term> speak of feet and inches, they should also be interpreted as methods or symbolic standards. "One" refers to the One Breath <term>Yiqi: The primordial energy of the universe</term>. This means the measurements of "three-five" are actually divisions of the One Breath. Thus, it says: "an inch and one minute."

The cauldron is used to store the medicinal substances and contain the fire talismans <note>symbolic instructions for regulating heat</note>, which is why it has a "mouth." The Four Images <term>Sixiang: Green Dragon, White Tiger, Vermilion Bird, and Black Tortoise</term> are contained within it, and the Eight Trigrams <term>Bagua: The fundamental symbols of reality in the I Ching</term> are arranged on its outside. Thus, it says: "the mouth is four-eight." "Two" refers to the Two Rituals <term>Liangyi: Yin and Yang</term>. Since the cauldron has a mouth, it must have lips; the upper and lower lips are measured to symbolize these Two Rituals. Thus, it says: "two inches for the lips."

"Length" <note>original: chang</note> implies "constancy" <note>also pronounced chang</note>. "One-two" refers to the single and dual breaths. This means the constant measure within the cauldron is the coming and going of the one and two breaths. Thus, it says: "one foot two in length." 

The energy that is light, clear, and floating is Yang and is considered "thin." The energy that is heavy, turbid, and sinking is Yin and is considered "thick." This means that the two energies within the cauldron—Yin and Yang, floating and sinking—are balanced and equal. Thus, it says: "the thickness is even." From here until the final chapter, this section is known as the "Song of the Cauldron."

<meta>This page continues the "Song of the Cauldron" from the previous page, moving from the external measurements of the vessel to the internal alignment of the practitioner's body and the symbolic timing of the alchemical process. # The seat is warm and the shadow hangs above; Yang rushes below. The head and tail are martial; the middle is civil.

"Belly" <note>referring to the final line of the previous page: "The belly is aligned at three-two"</note> refers to the belly of the human body. "Three" refers to the upper, middle, and lower regions <term>Sanjiao: The Triple Burner or three functional energy centers of the body</term>. This means that when the belly of the cauldron is properly settled, these three regions are unified and balanced throughout the body, without leaning or tilting. The method for establishing the cauldron-vessel is to align the mouth of the cauldron with the "heart" of the cauldron, and then the "heart" of the cauldron must face the navel. "Sitting" means to settle into one's proper position. "Hanging" means to manifest an image. This indicates that the seating position for settling the furnace and establishing the cauldron should manifest an image that is warm, peaceful, and upright. Thus, it says: "the belly is aligned at three, and the seat hangs warm."

The *Book of Documents* <note>original: Hong Fan; "The Great Plan" chapter of the Classic of History</note> states: "Water is said to moisten downwards; Fire is said to flame upwards." This describes the constant nature of these elements. However, within the cauldron of the Alchemical Way <term>Dandao: The path of internal alchemy</term>, Water is placed above and Fire rushes below. This is the reversal of Yin and Yang, representing the state of "Already Fording" <note>original: Jiji; the 63rd hexagram of the I Ching, symbolizing perfect completion or harmony</note> where Water and Fire aid one another. Therefore, it is called "Yin is above, and Yang rushes below." Xiao Chongxu said: "Yin dwells above and Yang dwells below; the Yang energy rises first, and the Yin energy follows." This is the meaning here.

"Zi and Wu" <note>the North/South or Midnight/Noon axes</note> are the head and tail of Yin and Yang. "Mao and You" <note>the East/West or Dawn/Dusk axes</note> are the middle points of Yin and Yang. Zi represents the head of Yang’s birth and the tail of Yin’s extremity; Wu represents the head of Yin’s birth and the tail of Yang’s extremity. This is the exchange of the two energies, and therefore it is considered "Martial" <term>Wuhuo: Intense, focused "Martial Fire" used for active transformation</term>. Mao and You represent the balance of Yin and Yang, where cold and heat are halved; this is the peaceful harmony of the two energies, and therefore it is considered "Civil" <term>Wenhuo: Gentle, steady "Civil Fire" used for nourishing the elixir</term>. Thus, it is called "the head and tail are martial, and the middle is civil." These are the principles of the Alchemical Way and the Heavenly Way alike. One need not search far for them elsewhere.

# Beginning at seventy and ending at two decades; two hundred and sixty are well-harmonized.

<gloss>The character for "harmonized" (yun) is pronounced "yun." "Three decades" <note>original: Sanxun</note> refers to thirty days. If thirty, seventy, and two hundred and sixty are combined, they equal three hundred and sixty days <note>The verse says "two decades" (20), but the gloss calculates using "thirty" to reach 360, a common variation in symbolic numerology</note>. This corresponds to the number of a full cycle of Heaven in one year. This is what Peng Zhenyi meant when he said that Lord Wei <note>Wei Boyang, author of the Cantong Qi</note> wished to create a harmonious literary rhythm and thus divided the numbers for the text.</gloss> Generally, the period for "Warm Nourishing" <term>Wenyang: The stage of gently incubating the alchemical elixir</term> begins with one hundred days to establish the foundation and ends after one year to reach full completion. However, during this time, one must constantly inspect and be mindful at every moment. If there is even a slight error, the Elixir will not be complete. Therefore, during the year of warm nourishing, one must be skilled at harmonizing the elements so that the stages are aligned without loss.

# Yin fire is white; Yellow Sprout is lead. The "Two-Sevens" gather to assist the Person.

This says that Yang fire and Yin fire—one rising and one falling—gather and surround the center to support and protect the Alchemical Embryo in the Central Palace. Thus, it says: "the two-sevens gather to assist the person."

## The *Seal of the Unity of the Three* provides a broad overview, but it cannot be perfectly uniform. It speaks in a general way, and the subtle details are not yet fully prepared, appearing broad and only roughly sketched. Now, I have further composed and recorded this to fill in the omissions, polish the deep and obscure passages, and link the concepts together so that the meaning is balanced and the objective is not contradicted. Therefore, I have written this again, titled the "Three Categories," so that the inner nature of the *Great Change* is fully expressed.

<gloss>"Fiber" is pronounced *xian*. "To polish" is pronounced *run*. "Roughly sketched" is pronounced *fangfu*. "Again" is pronounced *fu*.

"Three" <note>original: can</note> means three. "Unity" <note>original: tong</note> means to penetrate or connect. "Seal" <note>original: qi</note> means to tally or agree. This means that the *Great Change* <note>the I Ching</note>, the philosophy of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi, and the work of the Furnace and Cauldron are all three connected and in agreement with the Way. However, since these three use the *Weekly Change* <note>Zhou Yi</note> of the three sages as the foundation, it is called the *Weekly Change: Seal of the Unity of the Three*.

When Lord Wei <note>Wei Boyang</note> wrote this book, he set forth a broad overview of the Great Way, yet he feared leaking the mysterious mechanics of heaven too clearly. Therefore, he could not be perfectly uniform or detailed, but instead narrated in a general fashion. The subtle and minute meanings were certainly not fully detailed. Furthermore, fearing that later students would find the broad and sketchy language of the *Seal* difficult to understand, he composed the verses of the preceding chapters again to fill in what was missing and polish the obscure text. This ensures that the essential meanings within the three sections are linked and reach one another, making the intent naturally balanced. This allows the student to have a clear direction and avoid falling into error.

Therefore, by writing this and calling it the "Three Categories," the nature and characteristics of the *Great Change* can be fully expressed, and the meaning of the *Seal of the Unity of the Three* can be made clear. The text below further discusses these three categories and the nature of the *Change*.

Note: Regarding the word "Three" in "Three Categories," some editions write "Five." Master Quanyang says: "The Three Categories refer to the *Great Change*, the Yellow-Lao philosophy, and the Furnace and Cauldron; the Yin and Yang transformations of these three are similar to one another." Ever since Peng Zhenyi drew the "Diagram of the Five Positions," people have interpreted this as the "Five Elements" <note>Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, and Water</note>. This interpretation has been followed to this day without anyone correcting it. However, if one examines the text later in this chapter, it says: "The three ways follow the one; all emerge from the same path," and "Arranged in three branches, their stems are connected; they emerge together but have different names." From these phrases, it is clearly visible that it refers to Three Categories, not Five. 

Furthermore, the words "Three Categories" <note>San Xiang Lei</note> also carry the meaning of the book's title: Three is "Three" <note>Can</note>, Categories is "Seal" <note>Qi</note>, and "Similar" is "Unity" <note>Tong</note>. This argument by Master Yu deeply captures the essence, and so I record it here to inform my fellow seekers.</gloss>

# The practice of the furnace and fire truly has a basis; the three paths originate from the One and emerge from the same route.

The *Change* <note>the I Ching</note> says: "One Yin and one Yang are called the Way." It also says: "The firm and the yielding push against each other, producing change and transformation." This is the true nature of the *Great Change*. The transformations and nourishment that flow through the Three Powers <note>Heaven, Earth, and Humanity</note> each follow their proper measures without overstepping. Therefore it is said: "The nature of the *Great Change* follows its proper measures."

The Yellow Emperor said: "Observe the Way of Heaven and grasp the workings of Heaven." Laozi spoke of "the depth of contained virtue" and "the Valley Spirit never dies." This is the study of Yellow-Lao <note>a school of thought named after the Yellow Emperor and Laozi, foundational to early Daoism</note>. It should be used to investigate the source of things and be mastered to govern the body and mind. Therefore it is said: "The practice of Yellow-Lao is investigated and can be mastered."

Boiling and refining <term>lead and mercury: metaphorical or literal substances in alchemy representing the polarized energies of Yin and Yang</term> and compounding <term>golden cinnabar: the legendary elixir of immortality</term> is known as the <term>External Elixir of the furnace and fire: the physical laboratory practice of alchemy</term>. This is used to transform mundane matter. This is not baseless talk; it is a matter that truly has a historical and practical basis. Thus it is said: "The practice of the furnace and fire truly has a basis."

Though these three—the *Great Change*, Yellow-Lao, and the Furnace—each take different paths to achieve creation and transformation, their source originates from the single gate of the Way. Therefore it is said: "The three paths originate from the One; all emerge from the same route."

I humbly note: The External Elixir of the furnace and fire has existed since ancient times. However, it was not until Liu An, the King of Huainan, that its practice was widely transmitted. Now Lord Wei <note>Wei Boyang, the purported author of the text</note> also includes it here rather than discarding it. For when gold and mercury are refined into the Elixir, at the minor level they can transform the five metals into <term>yellow and white: a traditional term for gold and silver</term> to provide the funds to support the Way. 

At the major level, these elixirs can benefit the <term>Internal Elixir: the spiritual and energetic elixir cultivated within the practitioner's own body</term> and supplement any deficiencies in the "fire times" <note>the specific timing and intensity of focus required in meditation</note>. This is truly a mysterious and subtle thing. 

Alas, the people of the world do not understand the correct path and do not encounter the true oral instructions. They only remember the superficial words written on paper or listen to the reckless talk of "blind teachers." Consequently, they attempt to burn and refine ordinary mercury and ordinary cinnabar, along with various metals and minerals. Over years and months, they exhaust their fuel and waste their wealth. 

This leads to the total loss of family property, leaving wives and children cold and hungry. Or, they ingest these toxic concoctions hoping to extend their lives, but instead lose their lives. Instances of this kind recorded in the annals are too numerous to count. The Perfected One Lü <note>Lü Dongbin, a famous Daoist immortal</note> says in his <insert>Song of the Shattered Clay Pot</insert>: "Not knowing that the Returned Elixir is fundamentally without substance, how foolish it is to swallow gold and stone instead!" Another ancient song says: "The Returned Elixir is that which produces substance from the substanceless; do not trouble yourself with ordinary cinnabar and mercury." These are all ultimate truths.

Therefore, whether it be the Internal or External Elixir, that which produces substance from the substanceless is true; that which produces substance from physical substance is false. There is no need for further detailed distinction. Those in the world who love the External Elixir think they can create gold and silver to become rich, or transform the mundane body to become an immortal. Thus the greedy rush toward it like madmen. They little realize that the External Elixir's ability to create gold and silver is meant to provide funds for supporting the Way and practicing charity; it is not for the sake of satisfying the greedy. 

As for its ability to "touch off" the Internal Elixir: when a practitioner of internal refinement reaches the stage of "nurturing in the chamber" for a year, if there is a slight failure in harmony, the meditative fire times will be deficient. In such a case, the External Elixir is used only as a supplement. If one lacks this external substance, simply maintaining a pure and unified focus for nine years can also complete the work; one does not rely on the laboratory elixir alone. 

People today who ingest External Elixirs have not even a fraction of internal refinement within their bodies. How could their soft and fragile organs withstand the heavy metals and mercury that have been subjected to fire? Moreover, the formulas they use are not the correct ones, and the medicines are not the true medicines. It is only natural that they fail a thousand or ten thousand times, shortening their natural lifespan. How they delude themselves! Is it not a pity? Therefore, the student should seek the Ultimate Way and must not act out of greed or delusion. Yet, one should also not "stop eating because of a cough" <note>an idiom meaning to give up a necessary pursuit because of a minor risk</note> and abandon the Way entirely. Only accumulate...

# The branches, stalks, flowers, leaves, and fruits spread out, but they are anchored in the root and trunk; they do not lose their original nature. What is spoken from a sincere heart is examined and without error.
