# Therefore the *Book of Changes* governs the "Heart of Heaven"; the *Fu* (Return) hexagram establishes the beginning.

The *Book of Changes* is defined by the interaction of one Yin and one Yang. The "Heart of Heaven" refers to the center of the North, the position of *Zi* <note>The hour of midnight (11 PM – 1 AM) and the direction of North.</note>. The *Fu* (Return) hexagram corresponds to the eleventh lunar month. The structure of this hexagram sits precisely in the center of the Northern *Zi* position.

Its energy corresponds to the Winter Solstice. Shao Kangjie <note>Shao Yong (1011–1077), a famous philosopher and cosmologist of the Song Dynasty.</note> wrote in his *Songs of Striking the Earth*: "The Winter Solstice is the half-point of *Zi*; the Heart of Heaven never alters or moves." This is the meaning. Zhu Huian <note>Zhu Xi (1130–1200), the preeminent scholar of Neo-Confucianism.</note> considered this poem by Shao to be the very best on the subject. 

To explain further: the Start of Winter occurs at the beginning of the tenth month. "Light Snow" is in the middle of the tenth month. "Heavy Snow" is at the beginning of the eleventh month. The "Winter Solstice" is in the middle of the eleventh month. "Lesser Cold" is at the start of the twelfth month, and "Greater Cold" is in the middle of the twelfth month. Since the Winter Solstice is the "half-point of *Zi*," it is exactly the midpoint of the eleventh month. People often say that the midnight hour is the solstice because the first half of the midnight period belongs to the previous day’s cycle. Most modern practitioners of the <term>Five Elements</term> <note>The theory of Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, and Water used to describe all cosmic and biological cycles.</note> do not understand this. However, the "Count" always begins at this specific point without the slightest deviation; this is why it is called the "Heart of Heaven." 

Now, Wei Gong <note>Wei Boyang, the legendary 2nd-century author of the *Cantong qi*, the "Ancestor of all Alchemical Books."</note> says that the *Changes* governs the Heart of Heaven and the *Fu* hexagram establishes the beginning because the Yang energy is secretly sprouting during the month of "Early Winter" (the tenth month), which is the month that governs pure Yin. It begins at the bottom of the **Kun** hexagram <note>The hexagram of Pure Yin, consisting of six broken lines.</note>. Once a single line of Yang has accumulated, it transforms into the **Fu** hexagram <note>The hexagram of "Return," consisting of one solid Yang line at the bottom and five broken Yin lines above.</note>. 

Most people know that the tenth month corresponds to *Kun*, and by the eleventh month, the bottom-most of the five Yin lines changes into a single Yang line to become *Fu*. However, they do not realize that the Winter Solstice in the eleventh month is not an abrupt end; the "First Yang" does not simply appear out of thin air to create the "Return." In reality, during the "Light Snow" period of the tenth month, the Yang has already been born within the bottom line of the *Kun* hexagram. However, within a single day or a single month, it only grows by one-thirtieth at a time. It must accumulate for a full month until the Winter Solstice of the eleventh month before that single solid line is "full" and becomes the *Fu* hexagram. 

Yet, this is all a metaphor. In a year, the Winter Solstice is the "Return." In a month, the New Moon is the "Return." In a day, the midnight hour is the "Return." These are all used solely to illustrate the internal **Creation** <term>Creation (Zaohua): The natural transformative power of the universe, which the alchemist replicates within their own body.</term> within the body. One must not be stubbornly attached to literal years, months, days, or hours! 

The *Cuixu Pian* <note>The "Green Emptiness Treatise" by the alchemist Cui Xufan.</note> says: "A month of thirty days is the same as a single day; the method of refining the Elixir matches the work of Heaven." Since a year is like a month, a month is like a day, and a day is like an hour, then years become months, months become days, and days become hours. Within a single hour, there is naturally a mechanism for the "Return of the First Yang." This mechanism does not depend on the literal Winter Solstice, the New Moon, or the midnight hour. Unless one has deeply mastered the secrets of Yin and Yang, they will never know this "Dark Mechanism," as it is profoundly hidden.

# The First Son succeeds the Father’s body; the foundation is established through the Mother.

When the Father, **Qian** <note>The hexagram of Pure Yang (☰), representing the creative principle and the Heavens.</note>, descends to interact with the first line of the Mother, **Kun** <note>The hexagram of Pure Yin (☷), representing the receptive principle and the Earth.</note>, they form **Zhen** <note>The hexagram (☳) consisting of one Yang line at the bottom and two Yin lines above.</note>. # Waning and waxing correspond to the musical pitches; ascending and descending follow the pivot of the Big Dipper.

The period from the hour of *Zi* to *Si* <note>Midnight to Noon</note> is "waxing" (growth), while the period from *Wu* to *Hai* <note>Noon to Midnight</note> is "waning" (decrease). The phrase "waning and waxing correspond to the musical pitches" refers to the ancient twelve pitch-pipes <note>A system of standardized pipes used to calibrate musical scales and the ritual calendar.</note>. Within the twelve months of a single year, one pipe is changed each month, cycling through all twelve pitches. The "waning and waxing" of the **Fire Phasing** <term>Fire Phasing (Huohou): The precise timing and intensity of the internal breath and heat used to "cook" the Elixir.</term> within our own bodies is exactly like this.

Movement from the bottom upward is "ascending," and movement from the top downward is "descending." The phrase "ascending and descending follow the pivot of the Big Dipper" refers to the way the handle of the Dipper shifts its position every hour within the twelve hours of a day, completing a full circuit of the twelve earthly branches in twenty-four hours. The ascent and descent of the Fire Phasing in our own bodies is exactly like this. 

The *Zhixuan pian* <note>The "Pointing to the Mystery Treatise," likely referring to works attributed to the immortal Lü Dongbin.</note> says: "The refining process in the Nine Depths shifts the musical pipes; the wise man watches the handle of the Dipper turn in the vast heavens." These are merely images used as metaphors. One does not actually use the physical length of musical pipes or the literal direction of the stars to determine the timing of the work.

On the third day of the lunar month, the moon emerges at the position of *Geng* <note>The direction of West/Metal in the decimal cycle.</note>. The "Three-fold **Zhen**" <note>The Zhen hexagram ☳ representing the first appearance of light/energy.</note> receives the energy of *Geng* in the West.

If we speak of this in terms of the **Fire Phasing** <term>Fire Phasing (Huohou): The careful timing of breath and concentration used to cultivate the internal Elixir.</term> within our own bodies, this is the time of which it is said: "The **River Chariot** <term>River Chariot (Heche): An alchemical term for the circulation of internal energy, specifically the 'ascending' path up the spine.</term> does not dare to pause or stop for even a moment."

### The Toad and the Spirit of the Rabbit. The Sun and Moon share no equal brilliance.

The **Toad** <note>In Chinese mythology, a three-legged toad lives in the moon, representing the moon’s essence.</note> is the essence of the moon. The **Spirit of the Rabbit** <note>The "Jade Rabbit" is another dweller of the moon, often depicted pounding the elixir of immortality; here it refers to the light the moon receives from the sun.</note> is the light of the sun. That the "Sun and Moon share no equal brilliance" means that the sun shines in the day, while the moon shines at night. When the sun rises, the moon sets; when the moon rises, the sun sets. Day and night they take turns shining, and their appearing and disappearing are like the stretching and rolling of a scroll. How is the breathing of a human being any different from this? Do we not see that the **Yellow Court Classic** <term>Yellow Court Classic (Huangting Jing): A foundational Daoist meditation text focused on visualizing the spirits within the body's organs.</term> says: "Exhaling the sun and inhaling the moon, the breath preserves the Elixir." Inhalation and exhalation are themselves the sun and the moon.

***

### The Toad observes the hexagram stages; the Rabbit spits out the birthing light.

In the methods of the Elixir, the first half of the month is considered **Yang** <note>Active, masculine, and growing energy.</note>, belonging to the hexagrams **Zhen**, **Dui**, and **Qian**. The second half of the month belongs to **Yin** <note>Passive, feminine, and receding energy.</note>, belonging to the hexagrams **Sun**, **Gen**, and **Kun**. Therefore it is said: "The Toad observes the hexagram stages." The moon is the Great Yin, while the sun is the Great Yang. The Yang governs "spitting out" (exhaling/emitting), while the Yin governs "taking in" (inhaling/receiving). The moon originally has no light of its own; it becomes white only by receiving the light of the sun. Thus it is said: "The Rabbit spits out the birthing light."

***

### Seven and eight—the path is finished. Bending and folding, it descends downward.

"Seven and eight" refers to the fifteenth day <note>7 + 8 = 15, the date of the full moon.</note>. The **Yang Fire** rises from the hexagram **Zhen** (the 3rd day) and continues until the fifteenth, where it reaches the state of **Pure Qian** (the Full Moon). At this point, the timing of the first half of the month is full. The momentum has reached its limit; the path is at its most "perilous" peak. Therefore, it must "bend and fold," wheeling around to begin its low descent. The *Book of the Jade Mushroom* by Chen Chaoyuan says: "Inside the nine-fold city, the **Dragon Chariot** sets out; before the twelve-story tower, the **Tiger Carriage** returns." This is exactly what is meant here.

***

### On the sixteenth, the turn takes command; the Sun trigram appears at dawn in the position of Xin.

When the moon reaches the sixteenth day, the "dark spirit" <note>The waning portion of the moon.</note> is born. At dawn, the moon is in the Western position of **Xin** <note>The eighth Celestial Stem, associated with the West and Metal.</note>. The light has just begun to fail. Its image is like the hexagram **Sun** <note>The hexagram (☴) representing "Wind" or "Gently Penetrating," marking the first entrance of a Yin line at the bottom of the structure.</note>, which corresponds to the "Sun hexagram receiving Xin." Speaking in terms of the **Fire Phasing** within our own bodies, this is the moment when the Yin begins to receive the Yang, the time when the path turns and heads back.

# The Phases End and Give Way to the Next; The Body Continues and the Dragon is Reborn

**Lord Wei** <note>Wei Boyang, the 2nd-century author of the *Cantong qi*, the "Ancestor of Alchemical Books."</note> divided the thirty days of a single month into six stages.
*   From the first dawn to the fifth day is the first stage, belonging to **Zhen** (☳).
*   From the sixth to the tenth day is the second stage, belonging to **Dui** (☱).
*   From the eleventh to the fifteenth day is the third stage, belonging to **Qian** (☰).
*   From the sixteenth to the twentieth day is the fourth stage, belonging to **Sun** (☴).
*   From the twenty-first to the twenty-fifth day is the fifth stage, belonging to **Gen** (☶).
*   From the twenty-sixth to the thirtieth day is the sixth stage, belonging to **Kun** (☷).

Once these six stages are completed, the sun and moon meet in **conjunction** <note>The "Shuo" or New Moon, where the sun and moon occupy the same celestial longitude.</note>. After this, the **Yang** energy receives the "seed" from the **Yin**, and the cycle transforms back into **Zhen** <note>The first trigram of the waxing phase, representing the "first sprout" of light.</note> once again.

<summary>Yu Yan details the final stages of the lunar month (the 23rd and 30th days), correlating them with the Gen and Kun trigrams to illustrate the completion of the "Yin Tally" or cooling phase of alchemy. He then summarizes the entire month as a six-stage cycle that eternally resets.</summary>

# Zhen is the Dragon: One Yang Moves Beneath Two Yin

**Zhen** (☳) represents the **Dragon**. One **Yang** line <note>The solid line at the bottom of the trigram.</note> moves beneath two **Yin** lines <note>The two broken lines above.</note>; this is the nature of **Zhen**. Beneath the heavy depths of the abyss, there is a living thing moving—is this not the Dragon?

## Ren and Gui Match with Jia and Yi; Qian and Kun Encompass the Beginning and the End

**Qian** (☰) <note>Pure Yang/Heaven</note> receives the Celestial Stems **Jia** and **Ren**. **Kun** (☷) <note>Pure Yin/Earth</note> receives **Yi** and **Gui**. Therefore, it is said that "**Ren** and **Gui** match with **Jia** and **Yi**." The ten Celestial Stems begin with **Jia** and **Yi** and end with **Ren** and **Gui**. Thus, it is said that "**Qian** and **Kun** encompass the beginning and the end." 

This system of "Matching the Stems" is an image used for the **Fire Phasing** <term>Fire Phasing (Huohou): The precise timing and regulation of internal heat and breath used to "cook" and refine the elixir within the body.</term>. The "adding" and "subtracting" of the internal fire is no different from the waxing and waning of the moon. If we distribute the six trigrams across a single month, we see the following:
*   The **Zhen** (☳) image corresponds to the third day, when the moon appears in the **Geng** position (West).
*   The **Dui** (☱) image corresponds to the First Quarter, when the moon is seen in the **Ding** position (South).
*   The **Qian** (☰) image corresponds to the Full Moon, when the moon's light is full in the **Jia** position (East).
*   The **Sun** (☴) image <note>The trigram for "Wind," symbolizing the start of waning.</note> corresponds to the sixteenth day, when the moon begins to fade in the **Xin** position (West).
*   The **Gen** (☶) image corresponds to the Last Quarter, when the moon shrinks in the **Bing** position (South).
*   The **Kun** (☷) image corresponds to the Dark Moon, when the light vanishes in the **Yi** position (East).

However, these images are merely borrowed to discuss the progression and regression of the **Fire Phasing** within the six trigrams of our own bodies. One should not literally believe this refers to a physical thirty-day month. How do we know this? According to the laws of the calendar, days and nights vary in length. During the winter, when days are short, the sun and moon meet and part at different times and positions. In the twelve months of the year, the third-day moon will not always appear exactly at the **Geng** position, nor will the full moon always appear exactly at **Jia**. The quarters and the full moon do not always fall perfectly on the 8th, 15th, or 23rd days. 

Now, **Lord Wei** <note>Wei Boyang, the legendary author of the "Seal of the Unity of the Three" (Cantong qi).</note> says that the moon appears at **Geng** on the third day, and on the sixteenth day it begins to turn, with **Sun** and **Xin** appearing. This refers specifically to the time of the spring and autumn equinoxes, when day and night are perfectly balanced. He is simply "taking an image" <note>Using a standardized symbolic model to explain a complex internal process.</note>. It does not mean one must literally start the "fire" only when the moon appears in the West.

The student should simply observe the waxing and waning of the moon and seek its equivalent within their own body. When the single **Yang** is born within the body, that is the **Zhen** image of the third-day moon. When the second **Yang** grows, that is the **Dui** image of the eighth-day quarter moon. When the three **Yang** are full, that is the **Qian** image of the fifteenth-day full moon. When the first **Yin** is born, that is the **Sun** image of the sixteenth-day waning moon. When the second **Yin** grows, that is the **Gen** image of the twenty-third-day moon. When the three **Yin** are complete, that is the **Kun** image of the thirtieth-day dark moon. How could one be restricted by the literal directions of the moon's rising or the mathematical lengths of the calendar?

### A Separate Explanation of These Four Images to Instruct Future Generations

The "Four Images" refer to the numbers Seven, Eight, Nine, and Six. As mentioned previously, Seven and Eight total fifteen, and Nine and Six also match this. Combining Seven, Eight, Nine, and Six results in thirty, which corresponds to the number of thirty days in a single month. These are all established as symbolic metaphors. 

Lord Wei <note>Referring to Wei Boyang, the legendary author of the *Cantong qi* (The Kinship of the Three).</note> feared that students would fail to understand this explanation and lead each other astray, like the blind leading the blind. He was concerned they might mistakenly take the waxing and waning of the actual thirty days of a month as the literal "Fire Phasing" <term>Huohou: The precise timing and intensity of the internal alchemical heat or breath used to refine the elixir.</term> for a month. Therefore, he separately arranged these Four Images of Seven, Eight, Nine, and Six to enlighten those who do not yet understand. This clarifies that the number of thirty days in a month is entirely metaphorical; it does not literally mean one "advances the fire" for thirty days or begins the "retreating tally" <note>The phase of cooling or withdrawing the alchemical fire.</note> specifically on the sixteenth day. 

It is the same with terms like the earthly branches <note>Refers to the twelve characters used to denote hours and directions, such as Zi (North/Midnight) and Wu (South/Noon).</note>, the four seasons, the solstices and equinoxes, the "opening and closing," day and night, dawn and dusk, or "returning and dwelling." All carry this same symbolic meaning. If a student understands that Seven, Eight, Nine, and Six constitute the "thirty-day month," then all other broad references and winding metaphors can be understood intuitively. Why should one cling to the literal text or get bogged down by the symbols?

During the creation of the Elixir, the only fear is that the "Mind-Monkey" <note>A famous metaphor for the restless, jumping nature of the untrained human mind.</note> will escape to the outside. ## When at Rest, Observe the Images and Model Their Forms

The method of creating the Elixir requires that externally, one sets up markers and water clocks to measure the timing of the celestial movements. Internally, one must cultivate the "True Oneness" to verify the "internal water clock" of one's own body. In this way, one does not lose the critical timing of Heaven and Earth. However, if the spirit is settled and the breath is harmonious, then the internal and external will match perfectly. If the spirit is dimmed or scattered, the timing will be mismatched and erroneous. One must remain settled.

## Set the Standard to Serve as a Guide; Divine the Signs to Determine Fortune

The "Fire Phasing" <term>Huohou: The timing and intensity of internal heat/breath.</term> of the Great Elixir does not rely on literal hours. Why, then, must one set up markers to divine the signs? One does so for fear of missing the moment when Heaven and Man "act in unison." If one does not understand the "Mysterious Pivot" <note>The subtle turning point or mechanism of the universe/body.</note> and simply spends the day from dawn to dusk obsessed with literal sundials and water clocks as their "Fire Phasing," they are deeply mistaken.

## Issue Commands Following the Seasons; Do Not Miss the Time of Subtle Movement

"The Earthly Thunder shakes and the Gate of Wind <note>The trigram *Xun*, associated with wind and the southeast.</note> opens; the Dragon leaps from the Eastern Pool." This describes the moment within the body when the **First Yang Line** <note>The first stirrings of active, creative energy after a period of stillness.</note> moves. At this time, a warm vapor flows and blends, and the heart feels a sense of "trance-like blurring." This is exactly the moment to "advance the fire"—it must not be delayed.

> The *Collection of Pearls and Jade* in the "Returning to the Source" chapter says: "When the winds of the myriad flutes first rise, and the moon over the thousand mountains is perfectly round—hurry to issue the command, and you may then circulate the Heavens."

This is what that means.

> The *Understanding Mystery* <note>original: 指玄篇 (Zhixuan pian), an influential text on internal alchemy.</note> says: "Nurture the **Infant** <note>A metaphor for the newly formed spiritual embryo or elixir.</note> within the light of the stone; employ the **General** within the drumming forest."

This is what that means.

This says that the Way of the Great Elixir is in alignment with the Earth...

The Way does not act in a vacuum—it resides only in the person."

How profound and purposeful this is!

### In Movement, Follow the Hexagram Transformations; In Stillness, Follow the Commentary

The *Classic of the Way and Virtue* <note>The Tao Te Ching.</note> says: "Attain the ultimate emptiness; maintain the utmost stillness. As the myriad things arise together, I observe their return. Things flourish, and each returns to its root. Returning to the root is called stillness; stillness is called **Returning to Life**." How magnificent! This is how the myriad things return to their life-source.

The **Great Medicine of the Golden Elixir** <term>Jindan: Another name for the Elixir, emphasizing its precious, incorruptible nature.</term> is conceived within ultimate stillness and is produced at the moment of **Extreme Yin** <note>The point of maximum darkness or stillness, just before light/movement returns.</note>. The *Commentary on the Changes* says: "How great is the Primal Earth! The myriad things owe their birth to it; it submissively receives the influence of Heaven. The Earth is thick and sustains all things; its virtue matches the boundless." The Earth (the *Kun* hexagram) represents pure Yin. Just as the Earth receives the energy of Heaven so that all things can be produced from the soil, the method of the Elixir involves "containing the light and reflecting inward," hiding the spirit within. This is no different from the "Pure Yin Moon" or the season of winter when everything is closed and stored away. The *Chapters on Returning to Life* <note>original: 復命篇 (Fuming pian), a classic text of internal alchemy.</note> says: "If you obtain the formula of the True Immortals, you will refine the **True Yang** within the Yin." This is exactly what that refers to.

However, stillness at its peak must be followed by movement. Suddenly, a **Single Yang Line** <note>The first spark of creative energy.</note> moves beneath the six Yin lines. One transformation creates the hexagram **Return**; a second creates **Approach**; a third creates **Peace**; a fourth creates **Great Power**; a fifth creates **Breakthrough**; and finally, the sixth transformation creates **Pure Heaven** <note>This describes the "Sovereign Hexagrams" used to track the growth of energy (Yang) from midwinter to midsummer.</note>. At this point, the **Yang Energy** pervades the entire void, and the "Solar Disc" emerges from the deep pool. When the forces of Heaven and Earth are put into operation, the world is brought into order.

## Tightly Bundling the Subtle and Secret; Unfolding and Distributing the Treasure

"Tightly bundling the subtle and secret" means the eyes contain their light, the ears focus on their inner resonance, the nose regulates the breath, and the tongue seals the energy (*Qi*). Sit cross-legged and upright, hiding the spirit and maintaining internal guard; one must not allow even a hair's breadth of the mind to be used externally. 

Indeed, if the eyes do not look out, the **Cloud-Soul** <term>Hun: The ethereal, "heavenly" aspect of the soul associated with the Liver.</term> naturally returns to the Liver and does not leak out through the eyes. The **Will** <term>Yi: The focused intent associated with the Spleen.</term> naturally returns to the Spleen and does not leak through the mouth. The **Essence** <term>Jing: Vital reproductive and physical energy associated with the Kidneys.</term> naturally returns to the Kidneys and does not leak through the ears. The **Spirit** <term>Shen: The conscious awareness associated with the Heart.</term> naturally returns to the Heart and does not... <unclear>leak</unclear> ...When the five are all unmoved, the Will returns to the Spleen. However, when there is no leaking from the eyes, the **White-Soul** <term>Po: The corporeal, "earthly" aspect of the soul associated with the Lungs.</term> resides in the Lungs and does not leak through the nose. When the Spirit is in the Heart, it does not leak through the mouth; when the Essence is in the Kidneys, it does not leak through the ears; when the Will is in the Spleen, it does not leak. 

When these five are all without "leaks," then the Spirit, Essence, Cloud-Soul, White-Soul, and Will all fuse and blend together. They transform into a **Single Breath** <note>original: 一氣 (Yi Qi), the unified primal energy.</note> and gather in the **Cinnabar Field** <term>Dantian: The energetic center of the body, located below the navel.</term>. When a single breath eventually shifts at the nose, the mind is suddenly enlightened; then the "Dragon and Tiger" <note>Metaphors for the volatile (Breath) and stable (Essence) energies.</note> rush through, the Great Road is opened, the channels flow, and the "Great Ring" of circulation is awarded.

## The Essential Way of the Dipper: Governing the Transformation and Holding the Bonds

The secret of the **Way of the Elixir** <term>Dandao: The path of internal alchemy.</term> lies entirely in the "Dipper" <note>The Big Dipper, specifically its handle, which was seen as the "steering wheel" of the heavens.</note>. It is that which rotates the Yin and Yang of the entire body and governs the myriad things within oneself. It is like the main rope of a net or the buttons of a garment. 

The human body has **Three Fields** <note>The lower, middle, and upper Dantians.</note> divided into three locations. If one obtains the mechanism of the "Dipper Handle" to rotate them, then the **True Energy** will circulate up and down like the flowing of the Milky Way. This is what is called the "Essential Way." As the *Chapters on Returning to Life* <note>original: 復命篇 (Fuming pian).</note> says: 

> "Drive back the Northern Dipper, turn the Heavenly Web; hold the Southern Stars in your hand and enter the inner chamber." 

This is the most essential of the essentials.

## The Alignment of the Five Planets and the Lunar Mansions

The **Five Planets** <note>original: 五緯 (Wuwei), the "five latitudes" or the five visible planets corresponding to the Five Elements.</note> move in harmony or opposition, responding to the movements of time. The **Twenty-eight Mansions** <note>original: 四七 (Si-qi, "four sevens"), referring to the four clusters of seven lunar mansions that map the sky.</note> shift their positions, rising and falling in the heavens.

The **Five Elements** must be gathered together, and **Metal and Fire** must share the same furnace. This process depends entirely on a person’s moment of focused thought, allowing them to **return to the root and the origin**. If this is not achieved, the "constellations" within the **cauldron** <term>Ding: The internal energetic space where alchemy occurs.</term> will all fall out of alignment, and Heaven and Earth will remain suspended far apart.

## The Star of Literature and the Internal Bureaucracy

The *Records of the Grand Historian* <note>original: 史記 (Shiji), specifically the "Book of Celestial Offices."</note> states: "The bowl of the Dipper, which carries the six stars of the basket, is called the **Palace of Literature** <note>original: 文昌宮 (Wenchang Gong), associated with the star deity of culture and administration.</note>." 

When we speak of the "Star of Literature governing the records," it refers to the **Sovereign of the Crimson Palace** <term>Jianggong: A name for the Heart center in alchemy.</term> governing the **Creative and Receptive** <note>Qian and Kun, the polarities of the body.</note> forces. How could there be a physical "Star of Literature" inside the human body? These are nothing more than metaphors. 

Just as Heaven has the **Three Terraces and Four Assistants** <note>Specific star groups in Chinese astronomy.</note>, the Elixir has its **Three Dragons and Four Tigers**. The warning regarding the "Three Terraces and Assistants" is to ensure that the movements of the **Stems** <note>original: 甲乙庚辛 (Jia, Yi, Geng, Xin), used here to represent the balance of Wood/East and Metal/West.</note> do not fall into error. Heaven has the various stars and their earthly correspondences; the Elixir has the various **Hexagrams and Fire-Phases** <note>original: 卦火符 (Gua huofu), the timing system for internal refinement.</note>. All the "officials and departments" of the sky govern their respective areas; similarly, the internal furnace and its "fire-timing" must be weighed and pushed forward according to the **Twenty-four Solar Terms** and the **Twenty-eight Mansions**. 

From this, we can say that all the myriad phenomena of the Heavens are contained entirely within our own bodies.

## The Cycle of the Sun and Moon

The **Sun** contains the essence of the Five Elements; the **Moon** is governed by the Six Pitch-pipes. <note>original: 六律 (Liulü), the ancient standard for musical and calendrical tuning.</note> Five times six makes thirty degrees; when the degrees are complete, the cycle begins anew.

The Sun possesses the **Ten Stems**; five are "hard" and five are "soft." The Moon possesses the **Twelve Pipes**; six are Yin and six are Yang. In the language of the **Way of the Elixir** <term>Dandao: The path of internal alchemy.</term>, the Sun is the "Fire." That the "Sun contains the essence of the Five Elements" means that a single substance contains the five colors. The Moon is the "Medicine." That the "Moon is governed by the Six Pitch-pipes" refers to the **Six Hexagrams of Jing** <note>original: 京六卦 (Jing liu gua), a specific system of hexagram changes attributed to the scholar Jing Fang.</note>. 

The "thirty degrees" after which the cycle restarts refers to how the Sun travels one degree each day. When it reaches thirty degrees, it joins again with the Moon. This cycle of starting and ending never pauses for a moment.

The "thread of existence and loss" refers to the transition between the Dark Moon and the New Moon—the moment when the Yin is about to end but has not yet finished, and the Yang is about to be born but has not yet emerged. # The Original Source Hides the Light to Internally Illuminate the Physical Body

The *Collected Works of Quanzhen* <note>original: 全真集 (Quanzhen ji), the writings of the Complete Reality school of Daoism.</note> says: "To achieve penetration, one must seek the essential mystery. To see clearly, one must turn the gaze inward. Returning to the root and back to the source through 'internal illumination' <term>Neizhao: A meditative practice of visualizing the internal organs and the flow of energy to foster health and spiritual clarity.</term> is the primary method of cultivation." Even the scholars of old <note>Referring to Confucians.</note> said that the Daoist method of longevity involves "withdrawing the vision and looking back within," just as the radiance of metal and water is hidden deep inside. Truly, these are profound words.

## Close the Openings and Solidify the Spirit Root

"Dui" <note>The trigram ☱ from the I-Ching, symbolizing the mouth.</note> refers to the mouth. The "Spirit Root" refers to the **Kan Palace** <note>The "Water" center of the body, associated with the kidneys and the lower abdomen.</note>. By closing the mouth, one prevents energy from leaking out from above; by solidifying the Spirit Root, one ensures there is no leakage from below. 

The *Canon of Supreme Mystery* by Yang Xiong <note>original: 太玄經 (Taixuanjing), a text from the Han Dynasty (53 BCE – 18 CE).</note> says: "Hide the heart in the abyss and nourish the Spirit Root." If the Spirit does not race outward toward distractions, the "Harmonious Energy" <term>Heqi: The balanced, refined state of one's internal breath.</term> will fill the body, and beauty will be found within.

## The Three Lights Sink into the Six, Warmly Nourishing the Seed Pearl

The **Three Lights** <note>Sun, Moon, and Stars, representing the eyes and the internal spirit.</note> are the spiritual manifestations within the "Cavern Chamber" <note>An area inside the head.</note>. If a person can gather these three lights and turn them to shine inward, then at the central, correct position, the **Mysterious Pearl** <note>A symbolic term for the initial formation of the internal elixir.</note> will be produced. 

The *Yellow Court Scripture* says: "The spiritual manifestations of the Cavern Chamber resemble the Big Dipper, the Sun, and the Moon; the Three Lights shine brilliantly as they enter the 'Child's Room' <note>Another name for the internal space where the elixir is refined.</note>." I ask all insightful practitioners to reflect deeply on this.

## One Looks but Does Not See It; It Is Near and Easy to Seek

The **Great Medicine of the Golden Elixir** <note>The goal of internal alchemy: a state of perfected, immortal health and spirit.</note> is right before one's eyes. Is that not near? Yet, because people look but do not "see" it and reach for it but cannot "grasp" it, it seems far away even though it is close. 

If one obtains the proper method to seek it, it takes no more than a moment’s work before the "Yellow Flowers" <note>A metaphor for the flourishing of internal energy.</note> fill one’s vision. What distance could there possibly be? 

The *Chapters on Understanding Reality* <note>original: 悟真篇 (Wuzhen pian), a seminal 11th-century text on internal alchemy.</note> says: "The work is easy and the medicine is not far; once the secret is told, people cannot help but laugh." They laugh because it is so close and easy to find, yet people insist on searching for it in high and distant places. 

The *Chapters on Returning to Destiny* says: "It is clearly right before your eyes, yet the people of this age do not see the Heavens." Because they do not see it, they abandon the internal and pursue the external. Some try to ingest the essence of the sun and moon, some try to refine minerals and herbs <note>External alchemy, which often involved dangerous chemical concoctions.</note>, and others practice "bedroom arts" <note>Sexual longevity practices.</note>. This is exactly what is meant by "the Way is near, yet people seek it in the distance; the task is easy, yet people seek it in the difficult." How tragic!

The "Yellow Center" gradually permeates the inner principles; its nourishment reaches the skin. 

When there is "something" in the **Dantian** <term>Dantian: Literally "Cinnabar Field," refers to the energy centers in the body, most commonly the lower abdomen where vital energy is cultivated.</term> and the **One Qi** <term>Yiqi: The primordial, unified energy that precedes the division into Yin and Yang; the "Breath of Life."</term> flows through, then harmony and smoothness accumulate within, and its blossoming radiance is expressed outwardly. 

If the beginning is correct, the end will be perfected; if the trunk is established, the branches can be supported. 

If the post is upright, the shadow is straight; if the source is deep, the flow is long. Once the "One" is obtained, then all ten thousand matters are completed. 

The "One" is hidden and obscured; the people of the world do not know it. 

The ancestor of the Great Dao is formed from nothing other than the **One Qi**. Its transformations are analyzed as black and white, and divided into green and yellow. It is metaphorically called the Sun and Moon, and named the Dragon and Tiger. Despite such a wide variety of terms, these are all just the two words "Yin and Yang." In reality, it is just a single thing. Furthermore, names like the "Divine Water and Flowery Pool" and titles like the "Lead Furnace and Earthen Cauldron" all refer to the same single place. 

Some speak of the **Winter Solstice** or the **Zi Hour** <note>11 PM to 1 AM, the time of the first movement of Yang energy in the daily cycle.</note>; some speak of the period between the last and first day of the lunar month <note>original: 晦朔 (huishuo).</note>. People do not understand; they think that the "Return of the One Yang" must occur at the specific calendar time of the Winter Solstice, or that the "Alignment of Sun and Moon" must occur only at the transition of the lunar month. Thus, they consult calendars and calculate the hours—this is a great error. 

Who knows how to condense the year, the month, the day, and the hour? Within a single moment, there is naturally the creative transformation of an entire year or month. Indeed, a single "time" is a single "place," and a single "place" is a single "thing." 

Therefore, the solstices and equinoxes, the directional stems and branches, the phases of the moon, the twelve double-hours, the twenty-four solar terms, the seventy-two pentads, the yearly conjunctions, the monthly cycles, the times of **Li and Kan** <note>The trigrams for Fire and Water, representing the heart and kidneys/lower abdomen.</note>, the months of the Rabbit and Rooster, the apertures of **Xun and Qian** <note>Trigrams representing Wind and Heaven.</note>, the gates of "two-and-eight" <note>An alchemical reference to the balance of Yin and Yang, often associated with the second and eighth months or specific energy ratios.</note>, the morning hexagram **Tun** and evening hexagram **Meng**, the daytime hexagram **Gou** and nighttime hexagram **Fu**—all of these are entirely contained within this "One." 

The *Chapters of Emerald Emptiness* <note>original: 翠虛篇 (Cuixu pian), a classic work by the alchemist Chen Nan.</note> says: "Later on, as before, go and consult others; how many 'Wild Fox Spirits' <note>A Buddhist and Daoist term for false teachers or practitioners who have been deluded into believing they have reached enlightenment.</note> have been seen through? Every one of them is ignorant of the 'True Single Place'; they all follow side-doors <note>Secondary or heterodox practices that do not lead to the ultimate goal.</note> rather than the Truth." How many people in this world truly know this "One"?

## Superior Virtue is Non-Action; It Is Not Sought Through Investigation. Inferior Virtue Acts; Its Application Never Ceases.

The *Dao De Jing* says: "Superior Virtue is non-action and has no purpose in acting; Inferior Virtue acts and has a purpose in acting." Today, when we say "Superior Virtue is non-action and is not sought through investigation," it means the Spirit is guarded within the **Mysterious Palace** <note>The upper Dantian or the spiritual center within the head.</note> and...

It warns against getting distracted by literal calendars or "side-door" practices, emphasizing that true "Superior Virtue" is found in effortless internal focus.</summary>

...is profound silence and non-action. "Inferior Virtue acts and its application never ceases" means that the Qi <note>The vital life force or breath.</note> rises from the **Mysterious Gate** <term>Pinfu: Literally "Maternal Aperture," referring to the lower energy center or the source from which the vital breath emerges.</term> and flows continuously without interruption. This borrows the words of Laozi <note>The legendary author of the Dao De Jing.</note> to reveal the secrets of the two apertures of **Kan and Li** <note>The trigrams for Water and Fire, representing the internal alchemical "cauldron" and "fire" within the body.</note>.

When the upper is closed, it is called "Having"; when the lower is closed, it is called "Nothingness." This "Nothingness" is used to serve the upper. Above, there is the Divine Virtue dwelling in the law of these two apertures. "Having" and "Nothingness" also depend on each other.

To say that the "upper opening" is called "Having" means that the **Palace of Fire** <note>The heart center (Li trigram).</note> possesses an image that conceals its "water." To say that the "lower closing" is called "Nothingness" means that the **Gate of Water** <note>The kidney or lower abdomen center (Kan trigram).</note> is formless and hides the "Red Dragon" <note>An alchemical metaphor for the internal energy or the "true lead" within the water.</note>. This "Nothingness" serves the upper. As for "Divine Virtue dwelling" there, when the **Original Spirit** <note>Yuanshen: The innate, pure consciousness.</note> rests in its original palace, the Qi follows it and rises upward. Therefore, the secret lies in firmly locking the "Eight Gates."

->*The Chapters on Awakening to the Truth* <note>original: 悟眞篇 (Wuzhen pian), a seminal 11th-century text on internal alchemy by Zhang Boduan.</note> says:<-

->The Youngest Daughter first opens the flowers of the Northern land.<-

The "Yellow House" is the palace where the Original Spirit resides in the **Upper Cinnabar Field** <note>The energy center located in the head, between the eyebrows.</note>. Regarding the law of these two apertures where "Having" and "Nothingness" depend on each other: if the lower is not closed, the "fire" will not gather; if the upper is not closed, the "medicine" <note>The refined internal energy or elixir.</note> will not rise.

->*The Chapters on Awakening to the Truth* says:<-
->Send it back to the **Earthen Cauldron** and seal it firmly,<-
->Next, bring in the **Flowing Pearl** to match and pair them.<-

Therefore, they must depend on each other for the process to be possible. What are the "Flowing Pearl" and "Earthen Cauldron"? They are simply different names for the two apertures of Fire and Water (Kan and Li).

## Know the White and Keep to the Black, and the Divine Radiance Comes of Itself. "White" is the Essence of Gold; "Black" is the Foundation of Water.

"White" represents Gold (Metal); "Black" represents Water. The methods of alchemy use Water as the foundation, and the **Essence of Gold** <note>Jinjing: A metaphor for the most refined and potent stage of internal energy.</note> is born within the Water. Therefore, one who "knows the White" simply "guards the Black." By guarding the Black, the White naturally appears. How does one guard it? It is like a cat guarding a hole, waiting for a mouse to arrive: the body does not move, the eyes do not blink, and the mind is focused entirely on the mouse with no other thoughts.

"Divine Radiance" refers to the **Mechanism of Heaven** <note>Tianji: The subtle, hidden workings of the natural and divine order.</note>. If you wish to "steal" this mechanism, you must first empty your heart. When the heart is empty, the Spirit congeals. When the Spirit congeals, the breath stabilizes. When the breath stabilizes, the two sides rise together in equal measure, and the Divine Radiance arrives of its own accord.

->The "Far-off Journey" chapter of the *Songs of Chu* <note>original: 離騷遠遊篇 (Lisao Yuanyou pian), an ancient Chinese poetic work.</note> says:<-
->Do not disturb your soul, and it will naturally settle.<-
->The **One Qi** is profoundly divine; preserve it in the middle of the night.<-
->Wait for it in emptiness; let non-action come first.<-

This shares the same meaning. The commentator Master Zhu Xi <note>A famous Song Dynasty scholar who also studied Daoist texts.</note> noted that the instructions given by **Guangchengzi** to the **Yellow Emperor** <note>A legendary encounter where the immortal Guangchengzi teaches the sovereign the secrets of longevity and the Dao.</note> were nothing more than this; it is truly the essential secret of the immortals.

## Water is the Pivot of the Dao; Its Number is One.

Water is the beginning of Yin and Yang. The "Mystery" contains the **Yellow Sprout** <note>Huangya: The first sign of the Elixir or the "True Lead" emerging during meditation.</note>. It is the lord of the Five Metals and the **River Chariot** <term>Heche: An alchemical term for the mechanism or energy flow that transports the internal "medicine" through the body's channels.</term> of the North. Thus, Lead is black on the outside but holds the **Golden Flower** <note>Jinhua: The manifestation of refined spiritual light.</note> within. This is like "wearing coarse cloth while clutching jade"; the exterior is...

<meta>This page continues the technical discourse on the elemental relationships in internal alchemy, specifically focusing on Water as the primary element of the Dao. <margin>The Madman <note>original: 狂夫 (Kuangfu); a sobriquet often used by Daoist commentators to signal a humble or unconventional perspective.</note></margin>

Water is the pivot of the Dao and the beginning of Yin and Yang. Why is this so? "Heaven generates One, which is Water," placing it at the head of the **Five Elements** <note>Wuxing: The five phases of Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, and Water.</note>. The number of Water is One; by adding the number of Earth, which is Five, we arrive at the "completed number" of Water <note>In traditional Chinese numerology, 1 is the "generating" number for Water; adding the central number 5 results in 6, its "completion" number.</note>. Does its "Mystery" not contain the image of the **Yellow Sprout**? <term>Huangya: The "Yellow Sprout" is a symbolic term for the first sign of the emerging internal elixir during meditation.</term> To say the "Mystery contains the Yellow Sprout" means that "Lead" is produced within the Water. Lead is the master of the **Five Metals** and resides within the dark mystery of the North. When it meets Earth, it produces the Yellow Sprout. The Yellow Sprout is the **Golden Flower** <note>Jinhua: A manifestation of refined spiritual light.</note>. The Golden Flower is the refined essence of Lead. Therefore, the body of Lead is black on the outside, but the Golden Flower is hidden within it. This is like a most precious treasure hidden in the robes of a common man.

The **River Chariot** <term>Heche: An alchemical term for the internal energy flow that transports the refined "medicine" through the body's channels.</term> of the North is the Emperor’s Chariot. Because it follows the rotation of the Heavenly River <note>The Milky Way.</note>, it is called the River Chariot. Now, the **True Lead** is born in the Water; when it is refined by **True Fire**, the River Chariot dare not linger or stop for a moment, but carries the essence up to the **Peak of Kunlun** <note>In internal alchemy, the head is referred to as the Kunlun Mountain, the highest point of the body's energetic landscape.</note>.

### Metal is the Mother of Water; the Mother is Hidden in the Child's Embryo. Water is the Child of Metal; the Child is Hidden in the Mother's Womb.

Metal generates Water; therefore, it is said that Metal is the Mother of Water. Water is the child born of Metal. Since there is Metal within the Water, we say the "Mother is hidden in the Child’s embryo," and the "Child is stored in the Mother’s womb." If the practitioner understands the meaning of "Gold within the Water," they will know the source and origin of the **Medicine** <note>The refined internal energy or elixir.</note>.

### The True Person is Supremely Subtle; Seeming to Exist, Yet Seeming to Not. Like a Great Abyss, Now Sinking, Now Floating.

The "True Person" is the **Original Spirit** <note>Yuanshen: The innate, pure consciousness that exists before thought.</note>. To "seem to exist yet not" means it is continuous and subtle, as if barely there, yet its use is never strained or forced. "Like a great abyss, now sinking, now floating" describes how the True Person moves back and forth within the Great Abyss, faint and indistinct, floating and sinking without a fixed position. *The Great Collection of the Golden Elixir* <note>original: 金丹大成集 (Jindan dacheng ji), a text by Xiao Zixu.</note> says: "On the Kunlun Mountain is the Path of the Yellow Flower; it frequently leads the Original Spirit away and back again." The "Great Abyss" mentioned here is simply another name for the Kunlun peak within the body.

### Advancing and Retreating, Distributed and Spread; Each Keeps to the Boundaries of Its Territory.

In the Alchemical Law, one "advances" from the **Zi** hour <note>11 PM – 1 AM; the time when the first spark of Yang energy returns.</note> and "retreats" from the **Wu** hour <note>11 AM – 1 PM; the time when Yang reaches its peak and begins to decline.</note>. Advancing and retreating are distributed such that each maintains its own boundary and they do not interfere with each other. The *Chant on the Purity of the Golden Elixir* <note>original: 金丹純粹吟 (Jindan chuncui yin), a work by Yang Xubai.</note> says: "Before the furnace of Zi and Wu, distinguish advancing and retreating; within the cauldron of **Qian and Kun** <note>The trigrams for Heaven and Earth, representing the head and abdomen/cauldron.</note>, identify floating and sinking." This is exactly the meaning.

# On the Categories of Gathering: Creating Mercury through the White.

"White" refers to **White Gold** <note>original: 白金 (Baijin); in this context, a symbolic name for "True Lead" or the refined essence of the breath.</note>. "Vermilion" refers to **Vermilion Mercury** <note>original: 朱汞 (Zhugong); a symbol for the refined spirit or mind.</note>. Regarding the phrase "Categories of Gathering," the "White" refers to gathering the White Gold from the **Kan Palace** <note>The "Palace of Water" in the North, associated with the kidneys and the initial spark of life-energy.</note> in the North to serve as the Mother of the Elixir. White Gold and Vermilion Mercury are of the same kind and naturally follow one another. The phrase "Creating Mercury" refers to the daily practice of "circulating the fire," which involves extracting the "Lead-breath" and gradually adding "Mercury" in its place.

Chen Momo <note>original: 陳默默 (Chen Momo), likely referring to the Southern Lineage master Chen Nan.</note> said: "The main text states: Internally guard the **River Chariot** <term>Heche: The energetic path along the spine.</term> and dwell in the Northern Gate. Since 'Heaven produced One as Water,' Water comes first. To harmonize the seals, one must obtain the **Fire of the Heavenly Circuit** <note>Zhou tian huo: A method of timed breathing and focused attention that follows the cycles of the sun and moon.</note>. The meaning is like a boat crossing to the shore. When the work of transporting energy is successful day and night, the rotation becomes most subtle, and the body becomes like amber." A superior practitioner of the Elixir who understands this method will recognize the **True Lead** and realize they have no need for physical lead. Most scholars only know how to "couple" Lead and Mercury as a medicine, but they do not understand the "fire-work" of **Extracting Lead and Adding Mercury** <note>Chou qian tian gong: A core alchemical metaphor for replacing the dense, "heavy" aspects of vitality with refined, "light" spiritual essence.</note>. Without this, even if they form the "seed" of the elixir, they cannot prevent it from dissipating.

# Refining as the External Guard; Dwelling Purely within the White.

"Refining as the External Guard" refers to the **True Fire** being applied and circulated in the "External Furnace." "Dwelling Purely within the White" refers to the **Golden Elixir** resting securely within the "Internal Furnace" <note>In internal alchemy, the "furnace" and "cauldron" are energetic centers in the body used to "cook" or transform energy.</note>. When the internal furnace contains the elixir, it requires the heat of the external fire to be nourished and refined day and night. Only then can the elixir reach maturity.

Shao Guangnan <note>original: 邵廣南 (Shao Guangnan), the philosopher Shao Yong.</note> says in the *Collection of Great Antiquity*: "Around the neck, the **Dragon Pearl** <note>A symbol of the refined spiritual essence.</note> shines of its own accord; within the belly, the secret treasure glows brilliantly." Does this not mean the fire is circulated on the outside while the elixir is stored on the inside?

# A square-circle one inch in diameter, blended and supporting each other. Born before Heaven and Earth, lofty and supremely high. Beside it are walls and gates, shaped like a Penglai Gourd. Encircled and closed off, open in four directions but guarded. The lake-gates are closed to exclude evil influences; winding galleries are connected to guard against the unforeseen.

"A square-circle one inch in diameter" refers to the **Niwan Palace** <term>Niwan gong: Literally the "Muddy Pellet Palace," located in the center of the brain; the upper Dantian where the spirit resides.</term>. People today only call the Heart the "square inch," but they do not realize that within the human body there are **Three Elixir Fields** <note>Dantian: Three primary energetic centers located in the head, chest, and lower abdomen.</note>. Each center contains a void of one inch where the breath and pulses all connect. "Blended and supporting each other" refers to the head having **Nine Palaces**, with the Niwan Palace dwelling in the center.

The *Yellow Court Scripture* <note>original: 黃庭經 (Huangting jing), a foundational Daoist text on internal visualization.</note> says: "The Nine True Spirits of the Niwan each have a room; a square-circle of one inch is situated therein." This is the meaning. "Born before Heaven and Earth" means that the single orifice of the Niwan is the ancestor of the ten thousand pores of the body. If this orifice opens, all ten thousand pores open together. "Lofty and supremely high" signifies that the Niwan Palace is located at the very peak of the **Kunlun Mountain** <note>A metaphor for the top of the head.</note>.

This is the seat where the **Original Spirit** <term>Yuanshen: The innate, untainted consciousness or "true self" in Daoist thought, distinct from the ego or "thinking mind."</term> resides. Above, it corresponds to the **Mysterious Capital** <note>Xuandu: In Daoist cosmology, the celestial capital where the highest deities dwell; here, it signifies that the head is the "heaven" of the body.</note>; it is the village where the ten thousand spirits assemble. 

Regarding the "seven walls and gates" beside it, these are the orifices that surround it on the outside. The "Grotto Chamber" and the "Yellow Court" <note>Inner chambers of the brain described in Daoist visualization.</note> are both situated in front of it. As for the phrase "shaped like a Penglai Gourd," it is like the three divine mountains upon the sea, of which **Penglai** <note>A mythical island of the immortals.</note> sits at the peak. 

"Encircled and closed off" refers to the practice of withdrawing one's vision and reversing one's hearing <note>A common meditative instruction to pull the senses inward away from the external world.</note>, cautiously sealing the senses. "Open in four directions but guarded" means that the **Original Harmony** <note>Yuanhe: The primal, balanced state of life-energy.</note> circulates within, a single breath flowing through, while the **Vermilion Bird** <note>Zhunque: A symbol for the heart-fire or the spirit; here it suggests the spirit soaring at the "Jade Terrace" of the head without a fixed destination, yet remaining within.</note> frolics at the Jade Terrace without a set schedule. 

"Guarded and fortified" is like a dragon nourishing its pearl; the mind never forgets it. It is like a hen brooding over its eggs; the breath is never interrupted. "Excluding evil influences" means that even if demonic realms <note>Distractions, hallucinations, or mental obstacles during meditation.</note> approach, one naturally wields the "ax of focus" to cut them away. "Winding galleries connected to guard against the unforeseen" suggests that if the spirit should attempt to exit, it is immediately drawn back in, with the **Twin Boys** <note>A symbolic reference to the eyes or guardian spirits of the internal gates.</note> perpetually guarding the grotto entrance.

->**One can be without thought, but it is difficult to endure worry and labor.**<-

Tan Changzhen <note>original: 譚長真 (Tan Changzhen); referring to Tan Chuduan, one of the "Seven Realized Ones" of the Quanzhen school.</note> says in his *Water and Cloud Collection*: "Do not let even a thread of thought hang upon the Spirit Terrace <note>The heart/mind.</note>; if the spirit-embryo is formed within, you will achieve immortality." Generally, if the mind is in a state of **non-doing** <note>Wuwei: Effortless action or being without ego-driven intent.</note>, the breath will be harmonious. When the breath is harmonious, the "Ultimate Treasure" (the elixir) will form. If the mind is "doing" (full of intent and anxiety), the breath becomes chaotic. When the breath is chaotic, the "Radiant Essence" scatters. Therefore, one can thrive without thought, but cannot endure the exhaustion of worry.

->**Spirit and breath fill the room; none can remain. Those who guard it prosper; those who lose it perish. In movement, stillness, rest, and toil, it is always with the person.**<-

When true accumulation of effort has lasted long enough, the **Great Harmony** <note>Taihe: A state of total energetic balance.</note> overflows. Whether in movement, stillness, rest, or toil, one must always guard this state with diligence. If you guard it, you will prosper; if you lose it, you will perish. You must not be separated from it for even a moment.

This is not the method of "Traversing the Organs," where one uses internal vision to contemplate thoughts. Nor is it "Treading the Dipper or Pacing the Stars," or observing the "Six Jia" <note>Complex Daoist ritual movements and calendrical calculations used in "external" or liturgical Daoism.</note> and the movements of the sun and stars. Nor is it the "Yin Path of Suppressing the Nine," which only confuses the **Original Womb**. It is not "eating breath" <note>Biqi: A practice of swallowing air to replace food.</note> until the stomach and intestines growl, nor is it "expelling the upright and inhaling external evils." 

Some do not sleep day or night, or they fast during the dark of the moon, never resting. Their bodies become daily more fatigued, and they appear dazed as if foolish. Their hundred pulses boil like a cauldron, and they can never achieve clarity or stillness. They build mounds of earth, erect altars and shrines, and offer respectful sacrifices morning and night. They claim to see the forms of ghosts and spirits and are moved by what they encounter in dreams. Their hearts are filled with joy, and they tell themselves they will surely extend their lifespan—but then they suddenly die according to their heavenly fate, and their physical forms rot and are exposed. Their actions are full of errors, and they rebel against the "Pivot of the Universe." 

There are many such techniques—over ten thousand different paths. They retreat from the teachings of **Huang-Lao** <note>Yellow-Old: The ancient tradition of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi, focusing on the Dao.</note> and take winding paths toward the "Capital of Nine Gengs" <note>A likely reference to lower-level or misguided spiritual destinations.</note>.

There are three thousand, six hundred methods and dozens of schools for "Nourishing Life." They burn and fade away, too many to list. Some involve closing the eyes to "internally view" the five organs for the purpose of contemplation, or treading the stars and pacing the Dipper according to the day and hour...

It sharply critiques superficial practices like organ visualization, star-stepping, and extreme asceticism, labeling them as "false paths" that lead to exhaustion rather than immortality.</summary>
